examples.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.
examples.english: Hello, nice to meet you.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ shì tā de péngyou.
examples.english: Hello, I'm his friend.

words.tip: Two third tones in a row: the first one rises, so it sounds like ní hǎo. Between friends people often skip it entirely.

examples.english: Bye, see you tomorrow!
I'm off, bye!

words.tip: Literally 'again see'. 明天见 (see you tomorrow) reuses 见, a nice pattern to show.

characters.meaning: thank (讠 speech + 射 shè for the sound)
the same character, doubled and said with no tone

examples.english: Thanks for helping me.
Thank you, I really like it.

words.tip: The second 谢 is toneless. Teach the reply too: 不客气 (bú kèqi, you're welcome).

examples.english: Please sit down.
Please say it one more time.

words.tip: Goes at the start of a request: 请坐, 请进 (please come in). Also 'to treat': 我请你 = my treat.

examples.english: Sorry, I'm late.
Sorry, I don't understand.

words.tip: Roughly 'can't face you', a real apology. For a light 'excuse me' (getting attention, squeezing past), use 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi).

examples.english: I am German.
Let me help you.

words.tip: Same form for I and me. Add 的 for 'my' (我的). Pronouns never change form in Chinese, a relief after German.

examples.english: What's your name?
Are you busy today?

words.tip: The left side 亻 is the 'person' radical. Polite 'you' is 您 (nín), a bit like German Sie.

examples.english: He is my friend.
Which country is he from?

words.tip: Sounds exactly like 她 (she). Only the written radical differs: 亻 person.

examples.english: She is busy.
She's my mum.

words.tip: Same sound as 他 (he). The 女 radical means 'woman'. In speech you can't tell them apart either.

examples.english: We study together.
We're good friends.

words.tip: 们 makes any pronoun plural: 我们, 你们, 他们. 咱们 (zánmen) means 'we, including you', common in the north.

examples.english: This is my home.
Today is my birthday.

words.tip: Links nouns (我是德国人) but not adjectives: say 我很累, never 我是累. It never changes form.

examples.english: I have a younger sister.
There are a lot of people here.

words.tip: Always negated with 没, never 不: 没有. Also means 'there is': 这里有咖啡 (there's coffee here).

examples.english: What are you doing?
I'm cooking today.

words.tip: Do and make, like German machen. 做饭 = to cook. Watch out for 作, which has the same sound.

examples.english: Let's go to the supermarket.
Where do you want to go?

words.tip: No 'to' needed: 去 + place (去中国, 去超市). 吧 at the end turns it into 'let's'.

examples.english: Come over to my place.
My mum and dad are coming tomorrow.

words.tip: Movement towards the speaker, the opposite of 去.

characters.meaning: word ending, no meaning of its own (also in 怎么)

examples.english: What is this?
What do you like to eat?

words.tip: Question words sit where the answer would go: 这是什么? = 'this is what?'. No word-order change, unlike German and English.

examples.english: Who is he?
Whose phone is this?

words.tip: Two pronunciations: shéi (common in speech) and shuí. Both are correct.

examples.english: Where do you live?
Where are you now?

words.tip: Only the tone separates 哪里 (where) from 那里 (nàlǐ, there). Northern speakers say 哪儿 (nǎr). Also a modest reply to a compliment: 哪里哪里!

examples.english: When are you going home?
When are we eating?

words.tip: Literally 'what time'. It goes before the verb: 你什么时候来?

characters.meaning: word ending, no meaning of its own (also in 什么)

examples.english: How do you read this character?
What's wrong?

words.tip: Useful extras: 怎么了? = what's wrong? 怎么样? = how is it? / how about it?

examples.english: Right, I'm German.
You're right.

words.tip: Chinese has no all-purpose 'yes'. You repeat the verb (你去吗? 去!) or say 对 (that's right).

examples.english: I don't drink coffee.
I'm not busy today.

words.tip: Becomes bú before a 4th tone: 不是 (bú shì), 不要 (bú yào). Used for habits, preferences and the future.

examples.english: I don't have time.
I haven't eaten yet.

words.tip: Negates 有 and completed actions: 我没去 (I didn't go). The 不 vs 没 contrast is worth a few examples.

examples.english: Me too.
He likes drinking tea too.

words.tip: Always before the verb, never at the end of the sentence like English 'too'.

examples.english: It's cold today.
Your Chinese is very good.

words.tip: Often just links a subject and an adjective with little 'very' meaning: 我很好 = I'm good. Stress it to mean 'really'.

examples.english: Today is Monday.
What do you want to do today?

words.tip: Show the family: 今天 today, 明天 tomorrow, 昨天 (zuótiān) yesterday.

examples.english: See you tomorrow!
What day of the week is it tomorrow?

words.tip: 明 = sun 日 + moon 月, 'bright'. The same pattern gives 明年 = next year.

examples.english: What time is it now?
I'm not at home right now.

words.tip: Time words go near the start, before the verb: 我现在很忙.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài Běijīng zhù le sān tiān.
examples.english: We stayed in Beijing for three days.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jǐ tiān wǒ hěn máng.
examples.english: I've been busy these past few days.

words.tip: Also 'sky' and 'heaven'. Counts on its own with no measure word: 三天 = three days.

examples.english: Happy New Year!
Next year we're going to China.

words.tip: Counts on its own like 天: 两年. Chinese New Year (春节, Chūnjié) is a great thing to talk about together.

examples.english: Have you eaten?
I'd like to eat Chinese food.

words.tip: 你吃饭了吗? is a classic friendly greeting, not an invitation. The 口 (mouth) radical shows up in lots of mouth words.

examples.english: What would you like to drink?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang hē kāfēi.
examples.english: I drink coffee every morning.

words.tip: Another 口 radical. Common pairs: 喝水, 喝茶, 喝酒 (drink alcohol).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi shuǐ.
examples.english: Please give me a glass of water.
Do you want some water?

words.tip: Many Chinese people drink 热水 (hot water) by default, a good talking point next to German Kohlensäure.

examples.english: Let's go and eat.
The food is ready.

words.tip: Means both rice and 'a meal': 早饭 breakfast, 午饭 lunch, 晚饭 dinner. 米饭 is specifically rice.

examples.english: I like drinking green tea.
What kind of tea is this?

words.tip: German Tee and English 'tea' come from a southern Chinese pronunciation (tê), 'chai' from chá. Black tea is 红茶, 'red tea'.

examples.english: I'm at home.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén?
examples.english: How many people are there in your family?

words.tip: Means both home and family. The character is a roof 宀 over a pig 豕, a memorable picture.

examples.english: My room is small.
Is anyone in the room?

words.tip: 间 is also the measure word for rooms. 卧室 (wòshì) = bedroom.

examples.english: Please close the door.
I'll wait for you at the door.

words.tip: The character looks like a doorway. 开门 / 关门 = open / close the door, and also a shop opening or closing. 个 is fine in casual speech.

examples.english: We live together.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài zhèlǐ zhù le liǎng nián.
examples.english: I lived here for two years.

words.tip: 住在 + place: 我住在… Like German wohnen, it's about where you live, not being alive (活).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào shàng chuáng shuìjiào le.
examples.english: I'm going to bed.
This bed is comfortable.

words.tip: 张 is the measure word for flat things: beds, tables, paper. 起床 = get up.

characters.meaning: mum (女 woman + 马 mǎ for the sound)
the same character, doubled and said with no tone

examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma zuò de fàn hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: My mum's cooking is delicious.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gěi māma dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: I want to call my mum.

words.tip: The second syllable is toneless. 母亲 (mǔqīn) is the formal word. Note the 女 radical again.

characters.meaning: dad (父 father + 巴 bā for the sound)
the same character, doubled and said with no tone

examples.english: My dad works in Shanghai.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bàba xǐhuan hē chá ma?
examples.english: Does your dad like drinking tea?

words.tip: Same pattern as 妈妈. 父亲 (fùqīn) is formal.

examples.english: They have two kids.
This child is very cute.

words.tip: Use 两 (not 二) for 'two' before a measure word: 两个孩子.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.
examples.english: He's my good friend.
I'm seeing friends tonight.

words.tip: 男朋友 = boyfriend, 女朋友 = girlfriend, the same idea as German Freund / Freundin.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiārén dōu zài Déguó.
examples.english: My family are all in Germany.
How is your family?

words.tip: 家 (from the home session) + 人 person. A good moment to show how words are built from characters already known.

examples.english: I want a cup of coffee.
I'm going home now.

words.tip: Direct 'want', also 'going to': 我要走了 = I'm off now. 不要 = don't (want).

examples.english: I'd like to go to China.
I miss you a lot.

words.tip: Softer than 要, like German möchte. Also 'think' and 'miss': 我想你 = I miss you.

examples.english: I like reading.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan hé nǐ zài yìqǐ.
examples.english: I like being with you.

words.tip: 喜欢 + verb = like doing, the job German gern does. Works for people too: 我喜欢你.

examples.english: I'm happy today.
Why are you unhappy?

words.tip: Literally 'high mood'. 很高兴认识你 = nice to meet you, a callback to session 1.

examples.english: I'm really tired today.
Are you tired?

words.tip: 累死了 = exhausted (lit. tired to death), the same exaggeration as German todmüde.

examples.english: This one is good.
OK, let's go.

words.tip: 女 woman + 子 child = good, a classic picture. 好 + verb means 'nice to': 好吃 (tasty), 好看 (good-looking).

examples.english: Your room is big.
How old are you?

words.tip: A person with arms stretched wide. Also age: 你多大? = how old are you (to peers and adults).

examples.english: This cup is too small.
These shoes are a bit small.

words.tip: Also a friendly nickname prefix: 小王 = 'little Wang'. 太…了 = too…

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de xīn shǒujī.
examples.english: This is my new phone.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de xīn jiā hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: Your new home is beautiful.

words.tip: Already seen in 新年快乐. Goes straight before short nouns without 的: 新书, 新车.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de lǎo péngyou.
examples.english: He's an old friend of mine.
You're not old at all.

words.tip: For people and relationships (老朋友, 老师). Old things use 旧 (jiù): 旧手机. As a prefix it's affectionate: 老王.

examples.english: I have a question.
Please wait for me a moment.

words.tip: The tone shifts: yí before a 4th tone (一个 yí ge), yì before the others (一天 yì tiān), yī when counting or alone.

examples.english: Today is the 2nd of February.
I live on the second floor.

words.tip: For counting and in numbers (二十 = 20, 二月 = February). Before a measure word use 两 instead: 两个人.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu sān kǒu rén.
examples.english: There are three people in my family.
Let's meet at three.

words.tip: One, two, three are just one, two, three strokes. 口 (mouth) is the measure word for family members.

examples.english: I finish work at four.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le sì ge píngguǒ.
examples.english: I bought four apples.

words.tip: Sounds like 死 (sǐ, death), so 4 is unlucky and some buildings skip the 4th floor. Tongue twister: 四是四，十是十.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wǔ ge rén qù chī fàn.
examples.english: The five of us are going to eat.
I'll be there in five minutes.

words.tip: Show the one-handed Chinese counting gestures for 1–10. They're different from German finger counting.

examples.english: This is my book.
This isn't mine.

words.tip: Before a measure word many people say zhèi: 这个 zhège / zhèige. Both are fine.

examples.english: Who's that?
That's our car.

words.tip: 那 (nà, that) and 哪 (nǎ, which) differ by tone, and 哪 has the 口 radical that marks many question words.

examples.english: It's quiet here.
I really like it here.

words.tip: Northern speakers say 这儿 (zhèr). Same pattern as 哪里 from session 4.

examples.english: Have you been there?
Things there are expensive.

words.tip: Northern: 那儿 (nàr). Only the tone separates it from 哪里 (nǎlǐ, where), so drill the pair.

examples.english: The book is on the table.
Is your mum at home?

words.tip: Says where something is: 我在这里. Before a verb it means 'in the middle of': 我在吃饭 = I'm eating.

examples.english: You and I will go together.

examples.pinyin: Bàba hé māma dōu hěn hǎo.
examples.english: Mum and Dad are both well.

words.tip: Only joins nouns (我和你), never two sentences, unlike German und. Many speakers say 跟 (gēn) instead.

examples.english: Do you drink tea or coffee?

examples.text: 我们今天去还是明天去？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jīntiān qù háishi míngtiān qù?
examples.english: Shall we go today or tomorrow?

words.tip: 'Or' in questions. In statements use 或者 (huòzhě): 茶或者咖啡都可以 = tea or coffee are both fine.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn lèi, dànshì hěn gāoxìng.
examples.english: I'm tired but happy.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, dànshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
examples.english: I want to go, but I don't have time.

words.tip: Often shortened to 但. 可是 (kěshì) is a softer spoken alternative.

examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, wǒmen zài jiā.
examples.english: Because it's raining, we're staying home.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xué Zhōngwén, yīnwèi wǒ ài nǐ.
examples.english: I'm learning Chinese because I love you.

words.tip: The 'because' part normally comes first, whereas German usually puts the weil part second. Often paired with 所以.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn lèi, suǒyǐ zǎo diǎn shuì.
examples.english: I'm tired, so I'll go to bed early.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ bú qù.
examples.english: It's raining today, so I'm not going.

words.tip: Chinese happily says 因为… 所以… in one sentence ('because…, so…'), which sounds doubled up in English and German.

examples.english: How do you say it in Chinese?
What did you say?

words.tip: 用中文怎么说? is the most useful sentence for these sessions. 讠 is the 'speech' radical.

words.gloss: to look, to watch, to read

examples.english: Let's watch a film.
Let me have a look.

words.tip: A hand 手 over an eye 目, shading your eyes to look. Also read (看书) and visit (看朋友).

examples.english: Listen, it's raining.
I like listening to you talk.

words.tip: 听说… = I heard that… 听懂 = to understand by listening.

examples.english: I don't know.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào tā shì shéi ma?
examples.english: Do you know who he is?

words.tip: Knowing facts, like German wissen. In speech 道 is often toneless: zhīdao.

examples.english: Nice to meet you.
We've known each other for three years.

words.tip: Knowing people, like German kennen. Also recognising characters: 你认识这个字吗?

examples.english: I can speak a little Chinese.
Can you cook?

words.tip: For learned skills (languages, swimming), and 'will probably': 明天会下雨 = it'll probably rain tomorrow.

examples.english: Can you come tomorrow?
I can't go today.

words.tip: Ability or circumstances allowing. 会 (know how), 能 (able) and 可以 (allowed) make a great trio to explain.

examples.english: May I sit here?
We can go now.

words.tip: Permission, like German dürfen. 可以! on its own = sure, OK. Two 3rd tones: sounds like kéyǐ.

examples.english: You should go to bed earlier.
You should drink more water.

words.tip: Advice or expectation, like German sollen. Also 'probably': 他应该到了 = he should be there by now.

examples.english: I have to go.
You must go and see a doctor.

words.tip: Strong necessity. 'Don't have to' is 不用 (bú yòng), not 不必须, the same trap as German muss nicht.

examples.pinyin: Shànghǎi shì yí ge dà chéngshì.
examples.english: Shanghai is a big city.
Which city do you like?

words.tip: A walled market: 城 (wall) + 市 (market). Talk about which cities each of you has lived in.

examples.english: This road is long.
I don't know the way.

words.tip: 条 is the measure word for long thin things: roads, rivers, fish. 一路平安 = have a safe trip.

examples.pinyin: Tā de chē shì xīn de.
examples.english: His car is new.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí liàng chē.
examples.english: I want to buy a car.

words.tip: Any vehicle: 汽车 (car), 火车 (train, 'fire vehicle'), 自行车 (bicycle). Driving yourself is 开车.

examples.english: Let's take the train.
Do you take the bus to work?

words.tip: Sitting, and riding as a passenger: 坐车, 坐飞机. Two people 人人 on the ground 土. Same sound as 做 (do).

examples.english: Where is the station?
I'll pick you up at the station.

words.tip: Literally 'vehicle stand'. 火车站 = train station, 地铁站 = metro station.

examples.english: Where do you work?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan nǐ de gōngzuò ma?
examples.english: Do you like your job?

words.tip: Both a noun and a verb. The place comes before the verb: 在 + place + 工作.

examples.english: I'm studying Chinese.
Let's study together.

words.tip: Learning plus practising. 学 alone works too: 学中文.

examples.english: The kids are at school.

examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào lí wǒ jiā hěn jìn.
examples.english: The school is close to my home.

words.tip: 大学 (dàxué) = university, 'big learning'. 个 works as the measure word in speech.

examples.english: This book is really good.
What book are you reading?

words.tip: 看书 = to read. 书店 = bookshop.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de Zhōngwén lǎoshī.
examples.english: She's my Chinese teacher.
My mum is a teacher.

words.tip: Also how you address a teacher: 王老师. Fitting, since you're each other's 老师 now.

examples.pinyin: Xià ge xīngqī wǒmen qù Běijīng.
examples.english: Next week we're going to Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yí ge xīngqī gōngzuò wǔ tiān.
examples.english: I work five days a week.

words.tip: Days are numbered: 星期一 is Monday through 星期六 Saturday. Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日.

examples.english: Good morning!
I get up at seven in the morning.

words.tip: 早! on its own is a casual 'morning!'. 早饭 = breakfast.

examples.english: See you tonight!
What are we eating tonight?

words.tip: Covers evening and night. 晚安 (wǎn'ān) = good night, said at bedtime like Gute Nacht.

examples.english: It's three o'clock now.
What time do you finish work?

words.tip: 几点? = what time is it? 三点半 = 3:30, so no German-style 'half to four'. 一点儿 = a little.

examples.english: Do you have time?
It's getting late.

words.tip: Time as an amount, like German Zeit. Clock time uses 点. 没有时间 = no time.

examples.english: I'm going grocery shopping.
What do you want to buy?

words.tip: 买 (mǎi, buy) and 卖 (mài, sell) differ only by tone and the 十 on top. Drill them as a pair.

examples.english: Do they sell coffee here?
How much is this? (lit. how is this sold?)

words.tip: Falling tone, the partner of 买. 买卖 (mǎimai, 'buy-sell') = business.

examples.english: I'm out of money.
I didn't bring any money today.

words.tip: The 钅 radical means metal, because early money was metal. Prices use 块 (kuài) in speech, 元 (yuán) in writing.

examples.english: How much is this?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ shì duōshao?
examples.english: What's your phone number?

words.tip: Literally 'many-few'. 多少钱? is the shopping question. For small numbers people use 几 (jǐ) instead.

examples.english: Too expensive!
The coffee here isn't expensive.

words.tip: 太贵了! is essential at markets. Also 'honourable': 您贵姓? = may I ask your surname?

examples.english: I get up at six.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liù ge rén yìqǐ chī fàn.
examples.english: The six of us are eating together.

words.tip: A lucky number: 六 sounds like 溜 (liù, smooth, slick), as in 六六大顺 (may everything go smoothly). Online, 666 means 'awesome'.

examples.pinyin: Yí ge xīngqī yǒu qī tiān.
examples.english: A week has seven days.
My little sister is seven this year.

words.tip: Note the q, which sounds like 'ch' in 'cheese'. A good one for practising pinyin spelling.

examples.english: The film starts at eight.
This dish costs eight yuan.

words.tip: The luckiest number: 八 sounds like 发 (fā, to prosper). The Beijing Olympics opened on 8/8/2008.

examples.english: Nine o'clock is too early.
My birthday is in September.

words.tip: Sounds like 久 (jiǔ, long-lasting), so it's popular around weddings.

examples.english: I'll count to ten.

examples.text: 从我家到公司要十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā dào gōngsī yào shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: It takes ten minutes from my home to the office.

words.tip: Bigger numbers are perfectly regular: 十一 = 11, 二十 = 20, 九十九 = 99. Compare German neunundneunzig, which says the ones first.

examples.english: There are lots of people here.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì yí ge rén lái de.
examples.english: I came on my own.

words.tip: A person walking on two legs. Nationalities add 人: 德国人 (German), 中国人 (Chinese).

examples.english: Who's that man?
Men can cook too.

words.tip: 男 is a field 田 over strength 力: the one working the field. 男朋友 = boyfriend.

examples.english: That woman is a teacher.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn mài nǚrén de yīfu.
examples.english: This shop sells women's clothes.

words.tip: Note the ü in nǚ. The 女 radical has turned up in 她, 妈妈 and 好.

examples.english: That girl is reading a book.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie shēng le yí ge nǚhái.
examples.english: My older sister had a baby girl.

words.tip: Also 女孩子. Boy = 男孩. Fun contrast: German das Mädchen is grammatically neuter.

examples.english: His name sounds nice.
How do you write your name?

words.tip: Surnames come first: 王小明 = Wang Xiaoming. Talk about what each of your names means.

examples.english: Whose coffee is this?

examples.pinyin: Hóngsè de nàge shì wǒ de.
examples.english: The red one is mine.

words.tip: Turns anything into 'X's': 我的 (my), 妈妈的 (mum's). Often dropped for close family and friends: 我妈妈.

examples.english: Hi, everyone!
When are you all coming?

words.tip: Like German ihr (you all). Same 们 as 我们 from session 2.

examples.english: They're my friends.
Do you know them?

words.tip: 她们 for an all-female group; mixed groups use 他们. All sound the same.

examples.english: I cook for myself.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ zìjǐ de fángjiān.
examples.english: This is my own room.

words.tip: Adds 'myself / yourself': 你自己去吧 = go by yourself. 自己的 = one's own.

examples.english: Hello, everyone!
Everyone really likes you.

words.tip: Literally 'big family'. Matches German alle. 大家好 opens almost every speech.

examples.english: The child is sleeping.
What time do you go to bed?

words.tip: A verb-plus-object pair that can be split: 睡了一个好觉 = had a good sleep. 觉 is read jué in 觉得 (session 26).

examples.english: What book are you reading?

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ dú yíxià zhège jùzi.
examples.english: Please read this sentence out.

words.tip: Reading aloud, or studying (读大学 = go to university). Reading for fun is often just 看书.

examples.english: How do you write this character?

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ xiě nǐ de míngzi.
examples.english: Please write your name here.

words.tip: 这个字怎么写? will be your most-asked question. Practise stroke order together.

examples.english: The kids are playing in the park.
Where shall we go for fun at the weekend?

words.tip: Also 'hang out': 周末去哪儿玩? Sports and instruments use other verbs (打篮球, 弹钢琴), unlike German spielen.

examples.english: I'll wait for you.
Who are you waiting for?

words.tip: 等一下 = wait a moment. At the end of a list it means 'etc.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ yì běn shū.
examples.english: I'll give you a book.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gěi nǐ kàn yì zhāng zhàopiàn.
examples.english: I want to show you a photo.

words.tip: Also 'for / to': 给你打电话 = call you. 给你! = here you go.

examples.english: Hold this for a second.
I'll carry your luggage for you.

words.tip: There's a hand 手 at the bottom. 拿走 = take away, 拿来 = bring over.

examples.english: Don't forget to bring your keys.

examples.text: 我带你去我最喜欢的饭馆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dài nǐ qù wǒ zuì xǐhuan de fànguǎn.
examples.english: I'll take you to my favourite restaurant.

words.tip: Taking something or someone with you. 带孩子 = to look after the kids.

examples.english: Can you help me?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bāng wǒ kàn yíxià, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Take a look at this for me, would you?

words.tip: 帮忙 (bāngmáng) is the 'help out' form: 谢谢你帮忙. 帮我 + verb = do something for me.

examples.english: I need your help.
What else do we need to buy?

words.tip: Stronger than 要. 不需要 = no need.

examples.english: What do you think?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhège cài hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: I think this dish is delicious.

words.tip: Opinions and feelings, like German glauben or finden. 我觉得很好 = I think it's good.

examples.text: 我可以问你一个问题吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ wèn nǐ yí ge wèntí ma?
examples.english: Can I ask you a question?
Go and ask the teacher.

words.tip: A mouth 口 inside a door 门: asking at the door. 问题 = question; 没问题 = no problem.

examples.english: Tell me your name.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì bié gàosu wǒ māma.
examples.english: Don't tell my mum about this.

words.tip: 告诉 + person + thing. 我告诉你 = let me tell you.

examples.english: Do you understand?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de tài kuài, wǒ tīng bu dǒng.
examples.english: You speak too fast, I can't understand.

words.tip: 听懂 = understand by listening, 看懂 = understand by reading. 我不懂 = I don't get it.

examples.english: What does this character mean?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngbai nǐ de yìsi le.
examples.english: I understand what you mean now.

words.tip: A learner's best friend: …是什么意思? Also 有意思 = interesting, 不好意思 = excuse me.

examples.english: The weather's nice today.

examples.text: 天气好的时候我们去公园。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì hǎo de shíhou wǒmen qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: When the weather is nice we go to the park.

words.tip: Literally 'sky air'. 天气预报 = weather forecast.

examples.english: The sun's come out.
There's no sun today.

words.tip: 阳 is the 'yang' of yin and yang. The older word 日 lives on in 日本 (Japan, 'sun's origin').

examples.english: It's raining outside.
It often rains here.

words.tip: Rain 'falls down': 下雨, and snow is 下雪. No 'it' needed, unlike German es regnet.

examples.english: It's too hot today.

examples.pinyin: Chá hái hěn rè, děng yíxià zài hē.
examples.english: The tea is still hot, wait a bit before drinking it.

words.tip: The four dots at the bottom (灬) mean fire. 热水 (hot water) came up in session 7.

examples.english: Winter is cold.
Are you cold?

words.tip: The two strokes on the left (冫) mean ice. 我很冷 = I'm cold, simpler than German Mir ist kalt.

examples.english: I like red.
She likes wearing red clothes.

words.tip: The colour of luck: red envelopes (红包) at New Year. Add 色 for the colour as a noun: 红色.

examples.english: The sky is really blue.

examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjing shì lánsè de.
examples.english: His eyes are blue.

words.tip: The grass radical 艹 on top: blue dye originally came from a plant.

examples.english: The leaves are green.
I drink green tea every day.

words.tip: Another ü: lǜ. 绿茶 (green tea) from session 7.

examples.english: I drink black coffee.

examples.pinyin: Tā de tóufa yòu hēi yòu cháng.
examples.english: Her hair is black and long.

words.tip: Fire 灬 at the bottom: soot. 天黑了 = it's got dark.

examples.english: Snow is white.

examples.pinyin: Tā de tóufa dōu bái le.
examples.english: His hair has all turned white.

words.tip: Also 'for nothing': 白跑一趟 = a wasted trip. 明白 (clear and bright) = to understand.

examples.english: He's always late.
You're always so busy.

words.tip: Goes before the verb like other adverbs. 一直 (yìzhí) means 'all along, continuously'.

examples.english: We often eat together.
I often think of you.

words.tip: Doubled for emphasis. 经常 (jīngcháng) means the same.

examples.english: I never drink coffee.
She never gets angry.

words.tip: For past experiences use 从来没…过: 我从来没去过德国 = I've never been to Germany.

examples.english: I've already eaten.
It's already twelve o'clock.

words.tip: Usually paired with 了 at the end: 已经…了.

examples.english: Are you still at home?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái xiǎng chī yí ge.
examples.english: I want to eat another one.

words.tip: Still, also, and 还没 = not yet: 我还没吃. The same character as in 还是 (session 14).

examples.english: I have a headache.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de tóu hái téng ma?
examples.english: Does your head still hurt?

words.tip: …疼 = …hurts: 头疼, 肚子疼 (stomach ache). 头 is also the measure word for cattle.

examples.pinyin: Chī fàn qián yào xǐ shǒu.
examples.english: Wash your hands before eating.
Your hands are cold.

words.tip: 手机 = mobile phone ('hand machine'), just like German Handy.

examples.english: She has big eyes.
Please close your eyes.

words.tip: A pair of eyes: 一双眼睛. The 目 radical (an eye) also appears in 看.

examples.english: I'm sick.

examples.pinyin: Duō hē shuǐ, jiù bù róngyì shēngbìng.
examples.english: Drink plenty of water and you won't get ill so easily.

words.tip: The 疒 radical means illness (also in 疼). 多喝热水 (drink lots of hot water) is the classic advice!

examples.english: I need to see a doctor.

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō wǒ yào duō xiūxi.
examples.english: The doctor says I need to rest more.

words.tip: 看医生 = to see a doctor. 医院 = hospital.

examples.english: This top looks really nice.
I need to do the laundry.

words.tip: 件 counts tops and single garments. 衣 shrinks to 衤 on the left of clothing characters, as in 裤.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi tài cháng le.
examples.english: These trousers are too long.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yì tiáo xīn kùzi.
examples.english: I want to buy a new pair of trousers.

words.tip: One pair of trousers is 一条裤子, not 一双: 条 is for long, thin things. 短裤 (duǎnkù) = shorts.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào mǎi yì shuāng xié.
examples.english: I want to buy a pair of shoes.
Please change your shoes when you come in.

words.tip: 一双鞋 = a pair of shoes, 一只鞋 = one shoe. Many homes have slippers (拖鞋) waiting at the door: 换鞋 = change your shoes.

words.gloss: to wear, to put on (clothes, shoes)

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān hěn lěng, duō chuān diǎn yīfu.
examples.english: It's cold today, wear something warm.
What are you wearing tomorrow?

words.tip: 穿 is for things you get into: clothes, trousers, shoes, socks. Hats, glasses and watches take 戴 instead, where German uses tragen for both.

examples.english: He wears glasses.
I'm not wearing a watch today.

words.tip: Contrast with 穿: 戴帽子 (hat), 戴眼镜 (glasses), 戴手表 (watch). Don't mix it up with 带 (to bring), which sounds exactly the same.

examples.english: Mum is cooking in the kitchen.
Our kitchen isn't big.

words.tip: Same 房 as 房间. 厨师 (chúshī) = chef.

examples.english: I'll cook tonight.
My dad is a great cook.

words.tip: Literally 'make a meal'. It's verb + object, so it can split: 做了饭, 做一顿饭. Ask who does the cooking in each of your families.

examples.english: This table is big.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào yì zhāng dà zhuōzi.
examples.english: We need a big table.

words.tip: 张 counts flat surfaces: tables, beds, paper, photos. 桌 has 木 (wood) at the bottom.

characters.meaning: plate, tray (皿 dish at the bottom)

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí ge pánzi.
examples.english: Could you pass me a plate?
I'll go and wash the plates.

words.tip: 皿 at the bottom is a picture of a dish. 盘 also works as a measure for food: 一盘饺子 = a plate of dumplings.

examples.english: This is my cup.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu liǎng ge bēizi.
examples.english: There are two cups on the table.

words.tip: 杯 is also the measure for drinks: 一杯茶 (a cup of tea) vs 一个杯子 (a cup). 干杯 (gānbēi) = cheers!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān chī yí ge píngguǒ.
examples.english: I eat an apple every day.
How much are these apples?

words.tip: Also the brand: 苹果手机 = iPhone. On Christmas Eve (平安夜) people give apples, because 苹 sounds like 平 in 平安 (peace, safety).

examples.english: What fruit do you like?

examples.pinyin: Fàn hòu wǒmen chī diǎn shuǐguǒ ba.
examples.english: Let's have some fruit after the meal.

words.tip: Literally 'water fruit'. 种 = kind: 三种水果 = three kinds of fruit. A plate of cut-up fruit after dinner is a classic way Chinese families show care.

examples.pinyin: Duō chī shūcài duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Eating lots of vegetables is good for you.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duō mǎi yìdiǎn shūcài ba.
examples.english: Let's buy a few more vegetables.

words.tip: Both characters have the grass radical 艹. In everyday speech people often just say 菜, as in 买菜 (to buy groceries).

examples.english: I don't eat meat.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jīntiān mǎi diǎn ròu ba.
examples.english: Let's buy some meat today.

words.tip: Plain 肉 often means pork; 牛肉 = beef, 鸡肉 = chicken. At the market meat is sold by the 斤 (half a kilo).

examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang wǒ chī le liǎng ge jīdàn.
examples.english: I had two eggs this morning.

examples.pinyin: Jiā li hái yǒu jīdàn ma?
examples.english: Are there any eggs left at home?

words.tip: Literally 'chicken egg'. 西红柿炒鸡蛋 (tomato and egg stir-fry) is the classic first dish to cook together.

examples.english: The food at this restaurant is great.

examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào pángbiān yǒu yì jiā fànguǎn.
examples.english: There's a restaurant next to the school.

words.tip: 家 counts businesses. 馆 is a building for a purpose, as in 咖啡馆 (café) and 图书馆 (library).

examples.english: Let's order.
Waiter, we'd like to order!

words.tip: Show how to call the staff: 服务员，点菜! Dishes usually go in the middle for everyone to share, so ordering is a group decision.

examples.english: This dish is too spicy.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan chī Zhōngguó cài ma?
examples.english: Do you like Chinese food?

words.tip: Two meanings: vegetables (买菜) and a dish of food (中国菜 = Chinese food). 道 counts the dishes in a meal: 一道菜.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò de fàn hěn hǎochī!
examples.english: Your cooking is delicious!

examples.text: 这里的水果又便宜又好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de shuǐguǒ yòu piányi yòu hǎochī.
examples.english: The fruit here is cheap and tasty.

words.tip: 好 + verb = nice to …: 好喝 (nice to drink), 好看 (nice to look at), 好听 (nice to hear). The opposite is 不好吃 or 难吃.

examples.english: Excuse me, the bill please!

examples.pinyin: Fúwùyuán, qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi shuǐ.
examples.english: Waiter, a glass of water, please.

words.tip: Calling out 服务员! across the room is normal, not rude. 员 marks someone's job, as in 售货员 (shop assistant).

examples.english: We're travelling to Germany in the summer.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan yí ge rén lǚxíng.
examples.english: I like travelling alone.

words.tip: Note the ü: lǚ. 旅游 (lǚyóu) is the everyday word for a sightseeing trip.

examples.english: We're flying to Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài fēijī shang shuì bu zháo.
examples.english: I can't sleep on planes.

words.tip: Literally 'flying machine'. You 坐 (sit on) any transport: 坐飞机, 坐车. 架 counts planes: 一架飞机.

examples.english: I'll pick you up at the airport.
How do we get to the airport?

words.tip: 机 here is short for 飞机. Useful pair: 接 = pick someone up, 送 = see someone off.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de xíngli tài duō le!
examples.english: You've got too much luggage!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xíngli hái méi dào.
examples.english: My luggage hasn't arrived yet.

words.tip: Uncountable like German Gepäck, so count pieces: 两件行李. 行 is xíng here, not háng (as in 银行, bank), and 李 is also the surname Li.

examples.english: Don't forget your passport!

examples.text: 请给我看一下你的护照。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ kàn yíxià nǐ de hùzhào.
examples.english: Please show me your passport.

words.tip: It's a booklet, so it takes 本 like a book. 照 is also in 照片 (photo).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.english: My home is close to the school.
We live very close by.

words.tip: Pattern: A 离 B 很近 = A is close to B. The 辶 radical (walking) shows up in lots of movement and distance words.

examples.english: Is the airport far from here?
We walked a long way.

words.tip: The opposite of 近, with the same 辶 radical. Watch the tone: yuǎn (far) vs yuán (as in 元, the currency).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī zài zhuōzi shang.
examples.english: Your phone's on the table.
Let's go upstairs.

words.tip: It comes after the noun: 桌子上 = on the table. Also 'up' and 'previous': 上楼 (go upstairs), 上个星期 (last week).

examples.english: The cat is under the bed.
I'll wait for you downstairs.

words.tip: The mirror of 上, also after the noun: 床下, 桌子下面. Also 'next': 下个星期 = next week. Both characters are a stroke above or below a line.

examples.english: The station is right next to the school.
Is anyone sitting next to you?

words.tip: Pattern: A 在 B 旁边 = A is next to B. Point at things around the room and practise: 我在你旁边.

examples.english: What time are we meeting tomorrow?
We haven't seen each other in ages.

words.tip: Literally 'see face'. It takes no object: say 跟他见面 (meet him), never 见面他. Tell each other about the first time you met.

examples.english: I'm here!
What time does the train get to Beijing?

words.tip: 我到了 is the message you send when you arrive. Also 'to' with places and times: 从八点到十点 = from eight to ten.

examples.english: Let's go home.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng huí Zhōngguó kàn fùmǔ.
examples.english: I want to go back to China to see my parents.

words.tip: 回家 = go home. 回来 = come back, 回去 = go back. The character is a box inside a box, like something coming round again.

examples.text: 今天晚上我们出去吃饭吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang wǒmen chūqù chī fàn ba.
examples.english: Let's eat out tonight.
alternatives: 我们今天晚上出去吃饭吧。

examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn xià yǔ, wǒ bù xiǎng chūqù.
examples.english: It's raining outside, I don't want to go out.

words.tip: 出 + 去/来 shows direction: 出去 = go out (away from the speaker), 出来 = come out (towards the speaker). The 去 is often said lightly, chūqu.

examples.english: Come in, please!
Please come in and sit down.

words.tip: 请进 is what you say when someone knocks. 进 (enter) and 近 (near) sound exactly the same, so compare the characters.

examples.english: I was really tired yesterday.
Where did you go yesterday?

words.tip: No past tense needed: the time word does the work. Complete the set: 前天 (day before yesterday), 昨天, 今天, 明天.

examples.english: What do you want to do at the weekend?
I'm free this weekend.

words.tip: 周 is another word for week, like 星期. 末 is a tree 木 with a stroke marking the tip: the end. 周末快乐 = have a nice weekend.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān qǐ de hěn zǎo.
examples.english: You got up early today.

examples.text: 现在还早，再睡一会儿吧。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài hái zǎo, zài shuì yíhuìr ba.
examples.english: It's still early, sleep a bit longer.

words.tip: 早! on its own means 'morning!' (short for 早上好). The sun 日 sits on top; picture it just risen above 十.

examples.pinyin: Tài wǎn le, wǒmen huí jiā ba.
examples.english: It's late, let's go home.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān huì wǎn yìdiǎn huí jiā.
examples.english: I'll be home a bit late today.

words.tip: Also 'evening', as in 晚上 and 晚安 (good night). 我来晚了 = sorry I'm late.

examples.english: I have to work on Monday.
See you on Monday!

words.tip: The days are just numbered: 星期一 to 星期六, but Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日. 一 keeps its first tone here.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xià ge yuè qù Zhōngguó.
examples.english: We're going to China next month.

examples.pinyin: Yì nián yǒu shí'èr ge yuè.
examples.english: A year has twelve months.

words.tip: 三月 = March, but 三个月 = three months: the 个 makes all the difference. The moon itself is usually 月亮 (yuèliang).

examples.english: Let's go to the seaside in summer.
Summers here are very hot.

words.tip: Every season is just season + 天. 夏 (summer) is fourth tone, the same sound as 下.

examples.english: Winters in Germany are cold.

examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān wǒ chángcháng hē rè chá.
examples.english: In winter I often drink hot tea.

words.tip: 冬 (winter) sounds like 东 (east). Tell them apart by the two dots at the bottom of 冬, like the ice in 冷.

examples.english: Spring is here!

examples.pinyin: Chūntiān gōngyuán li yǒu hěn duō huā.
examples.english: In spring there are lots of flowers in the park.

words.tip: 春节 (Spring Festival) is Chinese New Year, which marks the start of spring in the lunar calendar. Note the sun 日 at the bottom of 春.

examples.english: Autumn is my favourite season.

examples.text: 秋天的天气不冷也不热。
examples.pinyin: Qiūtiān de tiānqì bù lěng yě bú rè.
examples.english: Autumn weather is neither cold nor hot.

words.tip: 秋 is grain 禾 next to fire 火: harvest time. At the Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节) families eat mooncakes (月饼).

examples.english: Don't be sad.
I know you're very sad.

words.tip: Literally 'hard to get through'. The everyday word for feeling down; 伤心 (shāngxīn) is stronger, heartbroken.

examples.english: I'm scared of dogs.
Don't be afraid, I'm here.

words.tip: Takes its object directly: 我怕黑 = I'm afraid of the dark. 忄 on the left is the heart radical, found in many feeling words.

examples.english: I love you.
Do you love me?

words.tip: Many people rarely say 我爱你 out loud and show it in actions instead. 520 (wǔ èr líng) sounds like 我爱你, so 20 May is a romantic day.

examples.english: What are you laughing at?

examples.pinyin: Tā xiào de shíhou hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: She's very pretty when she smiles.

words.tip: 笑 covers both laughing and smiling; 微笑 (wēixiào) is specifically a smile. Online, 哈哈哈 = haha.

examples.english: The child is crying.
Why are you crying?

words.tip: Two mouths 口 over a dog 犬: a howl. Watch the tone: kū (cry) vs kǔ (苦, bitter).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī méi diàn le.
examples.english: My phone's dead.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎo bu dào wǒ de shǒujī.
examples.english: I can't find my phone.

words.tip: 'Hand machine', just like German Handy. Practise asking for a number: 你的手机号是多少?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ wǎnshang gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: I'll call you tonight.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu shì gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: Call me if anything comes up.

words.tip: Pattern: 给 + person + 打电话 = call someone. 打 is a do-everything verb: 打球 (play ball), 打车 (take a taxi).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàndào wǒ de xiāoxi le ma?
examples.english: Did you see my message?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí ge hǎo xiāoxi!
examples.english: I have good news!

words.tip: 发消息 = send a message, e.g. on WeChat (微信). 好消息 = good news. 条 counts messages and news items.

examples.pinyin: Gěi wǒ kànkan nǐ de zhàopiàn.
examples.english: Show me your photos.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ pāi zhāng zhàopiàn ba.
examples.english: Let's take a photo together.

words.tip: 张, because a photo is flat. 拍照 = take a photo. Many speakers say zhàopiān in everyday speech.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de diànnǎo tài lǎo le.
examples.english: My computer is too old.
I work on a computer.

words.tip: Literally 'electric brain'. 台 counts machines and appliances: 一台电脑. A laptop is 笔记本 (notebook).

examples.english: Chinese isn't easy.
Making this dish is easy.

words.tip: Also 'likely to': 冬天容易生病 = it's easy to get sick in winter. The opposite is 难.

examples.english: Chinese characters are hard to write.
Is learning German hard?

words.tip: 难 + verb = hard to …, or unpleasant to …: 难吃 (tastes bad), 难看 (ugly). The same 难 as in 难过 (sad).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de tài kuài le!
examples.english: You're talking too fast!
Time flies!

words.tip: Also 'soon': 快…了 = about to, as in 快到了 (almost there). It has the heart radical 忄, as in 快乐 (happy).

examples.english: Please speak a bit more slowly.
Take your time, we have time.

words.tip: The learner's lifeline: 请说慢一点. 慢慢来 = take your time. Same heart radical 忄 as 快.

examples.english: Sorry, I was wrong.
This character is written wrong.

words.tip: The opposite of 对. 不错 (búcuò, 'not wrong') means 'pretty good' and is a very common compliment.

examples.english: Let's start!

examples.text: 你什么时候开始学中文的？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou kāishǐ xué Zhōngwén de?
examples.english: When did you start learning Chinese?

words.tip: Can be followed by another verb: 开始学中文 = start learning Chinese. Also a noun: 一开始 = at first.

examples.english: What time does the film finish?
The match is already over.

words.tip: For events ending: films, classes, meetings. To say you've finished doing something, use verb + 完: 我吃完了 = I've finished eating.

examples.english: You go on ahead.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān hē diǎn chá ba.
examples.english: Let's have some tea first.

words.tip: Goes before the verb, and pairs with 然后 or 再: 先吃饭，然后看电影. 先生 (xiānsheng) = Mr; husband.

examples.pinyin: Xiān xǐ shǒu, ránhòu chī fàn.
examples.english: Wash your hands first, then eat.

examples.text: 我吃了早饭，然后去上班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chī le zǎofàn, ránhòu qù shàngbān.
examples.english: I had breakfast and then went to work.

words.tip: Great for telling stories: …然后…然后…. Don't confuse it with 以后 (yǐhòu), 'later, in the future'.

examples.english: In the end we went to Beijing.
This is the last time.

words.tip: Also 'last': 最后一天 = the last day. 最 + adjective = most: 最好, 最大.

examples.english: Please open the window.
The window's open, it's a bit cold.

words.tip: 扇 (shàn) counts windows and doors: 一扇门. Many Chinese families air rooms every day, much like German Lüften.

examples.english: This chair is really comfortable.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hái xūyào liǎng bǎ yǐzi.
examples.english: We need two more chairs.

words.tip: 把 counts things you can grab by a handle: chairs, keys, knives, umbrellas (一把伞). 椅 has 木 (wood) on the left, like 桌.

examples.english: Where are my keys?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ yàoshi wàng zài jiā li le.
examples.english: I left my keys at home.

words.tip: 钥 is read yào here. 钅 on the left is the metal radical. 把 counts keys: 一把钥匙.

examples.english: Please turn off the light.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng kāi yíxià dēng ma?
examples.english: Can you turn the light on?

words.tip: 开灯 / 关灯 = turn the light on / off. 火 on the left: lamps used to be flames. 盏 (zhǎn) is the classic measure, 个 is fine in speech.

characters.meaning: to send out (used for its sound)

examples.pinyin: Tā zài shāfā shang shuìzháo le.
examples.english: He fell asleep on the sofa.

examples.pinyin: Māo xǐhuan shuì zài shāfā shang.
examples.english: The cat likes sleeping on the sofa.

words.tip: A sound loan from 'sofa': the characters just spell the sound. Find others together: 咖啡 (coffee), 巧克力 (chocolate).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yǎng yì zhī gǒu.
examples.english: I'd like to get a dog.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān dài gǒu qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: I take the dog to the park every day.

words.tip: 养 (yǎng) = to keep a pet. 犭 is the animal radical, also in 猫. 一条狗 is common too, especially in the north.

examples.english: The cat's asleep.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā de māo bù xǐhuan xǐzǎo.
examples.english: Our cat doesn't like baths.

words.tip: The sound part 苗 (miáo) echoes the meow, and cats say 喵 (miāo). Same animal radical 犭 as 狗.

examples.pinyin: Ménkǒu yǒu yì kē dà shù.
examples.english: There's a big tree by the door.

examples.pinyin: Zhè kē shù yǒu yìbǎi nián le.
examples.english: This tree is a hundred years old.

words.tip: 棵 (kē) counts trees and plants. 木 on the left means wood: 木 alone is a tree, 林 a wood, 森林 a forest.

examples.english: What's your favourite animal?
Children all like little animals.

words.tip: Literally 'moving thing'. 动物园 = zoo. Ask each other's zodiac animal: 你属什么?

examples.pinyin: Shān shang de fēngjǐng hěn měi.
examples.english: The view from the mountain is beautiful.

examples.pinyin: Shān shang yǒu hěn duō shù.
examples.english: There are lots of trees on the mountain.

words.tip: A picture of three peaks. 爬山 ('climb mountain') means hiking. 座 counts big, solid things: mountains, bridges, buildings.

examples.english: I like listening to music.
What kind of music do you like?

words.tip: 乐 has two readings: yuè (music) and lè (happy, as in 快乐). Swap favourite songs from each country.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān yùndòng bàn ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I exercise for half an hour every day.
I don't really like sport.

words.tip: Also a noun: 你喜欢什么运动? = what sports do you like? The same 动 (move) as in 动物.

examples.english: Let's go to karaoke!
She sings beautifully.

words.tip: Verb + object like 做饭: 唱一首歌 = sing a song. 去唱歌 usually means going to KTV (karaoke), a very popular night out.

examples.english: Can you dance?
They're dancing in the living room.

words.tip: Literally 'jump a dance'. Talk about 广场舞: groups dancing together in squares and parks every evening, often retirees.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshang qù kàn diànyǐng ba.
examples.english: Let's go to the cinema tonight.
What films do you like watching?

words.tip: 'Electric shadows'. 看电影 = watch a film, 电影院 = cinema. 部 counts films, just like phones.

examples.english: This question is hard.
Do you have any more questions?

words.tip: Both 'question' and 'problem': 没问题 = no problem! 问 is a mouth 口 in a doorway 门.

examples.english: Please answer my question.

examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí wǒ bú huì huídá.
examples.english: I can't answer this question.

words.tip: Literally 'return an answer', with the same 回 as 回家. 答 has bamboo ⺮ on top.

examples.english: Maybe it'll rain tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Tā yěxǔ yǐjīng dào jiā le.
examples.english: Maybe he's already home.

words.tip: Two third tones in a row, so it's said yéxǔ. 可能 (kěnéng) means the same and is just as common.

examples.english: Of course you can!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dāngrán jìde nǐ de shēngrì.
examples.english: Of course I remember your birthday.

words.tip: 当然 works as a full answer on its own: 你爱我吗？当然! The same 然 as in 然后.

examples.english: I'll definitely come.
You must be hungry, right?

words.tip: Also 'must be': 你一定很累 = you must be tired. 不一定 = not necessarily. 一 becomes yí before the fourth tone of 定.

examples.english: This is really cheap.
Can you make it a bit cheaper?

words.tip: 便 is usually biàn (as in 方便, convenient) but pián here. The bargaining line: 能便宜一点吗? = can you make it cheaper?

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn jǐ diǎn guānmén?
examples.english: What time does this shop close?
What does that shop sell?

words.tip: 家 counts businesses. 店 on its own turns up everywhere: 书店 (bookshop), 饭店 (restaurant, hotel).

examples.english: I'll pay.
How much did you pay?

words.tip: Arguing over who pays the bill is a classic ritual, and insisting 我来! is polite. Most people pay by phone with WeChat Pay or Alipay.

examples.text: 我在一家德国公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài yì jiā Déguó gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.english: I work for a German company.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī yǒu wǔshí ge rén.
examples.english: Our company has fifty people.

words.tip: 家 counts companies, like 饭馆 and 商店. 去公司 is how people often say 'go to the office'.

examples.english: I'm going to buy a few things.
I'd like something to eat.

words.tip: Literally 'east-west'. Keep xi toneless: with a full tone, dōngxī means 'east and west'. 买东西 = go shopping.

examples.english: We're getting married next year.
My older sister is already married.

words.tip: It takes no object: say 跟她结婚 (marry her), never 结婚她. 结 is the knot from 结束, and 婚 has the 女 radical.

examples.english: Our wedding is in the summer.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng yào shénmeyàng de hūnlǐ?
examples.english: What kind of wedding do you want?

words.tip: 场 (chǎng) counts events: 一场婚礼. Red is the wedding colour, and guests give money in red envelopes (红包).

examples.english: Let's go together.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hé wǒmen yìqǐ qù ma?
examples.english: Do you want to come with us?

words.tip: Goes before the verb, often with 和 or 跟: 我和你一起去. 一 becomes yì before the third tone of 起.

examples.english: You have such a kind heart.
You're in my heart.

words.tip: Also 'mind'. The heart radical 忄 in 快, 慢 and 怕 is a squeezed 心. 小心 ('small heart') = be careful!

examples.english: I miss you so much.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎngniàn māma zuò de cài.
examples.english: I miss my mum's cooking.

words.tip: In everyday speech plain 想 works too: 我想你 = I miss you. Both 想 and 念 have 心 (heart) at the bottom.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shēngrì shì jǐ yuè jǐ hào?
examples.english: When's your birthday?
How do you want to spend your birthday?

words.tip: Dates go from big to small: 五月二十号 = 20 May. Long-life noodles (长寿面) are the traditional birthday dish.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gěi nǐ de lǐwù.
examples.english: This is a present for you.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan wǒ sòng de lǐwù ma?
examples.english: Do you like the present I gave you?

words.tip: Never give a clock (送钟 sounds like 'attending a funeral') or share a pear (分梨 sounds like 'separate'). Gifts are often politely refused once before being accepted.

examples.text: 我们怎么庆祝你的生日？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zěnme qìngzhù nǐ de shēngrì?
examples.english: How shall we celebrate your birthday?

examples.text: 我们去饭馆庆祝一下吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù fànguǎn qìngzhù yíxià ba.
examples.english: Let's go to a restaurant to celebrate.

words.tip: Works for big and small occasions: 庆祝新年. 国庆节 (National Day, 1 October) uses the same 庆.

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ jiā yǒu ge jùhuì.
examples.english: We're having a get-together at ours this weekend.

examples.pinyin: Zuótiān de jùhuì hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: Yesterday's party was a lot of fun.

words.tip: More 'get-together' than wild party: friends or classmates meeting up for food and chat. 会 here means 'meeting', not 'can'.

examples.english: Happy birthday to you!

examples.text: 大家一起祝他生日快乐。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā yìqǐ zhù tā shēngrì kuàilè.
examples.english: Everyone wished him a happy birthday together.

words.tip: 祝你… is how to give any good wish: 祝你好运 (good luck), 祝你一路平安 (safe journey). Sing 祝你生日快乐 to the Happy Birthday tune.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ měi tiān jǐ diǎn qǐchuáng?
examples.english: What time do you get up every day?
Get up quick, we're going to be late!

words.tip: Literally 'rise from bed'. Just waking up is 醒 (xǐng), so you can 醒了 but not yet 起床. 起床了! is the classic wake-up call.

words.gloss: to shower, to have a bath

examples.english: I'm going to have a shower first.
I like to shower in the evening.

words.tip: Two third tones, so it's said xízǎo. It covers showers and baths alike, and it's verb + object, so it splits: 洗个澡 = have a quick wash.

examples.english: Have you brushed your teeth?

examples.pinyin: Shuìjiào qián bié wàng le shuāyá.
examples.english: Don't forget to brush your teeth before bed.

words.tip: 牙刷 (toothbrush) is the same two characters the other way round. 刷 is also swiping a card or phone: 刷卡.

characters.meaning: mirror (钅 metal: mirrors were once bronze)

examples.english: This mirror is big.
Is there a mirror in the bathroom?

words.tip: 面 counts flat things you look at, like mirrors and flags (一面旗). The same 镜 as in 眼镜 (glasses).

examples.english: Pass me a towel.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo máojīn shì shéi de?
examples.english: Whose towel is this?

words.tip: Literally 'fur cloth'. 条, because a towel is long and soft. 巾 is a hanging cloth, also in 纸巾 (paper tissue).

examples.english: There's no salt in this dish.
Please add a bit more salt.

words.tip: Use 放 (fàng, to put in) for adding seasoning: 放盐, 放糖. 皿 at the bottom is the dish radical, as in 盘子.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de kāfēi yào fàng táng ma?
examples.english: Do you take sugar in your coffee?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hē kāfēi bú fàng táng.
examples.english: I don't take sugar in my coffee.

words.tip: Both sugar and sweets: 吃糖 = eat sweets. 米 (rice) on the left hints at food. Don't mix it up with 汤 (tāng, soup): different tone.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ lái qiē cài, nǐ zuòfàn.
examples.english: I'll chop the vegetables, you cook.
Careful, don't cut your hand!

words.tip: For cutting with a knife: 刀 is on the right. Show 切菜 (chop vegetables) and 切水果; slicing fruit for someone is a small everyday way of showing care.

examples.english: I'll do the dishes.
Have you washed your hands?

words.tip: 洗碗 = do the dishes, 洗手 = wash your hands, 洗衣服 = do the laundry. 氵 is the water radical. Agreeing who does 洗碗 is a classic couple's negotiation.

examples.english: This apple is really sweet.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xǐhuan tài tián de dōngxi.
examples.english: I don't like things that are too sweet.

words.tip: 舌 (tongue) on the left. The other tastes: 酸 (suān, sour), 苦 (kǔ, bitter), 辣 (là, spicy). 甜 also describes a sweet smile or a sweet talker (嘴甜).

examples.english: Have you had breakfast?
What do you want for breakfast?

words.tip: Same pattern for every meal: 早饭, 午饭 (lunch), 晚饭 (dinner). 顿 counts meals: 一顿饭. Compare a German breakfast with a Chinese one (粥, 包子, 豆浆).

examples.text: 我每天早上喝一杯牛奶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang hē yì bēi niúnǎi.
examples.english: I drink a glass of milk every morning.

examples.pinyin: Kāfēi li yào jiā niúnǎi ma?
examples.english: Do you want milk in your coffee?

words.tip: Literally 'cow milk'. 杯 for a glass, 瓶 for a bottle. The same 奶 doubled gives 奶奶 (nǎinai), grandma on the father's side.

examples.pinyin: Zǎofàn wǒ chī le liǎng piàn miànbāo.
examples.english: I had two slices of bread for breakfast.

examples.pinyin: Déguó rén hěn ài chī miànbāo.
examples.english: Germans love eating bread.

words.tip: 片 = a slice, 个 = a roll or a loaf. 面 means flour here, as in 面条 (noodles). Bread is a big topic with a German partner!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hē yì wǎn zhōu.
examples.english: I'd like a bowl of congee.

examples.text: 生病的时候我喜欢喝粥。
examples.pinyin: Shēngbìng de shíhou wǒ xǐhuan hē zhōu.
examples.english: When I'm ill I like to have congee.
alternatives: 我生病的时候喜欢喝粥。

words.tip: A classic breakfast and what people eat when they're ill. You 喝 (drink) it rather than 吃. The character is rice 米 between two 弓.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào hē guǒzhī háishi niúnǎi?
examples.english: Would you like juice or milk?

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ zìjǐ zuò de guǒzhī.
examples.english: This is juice I made myself.

words.tip: Name a juice by putting the fruit in front: 苹果汁 = apple juice, 橙汁 (chéngzhī) = orange juice. The same 果 as in 水果.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù chāoshì mǎi diǎn dōngxi.
examples.english: I'm going to the supermarket to get a few things.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lóuxià yǒu yí ge chāoshì.
examples.english: There's a supermarket downstairs from my home.

words.tip: Short for 超级市场, 'super market', just like the English. 市 also means city, as in 城市.

examples.pinyin: Gōngyuán li yǒu hěn duō rén.
examples.english: The park's full of people.
Let's meet at the park entrance.

words.tip: 'Public garden'. Parks are busy early with tai chi (太极拳) and in the evening with 广场舞. Same 园 as in 动物园 (zoo).

examples.english: He's ill and in hospital.
My mum works at a hospital.

words.tip: Same 医 as in 医生. There are few GP practices, so 去医院 often just means going to see a doctor. Watch the tone: 院 yuàn, not 园 yuán.

examples.english: What time does the bank open?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù yínháng huàn qián.
examples.english: I need to go to the bank to change money.

words.tip: 行 is háng here, not xíng as in 旅行. 'Silver firm', as silver was once money; 钅 is the metal radical, as in 钥匙.

examples.english: The post office is next to the bank.
The post office is closed today.

words.tip: 邮 is also in 邮票 (stamp) and 邮件 (mail, email). 局 is an office or bureau, as in 警察局 (police station).

examples.english: Let's take the bus.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zuò gōngjiāochē shàngbān.
examples.english: I take the bus to work every day.

words.tip: 'Public transport vehicle', often shortened to 公交. 公共汽车 means the same. You 坐 a bus, like any transport where you sit.

examples.english: We're taking the train to Shanghai.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan zuò huǒchē lǚxíng ma?
examples.english: Do you like travelling by train?

words.tip: 'Fire vehicle', from the days of steam. 火车站 = train station; the fast trains are 高铁 (gāotiě). 列 is the proper measure for a whole train.

examples.english: I cycle to work.

examples.text: 你的自行车是什么颜色的？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de zìxíngchē shì shénme yánsè de?
examples.english: What colour is your bike?

words.tip: 'Self-going vehicle'. You 骑 (qí, ride astride) a bike or a horse, but 坐 a bus or train. Shared bikes (共享单车) are everywhere in Chinese cities.

examples.english: This metro line goes to the airport.
Taking the metro is faster than driving.

words.tip: 'Ground iron': the underground railway. 条 counts lines, 地铁站 = metro station, and lines are numbered: 几号线? = which line?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng huǒchēpiào.
examples.english: I bought two train tickets.
How much is one cinema ticket?

words.tip: Put the thing in front: 车票, 机票 (plane ticket), 电影票. 张, because tickets are flat. 买票 = buy a ticket.

examples.english: He has long legs.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǒu le hěn duō lù, tuǐ hěn téng.
examples.english: I walked a lot and my legs hurt.

words.tip: 月 on the left here is 肉 (flesh) squeezed: the body-part radical, also in 胳膊 and 脑. 条, because legs are long.

examples.english: My arm hurts.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de gēbo bǐ nǐ de cháng.
examples.english: My arms are longer than yours.

words.tip: 手 is only the hand; the whole arm is 胳膊. Both characters have the flesh radical 月, and the second syllable is said lightly.

examples.english: She's such a sweet talker.
You've got something on your mouth.

words.tip: 口 is the written and radical form, 嘴 the everyday word. 嘴甜 ('sweet mouth') describes someone who always says nice things.

examples.english: He has a high nose bridge.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, bízi bù shūfu.
examples.english: I have a cold and my nose feels stuffy.

words.tip: 自 on top was once a drawing of a nose, which is why people point at their nose to say 'me'. A 'high nose' (鼻子高) is a common compliment.

examples.english: His ears have gone red.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī gǒu de ěrduo hěn cháng.
examples.english: This dog's ears are very long.

words.tip: 耳 is a drawing of an ear. 朵 is also the measure for flowers (一朵花), which comes up later.

examples.english: Where does it hurt?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dùzi téng, bù xiǎng chī fàn.
examples.english: My stomach hurts, I don't feel like eating.

words.tip: Body part + 疼: 头疼 (headache), 肚子疼 (stomach ache). 疒 is the illness radical, as in 病. 痛 (tòng) means the same and is more formal.

examples.english: The child has a temperature.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ fāshāo le, bié qù shàngbān.
examples.english: You have a fever, don't go to work.

words.tip: Literally 'develop burning'. Expect the classic Chinese remedy for almost anything: 多喝热水! (drink lots of hot water).

examples.english: Have you taken your medicine?

examples.pinyin: Zhège yào yì tiān chī sān cì.
examples.english: Take this medicine three times a day.

words.tip: You 吃 (eat) medicine: 吃药, even for liquids. 艹 on top because medicine was made from herbs; 中药 = traditional Chinese medicine.

examples.english: Wishing you good health!
Health matters most.

words.tip: 祝你身体健康 is a standard toast and greeting, especially to older people. Also a noun: 健康最重要 = health comes first.

examples.english: Is there a pharmacy around here?
I'm going to the pharmacy to buy medicine.

words.tip: Medicine + shop, like 书店 (bookshop). 药房 (yàofáng) is also common. Look for the green cross, much like the German Apotheke's red A.

examples.english: You look really pretty today!

examples.pinyin: Tā de zì xiě de hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: Her handwriting is beautiful.

words.tip: Mostly for women, things and places; for a man, say 帅 (shuài, handsome). 亮 alone means bright, as in 月亮.

examples.english: Your child is very clever.
This dog is really clever!

words.tip: 聪 has 耳 (ear): a clever person listens well. 明 is sun 日 + moon 月: bright.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This film is really interesting.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de gōngzuò yǒu yìsi ma?
examples.english: Is your job interesting?

words.tip: Literally 'has meaning'. The opposite is 没意思 (boring). 意思 alone is 'meaning', from 什么意思?

characters.meaning: peaceful (女 under a roof 宀)

examples.english: Please be a bit quieter.

examples.pinyin: Háizi shuì le, jiā li hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: The kids are asleep and the house is quiet.

words.tip: 安 is a woman 女 under a roof 宀: peace. The same 安 as in 晚安. 安静! on its own = quiet, please!

examples.english: This cat is so cute!
This present is so cute!

words.tip: Literally 'lovable'. Used for babies, pets and partners alike. The apostrophe in kě'ài just marks the syllable break.

examples.english: There aren't many people today.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ chī de tài shǎo le.
examples.english: You've eaten too little.

words.tip: The opposite of 多. 少 is amount, 小 is size, and 少 has one stroke more. 很少 + verb = rarely: 我很少喝酒.

examples.english: We're running out of time!
Is this enough food?

words.tip: 够了! = that's enough! It goes before adjectives: 够大 = big enough, the other way round from German groß genug. Watch the tone: gòu, not 狗 gǒu.

examples.english: I prefer winter.
Tomorrow will be even better.

words.tip: Goes before the adjective or verb: 更好 = even better, 更喜欢 = like more, prefer. Read gèng here; in 更新 (update) it's gēng.

examples.english: It's half past three.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ děng le nǐ bàn ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I waited half an hour for you.

words.tip: 三点半 = 3:30, not halb drei as in German! Before a measure word: 半个小时 (half an hour); after it: 一个半小时 (an hour and a half).

examples.english: I speak a little Chinese.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài gěi wǒ yìdiǎnr shíjiān.
examples.english: Please give me a little more time.

words.tip: The 儿 just adds an r-sound, northern style; in the south people say 一点 (yìdiǎn). After an adjective it means 'a bit more': 慢一点儿 = a bit slower.

examples.english: I'm taller than you.
Today is colder than yesterday.

words.tip: Pattern: A 比 B + adjective. Never add 很: not 我比你很高. Use 一点儿 or 多了 to say how much: 我比你高一点儿.

examples.english: I'm just as tired as you.

examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn yīfu yánsè yíyàng.
examples.english: These two pieces of clothing are the same colour.

words.tip: Pattern: A 跟 B 一样 (+ adjective) = A is as … as B. 不一样 = different. 一 becomes yí before the fourth tone of 样.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou.
examples.english: You're my best friend.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuì xiǎng qù nǎge guójiā?
examples.english: Which country do you most want to visit?

words.tip: 最 + adjective makes the superlative: 最好 (best), 最大 (biggest). 最喜欢 = favourite. The same 最 as in 最后.

examples.english: We're almost there.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎng ge rén chàbuduō gāo.
examples.english: The two of us are about the same height.

words.tip: Literally 'differ not much'. Also 'about the same': 这两个差不多. 差不多先生 (Mr Near-Enough) is a famous satire of sloppy 'that'll do' thinking.

examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge cí yǒu shénme qūbié?
examples.english: What's the difference between these two words?
I can't see the difference.

words.tip: The learner's key question: A 和 B 有什么区别? 没有区别 = no difference. The same 别 as in 别难过.

examples.text: 周末我们一起打扫房间吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen yìqǐ dǎsǎo fángjiān ba.
examples.english: Let's clean the room together at the weekend.
alternatives: 我们周末一起打扫房间吧。

examples.english: I need to clean the kitchen today.

words.tip: Two third tones, so it's said dásǎo. Before Chinese New Year families do a 大扫除 (big clean) to sweep out the old year's bad luck.

examples.english: Can you take the rubbish out?
Where does the rubbish go?

words.tip: 扔垃圾 or 倒垃圾 = take out the rubbish. Both characters have 土 (earth). Compare 垃圾分类 (sorting rubbish), something Germany is famous for.

examples.english: My phone's broken.

examples.pinyin: Niúnǎi huài le, bié hē le.
examples.english: The milk has gone off, don't drink it.

words.tip: 坏了 = it's broken, or (for food) it's gone off. The opposite of 好: 坏人 = a bad person. A playful 你好坏! = you're so mean!

examples.english: Can you fix a bike?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de diànnǎo yào xiū yíxià.
examples.english: My computer needs fixing.

words.tip: Often with 好 to show it worked: 修好了 = it's fixed. 修理 (xiūlǐ) is the fuller word; 修 alone is everyday.

examples.english: Your room is so clean!

examples.pinyin: Bǎ shǒu xǐ gānjìng zài chī fàn.
examples.english: Wash your hands properly before eating.

words.tip: 干 is gān (dry) here, not gàn (to do). The second syllable is often said lightly, gānjing. The opposite is 脏 (zāng, dirty).

characters.meaning: to count, to plan (讠 speech radical)

examples.english: What are your plans for next year?
I think this plan is pretty good.

words.tip: Also a verb: 我们计划明年结婚. It sounds a little formal; in conversation 打算 is more common.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ dǎsuàn shénme shíhou huí jiā?
examples.english: When are you planning to go home?
I plan to learn to drive next year.

words.tip: Followed by a verb: 我打算学中文. More casual than 计划. 算 has bamboo ⺮ on top, from counting with bamboo sticks.

examples.text: 下班以后我给你打电话。
examples.pinyin: Xiàbān yǐhòu wǒ gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: I'll call you after work.
Let's talk about it later.

words.tip: On its own it means later on, in future (以后再说 = let's talk about it later); after an action it means 'after'. Don't mix it up with 然后 (and then).

examples.english: I'm coming right now!
The film is about to start.

words.tip: Literally 'on horseback', as fast as a rider. 马上就到 = almost there, though in practice it can mean anything from one minute to twenty!

examples.pinyin: Jiānglái wǒmen xiǎng zhù zài nǎlǐ?
examples.english: Where do we want to live in the future?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiānglái xiǎng zuò shénme gōngzuò?
examples.english: What job do you want to do in the future?

words.tip: 'What is going to come', for life plans and dreams; 以后 covers anything later, even this afternoon.

characters.meaning: to record, to remember (讠 speech radical)

examples.text: 你还记得我们第一次见面吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ hái jìde wǒmen dìyī cì jiànmiàn ma?
examples.english: Do you still remember the first time we met?
Remember to call me!

words.tip: 记得 = still have it in your memory; to memorise is 记住. It also works as a reminder: 记得带钥匙! = remember your keys!

examples.english: Sorry, I forgot.
I forgot to bring my phone.

words.tip: Usually with 了: 我忘了. 亡 (gone) over 心 (heart): gone from the mind. 别忘了 = don't forget.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián bù xǐhuan chī yú.
examples.english: I didn't use to like fish.
Have we met before?

words.tip: The mirror of 以后. On its own it means 'used to' (我以前住在北京); after an action it means 'before' (睡觉以前).

examples.english: I was scared of dogs as a child.
What did you like to play as a child?

words.tip: 'Small time': when I was little. Great for swapping childhood stories. Don't confuse it with 小时 (hour).

examples.pinyin: Zhè cì wǒ fù, shàngcì nǐ fù le.
examples.english: I'll pay this time, you paid last time.
When did we last meet?

words.tip: 上 = previous, 下 = next: 上次, 这次, 下次, just like 上个月. 次 counts times: 三次 = three times.

characters.meaning: to untie, to solve (角 horn + 刀 knife + 牛 ox)

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng gěi wǒ jiěshì yíxià ma?
examples.english: Can you explain it to me?
This is hard to explain.

words.tip: Pattern: 给 + person + 解释. 解 is a knife 刀 cutting an ox 牛 horn 角: taking something apart. 你听我解释! = let me explain!

examples.pinyin: Gěi wǒ jiǎng yí ge gùshi ba.
examples.english: Tell me a story.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng zài jiǎng yí cì ma?
examples.english: Can you say it once more?

words.tip: 讲故事 = tell a story, 讲课 = give a lesson. Close to 说, but 讲 suits telling or explaining something at length. 讠 is the speech radical.

examples.english: What does this word mean?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān xué wǔ ge xīn cí.
examples.english: I learn five new words every day.

words.tip: A word, as opposed to 字 (a single character): 中文 is one 词 made of two 字. 词典 = dictionary. Watch the tone: cí.

examples.english: This sentence is too long.

examples.text: 请用这个词说一个句子。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yòng zhège cí shuō yí ge jùzi.
examples.english: Please make a sentence with this word.

words.tip: 句 is also a measure word: 一句话 = one sentence, a thing said. 造句 (make a sentence with a word) is a classic school exercise.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì shuō jǐ zhǒng yǔyán?
examples.english: How many languages do you speak?
Learning a language takes time.

words.tip: 种 or 门 (a subject of study) count languages. Language names use 语 or 文: 德语 / 德文, 汉语 / 中文. 言 is the full form of the 讠 radical.

examples.pinyin: Xiànzài liǎng diǎn líng wǔ fēn.
examples.english: It's five past two.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de fángjiān hào shì sān líng wǔ.
examples.english: My room number is three-zero-five.

words.tip: A zero inside a number must be said: 105 = 一百零五. Years are read digit by digit: 2008 = 二零零八年. 雨 (rain) sits on top.

examples.english: This book costs a hundred yuan.

examples.text: 我们学校有五百个学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào yǒu wǔbǎi ge xuésheng.
examples.english: Our school has five hundred students.

words.tip: Always say the 一: 一百, never just 百. 一百零一 = 101. Memory trick: 一 on top of 白 (white).

examples.english: The plane ticket is three thousand yuan.
A thousand yuan is too expensive.

words.tip: Big numbers go in 万 (ten thousand): 10,000 is 一万, not 十千. Compare 千 with 干: 千 has a slanted top stroke.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ dìyī cì lái Déguó.
examples.english: This is my first time in Germany.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì dìyī ge dào de.
examples.english: You're the first to arrive.

words.tip: 第 + number makes ordinals: 第二, 第三. 一 keeps its first tone in ordinals. 第一次 = the first time.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī hàomǎ shì duōshao?
examples.english: What's your mobile number?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ huàn le xīn de diànhuà hàomǎ.
examples.english: I've got a new phone number.

words.tip: Phone numbers are read digit by digit, and 一 becomes yāo so it isn't confused with 七: 139 = yāo sān jiǔ.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā pángbiān yǒu yì tiáo hé.
examples.english: There's a river next to our place.

examples.pinyin: Hé li yǒu hěn duō yú.
examples.english: There are lots of fish in the river.

words.tip: 氵 (water) + 可 for the sound. 条, because rivers are long. 莱茵河 = the Rhine, 黄河 = the Yellow River; big rivers are often 江, as in 长江.

examples.english: Let's go for a walk by the lake.

examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān kěyǐ zài hú li yóuyǒng.
examples.english: In summer you can swim in the lake.

words.tip: 湖边 = lakeside, like 海边. The most famous is 西湖 (West Lake) in Hangzhou. Watch hú (lake) vs hé (河, river): both have 氵.

examples.english: I want to go to the seaside.
I've never seen the sea.

words.tip: 海边 = seaside. 上海 literally means 'on the sea'. 氵 (water) + 每 for the sound.

examples.english: This flower is so pretty!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ mǎi le huā.
examples.english: I bought you flowers.

words.tip: 朵 counts single flowers; a bunch is 一束花 (shù). 花 is also the verb 'to spend': 花钱. 艹 on top is the plant radical.

examples.english: Germany has lots of forests.
We're walking in the forest.

words.tip: Count the trees: 木 = tree, 林 = wood, 森 = forest. 片 counts large stretches, like a forest or a field.

examples.pinyin: Shù shang yǒu yì zhī niǎo.
examples.english: There's a bird in the tree.

examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang wǒ tīngdào niǎo zài chànggē.
examples.english: In the morning I heard birds singing.

words.tip: A picture of a bird, also a radical in 鸡 (chicken). Compare 乌 (wū, crow): one stroke less, because you can't see a black crow's eye.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang wǒmen chī yú ba.
examples.english: Let's have fish tonight.
How much is this fish?

words.tip: 条 for long fish. Fish is served at New Year because 鱼 sounds like 余 (surplus): 年年有余 = plenty every year.

examples.english: Can you ride a horse?

examples.pinyin: Nà pǐ mǎ pǎo de hěn kuài.
examples.english: That horse runs very fast.

words.tip: 匹 (pǐ) counts horses. 马 gives the ma sound in 吗 and 妈. The same 马 as in 马上.

examples.english: I was born in the Year of the Pig.
I like eating pork.

words.tip: 属 + animal = your zodiac sign. 犭 is the animal radical, as in 狗 and 猫. 小猪 can be an affectionate pet name between couples.

examples.pinyin: Chúfáng li yǒu yì zhī lǎoshǔ!
examples.english: There's a mouse in the kitchen!
Are you afraid of mice?

words.tip: 老 doesn't mean old here: it's a prefix, as in 老师 and 老虎 (tiger). Two third tones, so it's said láoshǔ. The rat comes first in the zodiac.

examples.english: Let's go and play football!
Pass me the ball!

words.tip: The verb tells you the game: 踢球 (kick: football), 打球 (hit: basketball, tennis and so on). 足球 = football, 篮球 = basketball.

examples.english: We won!
Who do you think will win?

words.tip: A big character built from 亡, 口, 月, 贝 (money) and 凡; children learn it as that list. Write it slowly together. Its opposite is 输.

examples.english: He hates losing.
Our team lost yesterday.

words.tip: Only for games, matches and bets; losing an object is 丢 (diū). It sounds like 书 (book), so gamblers avoid being given books at New Year.

examples.text: 今天晚上有一场足球比赛。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang yǒu yì chǎng zúqiú bǐsài.
examples.english: There's a football match tonight.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn zuótiān de bǐsài le ma?
examples.english: Did you watch yesterday's match?

words.tip: The same 比 as in comparisons: 'compare and compete'. 场 counts matches, like other events (一场婚礼). Also a verb: 我们比赛吧!

examples.english: Which team do you support?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shì yí ge duì de.
examples.english: We're on the same team.

words.tip: 足球队 = football team, 中国队 = Team China. Also a queue: 排队 = to queue up.

characters.meaning: to look into the distance; to hope

examples.english: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
I hope you can come.

words.tip: Followed by a whole clause: 我希望你喜欢. Also a noun, 'hope': 还有希望 = there's still hope.

examples.text: 我昨天晚上做了一个梦。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān wǎnshang zuò le yí ge mèng.
examples.english: I had a dream last night.

examples.pinyin: Nà zhǐ shì yí ge mèng.
examples.english: That was only a dream.

words.tip: You 'do' a dream: 做梦. Two trees 林 over 夕 (evening). 做个好梦 = sweet dreams.

characters.meaning: wish; willing (心 heart at the bottom)

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shēngrì yuànwàng shì shénme?
examples.english: What's your birthday wish?

examples.text: 我的愿望是去中国旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yuànwàng shì qù Zhōngguó lǚxíng.
examples.english: My wish is to travel to China.

words.tip: 许愿 (xǔyuàn) = make a wish, for example before blowing out the birthday candles. The same 望 as in 希望.

examples.english: He might not come.
That's impossible!

words.tip: Before a verb it means 'maybe': 可能会下雨. 不可能! = impossible! It means the same as 也许.

examples.english: You're so lucky!
I'm out of luck today.

words.tip: 运气好 = lucky, 运气不好 = unlucky. 祝你好运 = good luck. The same 运 as in 运动.

characters.meaning: to greet, to meet (辶 walking radical)

examples.english: Welcome to our home!
We all warmly welcome you.

words.tip: 欢迎光临 (welcome) is what shop staff call out as you walk in. 迎 has 辶, the walking radical: going out to meet someone.

examples.english: To our future, cheers!
Come on, cheers!

words.tip: Literally 'dry the cup', so at a formal dinner it can mean finishing your glass. Clinking your glass lower than an elder's shows respect.

examples.english: Good night, sweet dreams!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēn māma shuō le wǎn'ān.
examples.english: I said good night to Mum.

words.tip: Only for going to bed, not as an evening goodbye (that's 再见). The apostrophe in wǎn'ān marks the syllable break.

words.gloss: come on!, you can do it!

examples.english: Come on, you can do it!
Good luck in tomorrow's match!

words.tip: Literally 'add fuel', and it really is what you do at a petrol station. Shouted at sports matches and said before exams, like 'Du schaffst das!'

examples.english: Take care, get home safely!
Thanks for coming, take care!

words.tip: Said by the host to a leaving guest: 'walk slowly'. Hosts often see guests to the door or even the street; the guest can reply 别送了 (no need to see me out).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
examples.english: My older brother is three years older than me.
My older brother works in Beijing.

words.tip: Chinese always says whether a brother or sister is older or younger. The second syllable is light and toneless.
