examples.english: My older sister lives in Shanghai.
I have two older sisters.

words.tip: Low third tone, then a light toneless syllable. Also a friendly way to address a slightly older woman.

examples.english: My younger brother is still at school.
My younger brother is taller than me.

words.tip: Falling tone, then light. 兄弟 (xiōngdì) = brothers, also 'bros' among friends.

examples.english: Your younger sister is really cute.

examples.pinyin: Mèimei hé wǒ zhǎng de hěn xiàng.
examples.english: My little sister and I look alike.

words.tip: Falling tone, then light. 姐妹 (jiěmèi) = sisters. 兄弟姐妹 = brothers and sisters.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng dài nǐ jiàn wǒ fùmǔ.
examples.english: I want to take you to meet my parents.
Are your parents in good health?

words.tip: The formal 'father and mother' in one word. In everyday talk people also say 爸爸妈妈 or 爸妈.

examples.english: Let's go for a coffee.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi kāfēi tài kǔ le.
examples.english: This coffee is too bitter.

words.tip: A loanword that copies the sound of 'coffee'. Both syllables are high and level. 一杯咖啡 = a cup of coffee.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hē yì píng píjiǔ ba.
examples.english: Let's have a bottle of beer.
My dad loves drinking beer.

words.tip: 啤 copies the sound of 'beer', and 酒 says it's alcohol. 青岛啤酒 (Tsingtao) started as a German brewery.

examples.english: I don't drink alcohol.
You can't drink and drive.

words.tip: Any alcoholic drink: 红酒 = red wine, 白酒 = strong Chinese spirit. Sounds the same as 九 (nine).

examples.english: This bottle is empty.
Please pass me the bottle.

words.tip: 瓶 on its own is the measure word: 一瓶水 = a bottle of water. 瓶子 is the bottle itself.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn kě, xiǎng hē shuǐ.
examples.english: I'm thirsty and want some water.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kě le jiù hē diǎn shuǐ.
examples.english: If you're thirsty, have some water.

words.tip: The left side 氵 is the water radical. Compare 喝 (hē, to drink) with a mouth 口 on the left: easy to mix up.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ è le, wǒmen chī fàn ba.
examples.english: I'm hungry, let's eat.
Are you hungry?

words.tip: A short falling 'uh'. Usually with 了: 我饿了 = I've got hungry. 饿死了 = I'm starving.

examples.english: I'm full.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tài bǎo le, chī bu xià le.
examples.english: I'm too full, I can't eat any more.

words.tip: Almost always as 吃饱了, 'eaten to fullness'. The polite thing to say when a host keeps offering more.

examples.english: Let's have lunch together.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān méi shíjiān chī wǔfàn.
examples.english: I don't have time for lunch today.

words.tip: Same pattern as 早饭 (breakfast) and 晚饭 (dinner). Also called 午餐 (wǔcān) on menus.

examples.english: After dinner we'll go for a walk.
What time are we having dinner?

words.tip: 晚 (evening) + 饭 (meal). 吃晚饭 = to have dinner. Usually the main family meal.

examples.pinyin: Zhège cài de wèidào hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This dish tastes very good.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan kāfēi de wèidào.
examples.english: I really like the smell of coffee.

words.tip: Covers both taste and smell. 味道怎么样？ = how does it taste? The second syllable is often said lightly.

examples.english: Our bedroom is quiet.
The bedroom is upstairs.

words.tip: Two falling tones. 室 is the formal word for a room: 教室 = classroom, 办公室 = office.

examples.english: Excuse me, where is the toilet?
I'm just going to the toilet.

words.tip: Literally 'wash-hands room', the polite word in restaurants and shops. 厕所 (cèsuǒ) is blunter.

examples.english: The sofa is in the living room.
We watch TV in the living room.

words.tip: Literally 'guest hall': the room where you receive visitors.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen jiā yǒu yí ge xiǎo huāyuán.
examples.english: Their home has a small garden.

examples.pinyin: Huāyuán li de huā dōu kāi le.
examples.english: The flowers in the garden are all in bloom.

words.tip: 'Flower park'. 园 is the same character as in 公园 (park). Few city homes in China have one.

examples.english: We live on the fifth floor.
Which floor do you live on?

words.tip: Number + 楼 is the floor: 三楼 = third floor. The ground floor is 一楼, so Chinese floors are one higher than German ones. 一座楼 = a building.

words.gloss: to open; to turn on; to drive

examples.english: Please open the window.
Can you drive?

words.tip: One verb for doors, lights, machines and cars: 开门, 开灯, 开车. Also in 开始 (begin) and 开心 (happy).

examples.english: Please turn off the light before sleeping.
Please close the door.

words.tip: The opposite of 开: 关门, 关灯, 关手机. Also in 没关系 (it doesn't matter).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài zhǎo wǒ de yàoshi.
examples.english: I'm looking for my keys.
Someone's looking for you.

words.tip: Looking, not yet finding: found is 找到 (zhǎodào). 我找你 can also mean 'I'm coming to see you'.

examples.pinyin: Bǎ shū fàng zài zhuōzi shang ba.
examples.english: Put the book on the table.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ yàoshi fàng zài nǎlǐ le?
examples.english: Where did you put the keys?

words.tip: Usually 放在 + place. Also 'to let go': 放假 = to have a holiday, 放心 = don't worry (put your heart down).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ yòng nǐ de shǒujī ma?
examples.english: May I use your phone?
This phone is really easy to use.

words.tip: Also 'with' for tools: 用筷子吃 = eat with chopsticks. 不用 = no need; 不用谢 = you're welcome.

examples.english: Let's walk to the park.
He has already left.

words.tip: 走路 = to go on foot. On its own it often means to leave: 我走了 = I'm off. 走吧！ = let's go!

examples.english: He goes running every morning.
I can't run any more.

words.tip: 跑步 = to go running, as exercise. The left side 足 is the foot radical.

examples.english: Don't stand in the doorway.
Please stand up.

words.tip: The same character as in 车站 (station): a place where you stand and wait. 站起来 = stand up.

examples.english: In summer we go swimming at the seaside.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi ge xīngqī yóuyǒng liǎng cì.
examples.english: I swim twice a week.

words.tip: Both characters have the water radical 氵. 游泳池 (yóuyǒngchí) = swimming pool. 我不会游泳 = I can't swim.

examples.text: 我想在沙发上躺一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zài shāfā shang tǎng yíhuìr.
examples.english: I want to lie on the sofa for a while.

examples.pinyin: Tā tǎng zài chuáng shang kàn shū.
examples.english: He's lying in bed reading.

words.tip: The left side 身 means body. 躺下 = to lie down. Low third tone, unlike 糖 (táng, sugar) and 汤 (tāng, soup).

examples.english: Your hair is long.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen děng le hěn cháng shíjiān.
examples.english: We waited a long time.

words.tip: For length and time: 很长时间 = a long time. The same character read zhǎng means 'to grow'.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi tài duǎn le.
examples.english: These trousers are too short.
Winter days are short.

words.tip: Short in length or time, not height: a short person is 矮 (ǎi). 短信 = text message ('short letter').

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de xíngli zhòng bu zhòng?
examples.english: Is your luggage heavy?

examples.text: 这个包太重了，我拿不动。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bāo tài zhòng le, wǒ ná bu dòng.
examples.english: This bag is too heavy, I can't carry it.

words.tip: Also 'serious' and, in 重要, 'important'. The same character read chóng means 'again'.

examples.english: This computer is very light.
Please close the door a bit more gently.

words.tip: High level tone. Also 'gentle, soft': 轻一点 = more gently. 年轻 (niánqīng) = young.

examples.english: The cup is already full.

examples.pinyin: Fànguǎn li zuò mǎn le rén.
examples.english: The restaurant is packed with people.

words.tip: For containers and places. Full after eating is 饱. 满意 (mǎnyì) = satisfied. Low third tone, unlike 慢 (màn, slow).

examples.english: What colour do you like best?

examples.pinyin: Zhège yánsè wǒ bú tài xǐhuan.
examples.english: I don't really like this colour.

words.tip: 色 alone is the ending that turns a colour word into a noun: 红色, 蓝色, 黄色.

examples.english: In autumn the leaves turn yellow.
Bananas are yellow.

words.tip: The colour of the Yellow River (黄河) and once the emperor's colour. Also a common family name.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānkōng shì huīsè de.
examples.english: The sky is grey today.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yì shuāng huīsè de xié.
examples.english: I want to buy a pair of grey shoes.

words.tip: Literally 'ash': the bottom of the character is fire 火. As a noun the colour is 灰色.

examples.english: She likes purple flowers.
You look good in purple.

words.tip: The z is like 'ds' in 'kids', with a buzzing vowel, low third tone. 紫色 is the noun.

examples.text: 她穿了一件粉红色的衣服。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān le yí jiàn fěnhóngsè de yīfu.
examples.english: She wore a pink top.

examples.pinyin: Zhè duǒ huā shì fěnhóngsè de.
examples.english: This flower is pink.

words.tip: 'Powder red'. Also said 粉色 or 粉红色. 粉 alone also means noodles made from rice or beans.

examples.english: Don't be angry any more, OK?

examples.pinyin: Tā yì shēngqì jiù bù shuōhuà.
examples.english: As soon as he gets angry he stops talking.

words.tip: Literally 'to produce air'. Angry at someone: 生你的气 = angry with you, the person goes in the middle.

examples.text: 要见你父母，我有点紧张。
examples.pinyin: Yào jiàn nǐ fùmǔ, wǒ yǒudiǎn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: I'm a bit nervous about meeting your parents.
Don't be nervous, take your time.

words.tip: 'Tight and stretched'. 别紧张 = don't be nervous, relax.

examples.english: This film is so boring.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yí ge rén zài jiā hěn wúliáo.
examples.english: I'm bored at home on my own.

words.tip: Memory hook: 'nothing to chat about' (originally 聊 here meant 'something to lean on'). Works for the person and the thing: 我很无聊 = I'm bored. Two rising tones.

examples.english: Don't worry, no problem.
Mum is very worried about you.

words.tip: 'To carry your heart'. Takes the person directly: 我担心你 = I'm worried about you. Opposite: 放心.

examples.pinyin: Hé nǐ zài yìqǐ wǒ hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: I'm happy when I'm with you.
Did you have fun today?

words.tip: 'Open heart'. More casual than 高兴, and more about having a good time. 玩得开心！ = have fun!

examples.english: I'm still at the office.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de bàngōngshì zài sān lóu.
examples.english: My office is on the third floor.

words.tip: 'Handle-business room'. 办公 = to do office work. The company as a whole is 公司.

examples.english: He's my colleague.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xīn tóngshì shì Déguó rén.
examples.english: My new colleague is German.

words.tip: 'Same work'. 同 builds many 'fellow' words: 同学 = classmate, 同意 = to agree.

examples.english: Our boss is a nice person.
The boss isn't in today.

words.tip: Two third tones, so the first one rises: láobǎn. Also how you call the owner in a small shop or restaurant.

examples.english: I have a meeting this afternoon.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài kāihuì, bù néng jiē diànhuà.
examples.english: He's in a meeting and can't take the call.

words.tip: Verb + object: 开 (hold) + 会 (meeting). It can be split: 开一个会 = to hold a meeting.

words.gloss: to rest, to take a break

examples.pinyin: Nǐ lèi le, xiūxi yíxià ba.
examples.english: You're tired, have a rest.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zài jiā xiūxi yì tiān.
examples.english: I want to rest at home for a day.

words.tip: 休 is a person 亻 leaning on a tree 木. 好好休息 = rest well, said to someone who is ill or tired.

examples.english: Please wait ten minutes for me.

examples.pinyin: Zǒulù qù zhǐ yào wǔ fēnzhōng.
examples.english: It's only five minutes on foot.

words.tip: A length of time, with no measure word: 五分钟. For clock time just 分: 三点十分 = ten past three.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān gōngzuò bā ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I work eight hours a day.

examples.pinyin: Zuò huǒchē yào liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: It takes two hours by train.

words.tip: A length of time; clock time is 点. 个 is optional: 两小时 or 两个小时. 半个小时 = half an hour.

examples.pinyin: Zhōngwǔ wǒmen yìqǐ chī fàn ba.
examples.english: Let's eat together at noon.
I'm not coming home at midday.

words.tip: 'Middle noon', roughly 11 to 1. Time words go before the verb, with no 'at'.

examples.english: See you at three in the afternoon.
Are you free this afternoon?

words.tip: 'After noon'. It comes before the clock time: 下午三点 = 3 pm. 下午好 = good afternoon.

examples.english: I have class in the morning.
I went to the supermarket this morning.

words.tip: 'Before noon': the working morning, roughly 8 to 12. 早上 is the early morning.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù tóngyì nǐ shuō de.
examples.english: I don't agree with what you said.
My parents agree to us getting married.

words.tip: 'Same idea'. Takes the person or idea directly, with no 'with': 我同意你.

examples.english: Family is very important to me.
This matter is very important.

words.tip: 'Heavy and needed'. Important to someone = 对…很重要. Two falling tones.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge hǎo zhǔyi!
examples.english: That's a good idea!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bu chū hǎo zhǔyi.
examples.english: I can't think of a good idea.

words.tip: 好主意！ on its own = good idea! Many speakers say zhúyi. Don't mix it up with 注意 (zhùyì, to pay attention).

examples.english: What's your opinion?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tīngting nǐ de yìjiàn.
examples.english: I'd like to hear your opinion.

words.tip: Careful: 我对他有意见 means 'I have a problem with him'. 我没意见 = fine by me.

examples.english: This taste is a bit strange.
How strange, why is the door open?

words.tip: 真奇怪！ = how odd! Rising tone, then falling.

examples.english: It's very windy today.

examples.pinyin: Fēng tài dà le, guān shang chuānghu ba.
examples.english: It's too windy, let's close the window.

words.tip: Wind is 'big' or 'small' in Chinese, not strong: 风很大. 刮风 (guā fēng) = the wind is blowing.

examples.english: It's snowing outside.
Children love playing in the snow.

words.tip: 下雪 = to snow, like 下雨. The top 雨 is the rain radical, also in 雷 (thunder) and 零 (zero). 一场雪 = a snowfall.

examples.english: There are no clouds in the sky.
It's very cloudy today.

words.tip: The ü sound after y: lips rounded as for 'oo', tongue as for 'ee'. 多云 = cloudy, in forecasts.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang de yuèliang hěn yuán.
examples.english: The moon is very round tonight.
Look, the moon has come out!

words.tip: 'Bright moon'. The full moon means family reunion: Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节) is a good thing to talk about.

examples.pinyin: Tiān shang yǒu hěn duō xīngxing.
examples.english: There are lots of stars in the sky.

examples.pinyin: Chéngshì li kàn bu dào xīngxing.
examples.english: You can't see the stars in the city.

words.tip: The same 星 as in 星期 (week). A film star is 明星 (míngxīng), a 'bright star'.

examples.english: Let's watch TV tonight.

examples.pinyin: Diànshì tài chǎo le, guān le ba.
examples.english: The TV is too loud, turn it off.

words.tip: 'Electric vision', like 电脑 (electric brain) and 电话 (electric speech). 看电视 = to watch TV.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba měi tiān kàn bàozhǐ.
examples.english: My dad reads the newspaper every day.

examples.pinyin: Xiànzài hěn shǎo yǒu rén kàn bàozhǐ.
examples.english: Few people read newspapers nowadays.

words.tip: 'Report paper'. You 看 (look at) a newspaper rather than 读 it. 一张纸 = a sheet of paper.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan tīng nǐ jiǎng gùshi.
examples.english: I like listening to you tell stories.

examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi shì zhēn de ma?
examples.english: Is this story true?

words.tip: 'Past events'. You 讲 (tell) a story: 讲故事. The second syllable is light.

examples.english: This song is lovely.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì chàng zhè shǒu gē ma?
examples.english: Can you sing this song?

words.tip: The noun inside 唱歌 (to sing). Sounds the same as 哥 (older brother). Songs and poems are counted with 首.

examples.pinyin: Qiáng shang yǒu yì fú huà.
examples.english: There's a painting on the wall.
You draw really well!

words.tip: Noun and verb in one: 画画 = to draw pictures. Falling tone, unlike 花 (huā, flower). 话 (huà, speech) sounds exactly the same but is written differently.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì yíxià zhè jiàn yīfu.
examples.english: Try this piece of clothing on.
Let me try!

words.tip: Usually softened: 试一下 or 试试 = have a try. Sounds the same as 是. 考试 (kǎoshì) = exam.

examples.english: We've decided to get married next year.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì nǐ zìjǐ de juédìng.
examples.english: This is your own decision.

words.tip: The ü sound again after j. Also a noun: 做决定 = to make a decision.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xuǎn yí ge diànyǐng ba.
examples.english: You choose a film.

examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge dōu hǎo, hěn nán xuǎn.
examples.english: Both are good, it's hard to choose.

words.tip: The u here is ü (always after x, j, q). The fuller word is 选择 (xuǎnzé).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng huàn yí ge gōngzuò.
examples.english: I want to change jobs.
I'm going to get changed.

words.tip: Swapping one thing for another: 换衣服 = change clothes, 换钱 = change money, 换车 = change trains.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de gōngzuò hái méi wánchéng.
examples.english: My work isn't finished yet.
When can you get it finished?

words.tip: For tasks and work. 完 alone goes after a verb for 'finished doing': 吃完了 = finished eating.

examples.english: We have guests at home today.
What time are the guests coming?

words.tip: Hosts in China keep filling a guest's bowl and cup. Often said with a light second syllable: kèren.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yāoqǐng nǐ lái wǒ jiā.
examples.english: I'd like to invite you to my home.
Thank you for the invitation!

words.tip: The formal word. In everyday talk 请 alone does the job: 我请你吃饭 = dinner is on me.

examples.text: 我来介绍一下我的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lái jièshào yíxià wǒ de péngyou.
examples.english: Let me introduce my friend.
Please introduce yourself.

words.tip: 我来介绍一下 is the set opening. 自我介绍 = to introduce yourself. Two falling tones.

examples.english: You're too kind!
Don't be polite, eat some more.

words.tip: 'Guest manner'. 不客气 = you're welcome. 别客气 = make yourself at home, no need to be formal.

examples.english: Our neighbours are quiet.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de línjū yǒu yì zhī gǒu.
examples.english: Our neighbours have a dog.

words.tip: The u is ü after j. A proverb: 远亲不如近邻, a near neighbour beats a distant relative.

examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù zài jiā.
examples.english: If it rains, we'll stay home.

examples.text: 如果你不想去，也没关系。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ bù xiǎng qù, yě méi guānxi.
examples.english: If you don't want to go, that's fine too.

words.tip: Usually paired with 就 (then) in the second half. In speech 要是 (yàoshi) is a common alternative.

examples.text: 虽然很累，但是我很开心。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì wǒ hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: Although I'm tired, I'm happy.

examples.text: 这件衣服虽然贵，但是很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu suīrán guì, dànshì hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: Although this piece of clothing is expensive, it's very pretty.

words.tip: Chinese says both halves: 虽然…但是…, 'although… but…'. Leaving out 但是 sounds unfinished.

examples.text: 这个菜好吃，而且很便宜。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cài hǎochī, érqiě hěn piányi.
examples.english: This dish is tasty, and cheap too.

examples.text: 他会说中文，而且说得很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā huì shuō Zhōngwén, érqiě shuō de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He can speak Chinese, and speaks it well too.

words.tip: Adds a second point in the same direction. The full pattern is 不但…而且… = not only… but also…

examples.text: 我们坐地铁或者公交车去。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò dìtiě huòzhě gōngjiāochē qù.
examples.english: We'll go by underground or bus.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ hē chá huòzhě kāfēi.
examples.english: You can have tea or coffee.

words.tip: Two words for 'or': 或者 in statements, 还是 in questions. Mixing them up is the classic learner slip.

examples.text: 我想去，不过今天太累了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, búguò jīntiān tài lèi le.
examples.english: I'd like to go, but I'm too tired today.

examples.text: 这个房间很小，不过很干净。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān hěn xiǎo, búguò hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: This room is small, but it's clean.

words.tip: A softer, more conversational 'but' than 但是. 不 is said bú here because a falling tone follows.

examples.english: Why are you learning Chinese?

examples.text: 为什么今天商店不开门？
examples.english: Why aren't the shops open today?
alternatives: 今天商店为什么不开门？

words.tip: Literally 'for what'. It usually goes after the subject (你为什么…), but it can also start the sentence, as in the second example. The answer begins with 因为.

examples.english: Which colour do you like?
Which one is yours?

words.tip: 哪 + measure word. Low third tone: with a falling tone it becomes 那个, 'that one'. Many people say něige.

words.gloss: how many (up to about ten); a few

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ ge fángjiān?
examples.english: How many rooms does your home have?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zài zhèlǐ zhù jǐ tiān.
examples.english: I'd like to stay here for a few days.

words.tip: For small numbers, and always with a measure word: 几个, 几点, 几岁. For bigger numbers use 多少.

examples.english: What's the weather like today?
How about eating together tomorrow?

words.tip: Asks for a description or an opinion, and comes last. Also for suggestions: 明天怎么样？ = how about tomorrow?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xué Zhōngwén xué le duōjiǔ?
examples.english: How long have you been learning Chinese?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào zài Zhōngguó zhù duōjiǔ?
examples.english: How long are you going to stay in China?

words.tip: 多 + adjective asks 'how…': 多久 (how long), 多大 (how old), 多远 (how far). It goes after the verb.

examples.english: Quick, call the police!

examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá lái le, méi shì le.
examples.english: The police are here, it's all right now.

words.tip: The emergency number in China is 110 (yāo yāo líng): on the phone, one is said yāo, not yī.

examples.english: It's dangerous here at night.
Looking at your phone while driving is dangerous.

words.tip: On warning signs everywhere. Many Taiwanese speakers say wéixiǎn with a rising first tone.

examples.english: Take care on the way!
Careful, there's water on the floor!

words.tip: 'Small heart'. 小心！ alone = watch out! 路上小心 is what you say to someone setting off.

examples.english: This city is very safe.

examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang yí ge rén zǒu ānquán ma?
examples.english: Is it safe to walk alone at night?

words.tip: 安 is a woman 女 under a roof 宀: peace at home. The u in quán is ü.

examples.english: Help! Is anyone there?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīngdào yǒu rén hǎn jiùmìng.
examples.english: I heard someone shouting for help.

words.tip: Literally 'save life': only for real emergencies. Everyday help is 帮: 请帮帮我. Two sharp falling tones.

examples.english: We rarely argue.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng gēn nǐ chǎojià.
examples.english: I don't want to argue with you.

words.tip: Verb + object, so the person needs 跟: 我跟他吵架了 = I had a row with him. 吵 alone also means noisy.

examples.english: I should apologise to you.
You don't need to apologise.

words.tip: 'To say sorry'. The person comes before the verb with 向 or 跟: 向你道歉. Two falling tones.

examples.english: Please forgive me, OK?
I've already forgiven you.

words.tip: Takes the person directly: 原谅我. Stronger and more serious than 没关系.

examples.english: This is a misunderstanding.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ wùhuì wǒ de yìsi le.
examples.english: You've misunderstood what I meant.

words.tip: Also a verb: 你误会我了 = you've got me wrong. A good word for calming an argument.

examples.english: I promise I won't be late tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàng nǐ bǎozhèng, zhè shì zhēn de.
examples.english: I promise you, it's true.

words.tip: A firm promise that something will happen. 我保证！ = I promise! Agreeing to a request is 答应 (dāying).

examples.english: There's no milk left at home.
What's in the cup?

words.tip: Comes after the noun, like 上 and 下: 房间里 = in the room, and it's usually toneless there (li). Not used after place names: 在北京, never 在北京里. 里面 is the fuller form.

examples.english: It's cold outside.
The children are playing outside.

words.tip: Its opposite is 里面 (inside). At the start of a sentence it sets the scene: 外面下雨了. 外 also gives 外国 (abroad) and 外卖 (takeaway).

examples.english: The station is just ahead.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ qiánmiàn de rén shì shéi?
examples.english: Who's the person in front of you?

words.tip: Pattern: A 在 B 前面 = A is in front of B. 前 is also 'before' in time (以前): in Chinese the past lies in front.

examples.english: The cat is behind the sofa.

examples.pinyin: Hòumiàn hái yǒu liǎng ge rén.
examples.english: There are two more people at the back.

words.tip: The mirror of 前面: 房子后面 = behind the house. 后 is 'after' in time (以后). Sit one behind the other and practise: 我在你后面.

examples.english: I'll sit between you two.
The one in the middle is my younger sister.

words.tip: Between A and B: 在 A 和 B 中间. 中 is a line through the middle of a target, the same 中 as in 中国, the 'Middle Country'.

examples.english: How many countries have you been to?
This country is very big.

words.tip: Country + home. 国 alone is the building block in names: 中国, 德国, 法国 (France), 美国 (USA). Ask each other: 你想去哪个国家?

examples.text: 我想去中国看你的家人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Zhōngguó kàn nǐ de jiārén.
examples.english: I want to go to China to see your family.
Chinese food is delicious.

words.tip: The 'Middle Country'. Add 人 for the people (中国人) and 菜 for the food (中国菜). Capital letter in pinyin, as for all place names.

examples.text: 德国有很多好喝的啤酒。
examples.pinyin: Déguó yǒu hěn duō hǎohē de píjiǔ.
examples.english: Germany has lots of good beer.
My boyfriend is German.

words.tip: 德 was picked for its sound (from 'Deutsch') and its flattering meaning, virtue. The language is 德语 (Déyǔ) or 德文. Have your partner say where they're from: 我是德国人.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de Zhōngwén míngzi shì shénme?
examples.english: What's your Chinese name?

examples.text: 我每天学一个小时中文。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān xué yí ge xiǎoshí Zhōngwén.
examples.english: I study Chinese for an hour every day.
alternatives: 每天我学一个小时中文。

words.tip: 中文 is the everyday word; textbooks say 汉语 (Hànyǔ), and 普通话 (Pǔtōnghuà) is standard Mandarin as opposed to the dialects.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu hěn duō wàiguó péngyou.
examples.english: I have lots of foreign friends.
Have you ever lived abroad?

words.tip: 'Outside country'. 外国人 = foreigner; the casual 老外 (lǎowài) is what your partner will hear in China, usually meant kindly. Going abroad is 出国.

examples.english: Would you like anything else?
Let's go somewhere else.

words.tip: Before a noun: 别的东西 = other things. Alone: 还要别的吗? = anything else?, the question every waiter asks. 别 by itself also means 'don't': 别走!

examples.pinyin: Suǒyǒu de rén dōu lái le.
examples.english: Everyone has come.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan nǐ zuò de suǒyǒu cài.
examples.english: I like all the dishes you make.

words.tip: Goes before the noun, usually with 的, and 都 follows before the verb: 所有的…都… Two third tones, so the first one rises in speech: suóyǒu.

examples.english: Don't tell anyone else.
What other people think doesn't matter.

words.tip: Everyone except yourself (or the two of you). The first example uses both meanings of 别: 'don't' and 'other'. Often said with a light second syllable: biéren.

examples.english: I bought some fruit.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yìxiē wèntí xiǎng wèn nǐ.
examples.english: I have a few questions I'd like to ask you.

words.tip: An unspecified amount, with no measure word needed: 一些书, 一些人. 些 also makes the plurals of this and that: 这些 (these), 那些 (those).

examples.english: Some people don't eat meat.

examples.pinyin: Yǒude hěn guì, yǒude hěn piányi.
examples.english: Some are expensive, some are cheap.

words.tip: Used at the start of a sentence, often in pairs: 有的…有的… = some…, others… It can't follow the verb: for 'I bought some' use 一些.

examples.english: I'd like a bowl of rice.
Are you having rice or noodles?

words.tip: 米 is the raw grain, 饭 the cooked meal; together they mean plain steamed rice, as opposed to noodles. In restaurants you order it by the bowl.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò de miàntiáo hǎochī ma?
examples.english: Are the noodles I made tasty?
On your birthday you should eat noodles.

words.tip: Often just 面: 牛肉面 = beef noodles. Long noodles stand for a long life, so they're eaten on birthdays. Roughly, the north eats noodles and the south eats rice.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de tāng shì wǒ zuò de.
examples.english: I made today's soup.
The soup is hot, drink it slowly.

words.tip: You drink soup in Chinese: 喝汤. It often comes at the end of the meal. First tone; 糖 (táng, sugar) rises. 氵 is the water radical.

examples.english: Let's make dumplings together.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā de jiǎozi zuì hǎochī.
examples.english: This place has the best dumplings.

words.tip: The Chinese New Year food of the north, made together as a family: 包饺子, 'to wrap dumplings'. Boiled ones are 水饺; fried ones are 锅贴. They're dipped in vinegar, 醋.

examples.english: Have you ever had mapo tofu?

examples.pinyin: Dòufu hěn piányi, yě hěn jiànkāng.
examples.english: Tofu is cheap and healthy too.

words.tip: The second syllable is toneless: dòufu. German Tofu comes from this word by way of Japanese. As slang, 吃豆腐 means to take liberties with someone, to flirt in a handsy way, so teach it with a wink.

examples.english: This restaurant is pretty good.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò de cài zhēn búcuò!
examples.english: Your cooking is really good!

words.tip: Literally 'not wrong', but it's real praise. German nicht schlecht works the same way. 不 changes to bú before a fourth tone.

examples.english: You're great!
That idea is fantastic!

words.tip: Spoken praise, especially 太棒了! and 你真棒! The character literally means 'stick'. Say it every time your partner gets a tone right.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de Zhōngwén hái hěn chà.
examples.english: My Chinese is still very poor.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā fànguǎn de fúwù hěn chà.
examples.english: The service in this restaurant is bad.

words.tip: For a low level or quality; 坏 is broken or wicked. Also 'lacking': 差五分三点 = five to three. It's the 差 inside 差不多 (almost).

examples.english: Your mum looks so young!
We're still young.

words.tip: 'Light in years'. For adults; a small child is 小. 年轻人 = young people. Telling someone their mother looks 年轻 always goes down well.

examples.text: 你会说三种语言，真厉害！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì shuō sān zhǒng yǔyán, zhēn lìhai!
examples.english: You speak three languages, that's amazing!
My mum is a fantastic cook.

words.tip: The all-purpose 'wow, you're good'. It also means severe: 疼得很厉害 = it hurts badly. The second syllable is toneless.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì cóng nǎlǐ lái de?
examples.english: Where have you come from?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng bā diǎn gōngzuò dào wǔ diǎn.
examples.english: I work from eight to five.

words.tip: A starting point in place or time, and the phrase goes before the verb: 从德国来. 从…到… = from…to… The character is two people (人人), one following the other.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí gōngsī hěn jìn.
examples.english: My home is close to the office.
Is it far from here to the station?

words.tip: Only for distance: A 离 B 很近 / 很远. No 是 and no 从 in this pattern. Second tone; 里 (lǐ, inside) dips.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ gēn wǒ yìqǐ qù ba.
examples.english: Come along with me.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ shuō yí jiàn shì.
examples.english: I'd like to tell you something.

words.tip: 'With' a person, and it goes before the verb: 跟朋友吃饭. More colloquial than 和. Literally 'heel, to follow' (足 is the foot radical): 跟我来 = follow me.

examples.english: Which way do we go?
Look to your left!

words.tip: A direction, placed before the verb: 往左, 往右, 往前. You'll hear it in taxis and on the metro. Third tone; 忘 (wàng, to forget) falls.

examples.english: For you, I'm learning Chinese.

examples.text: 我这么做都是为了我们。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhème zuò dōu shì wèile wǒmen.
examples.english: I'm doing all this for us.

words.tip: States the purpose, or the person something is done for, usually at the start of the sentence. Not for giving things: 'a present for you' is 给你的礼物.

examples.english: My feet are cold.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de jiǎo bǐ wǒ de dà.
examples.english: Your feet are bigger than mine.

words.tip: One foot is 一只脚, a pair 一双脚. 月 on the left is the 'flesh' radical found in many body parts: 腿, 脸, 肚, 背. Foot massage (足疗) is big in China.

examples.english: The child's fingers are tiny.
I've cut my finger.

words.tip: 手 hand + 指 to point. Show how Chinese people count to ten on one hand: the signs for six to ten are worth learning. Toes are 脚趾.

examples.pinyin: Zuò le yì tiān, wǒ de bèi hěn téng.
examples.english: After sitting all day, my back really hurts.

examples.pinyin: Bāng wǒ kànkan wǒ de bèi.
examples.english: Have a look at my back for me.

words.tip: Fourth tone for the body part. With a first tone (bēi) it's a verb, to carry on your back, as in 背包 (backpack). 月 at the bottom is the flesh radical.

examples.english: I'm hungry.
What's wrong with your stomach?

words.tip: Hunger and stomach aches both live here: 肚子饿, 肚子疼, and 拉肚子 (to have diarrhoea), a useful travel word.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de liǎn zěnme zhème hóng?
examples.english: Why is your face so red?
I'm going to wash my face.

words.tip: Counted with 张, like other flat things. Losing face, 丢脸 (diūliǎn), matters socially: a good culture topic. 洗脸 = to wash your face.

examples.english: I'm going to see a doctor tomorrow.
Is it expensive to see a doctor in Germany?

words.tip: Literally 'look at the illness'. Confusingly, both the patient and the doctor can 看病. In China you go straight to a hospital rather than a family doctor. Also 看医生.

examples.english: How long have you had this cough?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ wǎnshang késou, shuì bu hǎo.
examples.english: I cough at night and can't sleep well.

words.tip: Both characters have the mouth radical 口. The second syllable is toneless. Also a noun. Expect the advice 多喝热水 (drink lots of hot water).

words.gloss: to have a cold; a cold

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, bù néng qù shàngbān.
examples.english: I've got a cold and can't go to work.
Take care not to catch a cold.

words.tip: A verb in Chinese: 我感冒了 = I've caught a cold. Cold weather gets the blame, so expect to be told to dress warmly: 多穿点儿!

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng yào jiǎnchá nǐ de yǎnjing.
examples.english: The doctor wants to examine your eyes.
Check the passports once more.

words.tip: For doctors, homework and luggage alike. 做检查 = to have tests done. A yearly 体检 (health check) is standard in Chinese companies.

examples.english: To see a doctor you have to register first.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bāng wǒ guàhào, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Could you register for me?

words.tip: The first step in any Chinese hospital: you 'hang up a number' for a department and pay a small fee before you see a doctor. Today it's mostly done by app. Walk your partner through the whole process.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yì kē yá téng.
examples.english: One of my teeth hurts.
Your teeth are so white!

words.tip: Also 牙齿 (yáchǐ). Counted with 颗, like other small, roundish things. 刷牙 = to brush your teeth, 牙疼 = toothache.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan nǐ de cháng tóufa.
examples.english: I like your long hair.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān bù xiǎng xǐ tóufa.
examples.english: I don't feel like washing my hair today.

words.tip: Only the hair on your head; body hair and fur are 毛. One strand is 一根头发. 发 is fà when it means hair (fā = to send), and toneless in this word: tóufa.

examples.english: I want to go and get a haircut.
Where do you get your hair cut?

words.tip: 'Put the hair in order'. The shop is a 理发店. It's verb + object, so extras go in between: 理一次发. For women's styling people also say 做头发.

examples.english: I'm really scared of going to the dentist.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi hǎo de yáyī ma?
examples.english: Do you know a good dentist?

words.tip: 牙 + 医, as in 医生. 看牙医 = to go to the dentist. Compare what a visit costs, and who pays, in each country.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiǎn tóufa le? Zhēn hǎokàn!
examples.english: You've had a haircut? It looks great!
Don't cut it too short.

words.tip: Cutting with scissors (剪刀): hair, nails, paper. Cutting with a knife is 切. The 刀 at the bottom of the character is a knife.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ yǒu shí kuài qián.
examples.english: I only have ten yuan.
We're only going for three days.

words.tip: Goes before the verb, never straight before a noun: 我只喝茶. Third tone. Read zhī, the same character is the measure word for animals: 一只猫.

examples.english: Have a bit more!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān zài gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: I'll call you again tomorrow.

words.tip: 'Again' for things that haven't happened yet; the same 再 as in 再见 (see you again). Also 'and then': 吃了饭再走. Sounds exactly like 在.

examples.english: You're late again!
It's raining again today.

words.tip: 'Again' looking back, often with a sigh. Contrast with 再: 再来 (come again, future) and 又来了 (here again, it's happened). 又…又… = both…and…: 又好吃又便宜.

examples.english: They all like you.

examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng běn shū wǒ dōu kànguo.
examples.english: I've read both of these books.

words.tip: Sums up whatever comes before it and goes before the verb: 我们都去. There's no separate word for 'both'. 都不 = none, 不都 = not all. Read dū, the same character means capital city (首都).

examples.english: It's really cold today!

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhēn de bú qù ma?
examples.english: Are you really not going?

words.tip: For exclamations: 真好吃! Stronger and more personal than 很. 真的 = real, really; 真的吗? = really? Not used in neutral descriptions before a noun.

examples.english: Can you use chopsticks?

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài gěi wǒ yì shuāng kuàizi.
examples.english: Please give me another pair of chopsticks.

words.tip: The bamboo radical 竹 sits on top. Counted in pairs: 一双筷子. Etiquette to teach: never stand them upright in a bowl of rice, because it looks like incense for the dead.

examples.english: You need a spoon for soup.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ sháozi tài dà le.
examples.english: This spoon is too big.

words.tip: 把 because it has a handle. The flat-bottomed Chinese soup spoon is also called a 汤匙 (tāngchí). 一勺糖 = a spoonful of sugar.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ dāo hěn kuài, xiǎoxīn!
examples.english: This knife is very sharp, be careful!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qiē cài de dāo zài nǎlǐ?
examples.english: Where's my vegetable knife?

words.tip: A sharp knife is 快 (fast) in Chinese. The character is a picture of a blade, and it hides in 切 and 剪. Chinese kitchens use one big 菜刀 for everything.

examples.english: I eat noodles with a fork.
Waiter, do you have a fork?

words.tip: 刀叉 = knife and fork, the 'Western' way to eat. First tone; 差 (chà, poor) falls and 茶 (chá, tea) rises.

examples.english: Careful, the bowl is hot!
Whose bowl is this?

words.tip: Both the thing and a measure word: 一碗米饭. 洗碗 = to do the dishes, whatever is in the sink. 石 (stone) on the left: bowls were ceramic.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ lái chǎo liǎng ge cài.
examples.english: I'll stir-fry a couple of dishes.
Do you like fried rice?

words.tip: The heart of Chinese home cooking: a hot wok and quick stirring. 炒饭 = fried rice, 炒面 = fried noodles. 火 on the left is the fire radical, shared by 烤 and 烧.

examples.english: How many minutes do the noodles need to boil?
I'll make you some coffee.

words.tip: For anything cooked in water: 煮面, 煮鸡蛋, 煮饺子. The four dots 灬 at the bottom are another form of fire. Just boiling water is 烧水.

words.gloss: to roast, to bake, to grill

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng kǎo yí ge dàngāo.
examples.english: I'd like to bake a cake.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài huāyuán li kǎo ròu ba.
examples.english: Let's have a barbecue in the garden.

words.tip: Dry heat: oven, grill or open fire. 烤鸭 = roast duck, 烤肉 = barbecue. Chinese kitchens rarely have an oven (烤箱), which often surprises Germans.

examples.english: Have a taste of this soup.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chángchang nǐ zuò de cài.
examples.english: I'd like to try your cooking.

words.tip: Usually softened by doubling or with 一下: 尝尝, 尝一下 = have a little taste. Trying clothes or ideas is 试. Second tone, the same sound as 长 (long).

examples.english: There's still soup in the pot.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào yí ge dà guō.
examples.english: We need a big pot.

words.tip: One word for pot, pan and wok. 火锅 (hotpot) is the meal to share with friends. 钅 is the metal radical. First tone; 国 (guó) rises.

examples.english: Can you eat spicy food?
I'd like one that isn't spicy.

words.tip: The key restaurant question in China: 能吃辣吗? 不辣 = not spicy, 微辣 = mild. Sichuan's 麻辣 adds a numbing tingle. Never used for temperature.

examples.english: This juice is a bit sour.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan yòu suān yòu tián de cài.
examples.english: I like sweet-and-sour dishes.

words.tip: Also for aching muscles: 腿很酸. 酸奶 = yoghurt ('sour milk'), 酸辣汤 = hot and sour soup. Jealousy is 'sour' too: see 吃醋.

examples.english: This medicine is bitter.

examples.pinyin: Kāfēi tài kǔ, wǒ yào fàng táng.
examples.english: The coffee's too bitter, I'm adding sugar.

words.tip: Also a hard life: 辛苦 (xīnkǔ) = hard, exhausting, and 辛苦了! thanks someone for their effort. 艹 on top: bitter herbs. Third tone; 哭 (kū, to cry) is flat.

examples.english: Today's soup is a bit salty.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan tián de háishi xián de?
examples.english: Do you prefer sweet or savoury?

words.tip: The great breakfast divide: sweet or salty? Chinese breakfasts are mostly 咸. Too salty = 太咸了. Second tone; 先 (xiān, first) is flat.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde wèidào tài dàn le.
examples.english: I think it tastes too bland.

examples.text: 我喜欢喝淡一点儿的茶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan hē dàn yìdiǎnr de chá.
examples.english: I like my tea a bit weaker.

words.tip: Not enough salt or flavour; also weak tea and pale colours. The opposite of 咸 for food and of 浓 (nóng) for drinks. 氵 water next to two fires.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de māo ne? Tā zài nǎlǐ?
examples.english: Where's my cat? Where is it?
It doesn't like having a bath.

words.tip: The third way to write tā, after 他 and 她: same sound, used for animals and things. Often it's simply left out: 我不喜欢 (I don't like it) rather than 我不喜欢它.

examples.english: Hello, please come in!
What would you like to drink?

words.tip: 你 with a heart (心) underneath: you, with respect. For elders, customers and your partner's parents. Like German Sie, but only for one person and used much less.

examples.english: Let's go!
What shall we eat tonight?

words.tip: Northern and warm: a 'we' that always includes the person you're talking to. 我们 can mean either. Perfect for couples: 咱们家 = our home.

examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōu shì nǐ de ma?
examples.english: Are these all yours?
I like all of these dishes.

words.tip: 这 + 些 makes the plural, and no measure word is needed: 这些书. Chinese nouns never change, so 些 does the work.

examples.english: Who are those people?

examples.text: 那些是我小时候的照片。
examples.pinyin: Nàxiē shì wǒ xiǎoshíhou de zhàopiàn.
examples.english: Those are photos from my childhood.

words.tip: The plural of 那. Mind the tone: 哪些 (nǎxiē, third tone) asks 'which ones?'. Point at near and far things and drill 这些 against 那些.

examples.english: You're taller than me.
This mountain is very high.

words.tip: Tall people and high mountains, prices and temperatures: one word where German splits groß and hoch. The character is a tall tower. 多高? = how tall?

examples.english: I'm shorter than my older brother.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ yǐzi tài ǎi le.
examples.english: This chair is too low.

words.tip: Short in height only; short in length is 短. Third tone; with a falling tone you'd be saying 爱 (love). About people it can sting, so 不高 is kinder.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì bu shì pàng le?
examples.english: Have I put on weight?
This cat is really fat!

words.tip: Said far more directly in China than in Germany: 你胖了! can simply mean 'you look well fed'. Warn your partner so they don't take offence. For babies it's a compliment.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ tài shòu le, duō chī yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: You're too thin, eat a bit more.
He's tall and thin.

words.tip: Thin for people, lean for meat (瘦肉), tight for clothes. 疒 is the illness radical: being thin wasn't always a good sign. 减肥 = to lose weight.

examples.english: You look really handsome today!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ nánpéngyou yòu gāo yòu shuài.
examples.english: My boyfriend is tall and handsome.

words.tip: For men; women are 漂亮 or 美. 帅哥 (shuàigē, 'handsome brother') is how shop staff address any young man, as 美女 is for women.

examples.english: The toilet is on the left.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yòng zuǒ shǒu xiě zì.
examples.english: I write with my left hand.

words.tip: Usually with 边: 左边 = the left side. 往左 = to the left. To tell the two apart, look inside: 左 has 工, and 右 has 口 (a mouth: you eat with your right hand).

examples.english: The bank is on your right.

examples.pinyin: Xiān wǎng yòu, ránhòu yìzhí zǒu.
examples.english: First go right, then keep going straight.

words.tip: 右边 = on the right. Sounds exactly like 又 (again). Not 'correct': that's 对. Play robot together: 往左! 往右!

examples.english: Keep going straight and you're there.
He's been looking at his phone the whole time.

words.tip: In space: straight ahead (一直走). In time: continuously, the whole time (一直下雨).

examples.english: Turn left up ahead.

examples.pinyin: Dào le yínháng wǎng yòu guǎi.
examples.english: Turn right when you get to the bank.

words.tip: 往左拐, 往右拐: what you tell a taxi driver. Southerners and sat-navs say 转 (zhuǎn). 扌 is the hand radical.

examples.pinyin: Guò le zhège lùkǒu jiù dào le.
examples.english: Once you're past this junction you're there.

examples.pinyin: Xià yí ge lùkǒu wǎng yòu guǎi.
examples.english: Turn right at the next junction.

words.tip: 'Road mouth': where roads open into each other. A crossroads is a 十字路口, shaped like 十. The traffic light there is a 红绿灯, a 'red-green lamp'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ tài huì huā qián le!
examples.english: You're far too good at spending money!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xǐhuan huā qián mǎi yīfu.
examples.english: I don't like spending money on clothes.

words.tip: 花 alone is the verb 'to spend', for money and for time: 花了一百块, 花时间. Yes, it's the same character as flower. Verb + object, so amounts go in the middle: 花很多钱.

examples.english: Taking the metro saves a lot of money.

examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng néng shěng hěn duō shíjiān.
examples.english: This way we can save a lot of time.

words.tip: Using less of something: 省钱, 省时间, 省电. Putting money aside is 存钱 (cúnqián). The same character also means province: 四川省.

examples.english: He doesn't earn much.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng duō zhuàn yìdiǎnr qián.
examples.english: I'd like to earn a bit more money.

words.tip: 赚钱 = to make money. 贝 on the left is a shell, the oldest Chinese money, also found in 贵. Talking about salaries is much less of a taboo in China.

examples.english: I didn't bring any cash.
You can only use cash here.

words.tip: 'Ready gold'. Rarely needed in China, where everyone pays by phone (扫码, scanning a code): the opposite of cash-loving Germany, and a good culture-shock topic.

examples.english: I get paid tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de gōngzī gòu yòng ma?
examples.english: Is your salary enough to live on?

words.tip: 发工资 = payday, literally 'the salary is handed out'. Asking 你工资多少? is quite normal among Chinese relatives, so prepare your partner.

examples.english: Rent is expensive here.

examples.text: 我们每个月一号交房租。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen měi ge yuè yī hào jiāo fángzū.
examples.english: We pay the rent on the first of every month.
alternatives: 每个月一号我们交房租。

words.tip: 租 alone is the verb: 租房子 = to rent a flat. The landlord is the 房东. In China rent is often paid three months at a time.

examples.english: We're signing the contract tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn hétong wǒ kàn bu dǒng.
examples.english: I can't understand this contract.

words.tip: Both sides 'join and agree'. 签合同 = to sign a contract. The second syllable is light: hétong.

examples.english: The power's gone off at home.

examples.pinyin: Chūmén yào guān dēng, shěng diàn.
examples.english: Turn the lights off when you go out, to save electricity.

words.tip: Originally 'lightning'. It powers a whole word family: 电话, 电脑, 电视, 电影 (electric speech, brain, vision, shadows). 没电了 = out of power, said of phones too.

examples.english: Do you have insurance?
You should buy insurance before travelling.

words.tip: 'Protect against danger', with the 险 of 危险. You buy insurance: 买保险. Two third tones, so the first one rises in speech: báoxiǎn.

examples.english: Have you paid the electricity bill?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng duō jiāo jǐ ge péngyou.
examples.english: I'd like to make a few more friends.

words.tip: To hand something over: rent, fees, homework (交作业). Also in 交朋友, to make friends. First tone; 脚 (jiǎo, foot) dips and 叫 (jiào, to call) falls.

examples.english: That's great!

examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié tài xiǎo le.
examples.english: These shoes are too small.

words.tip: Usually wrapped up as 太…了. It can complain (太贵了 = too expensive) or enthuse (太好了 = great!). 不太 = not very: 不太好.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ fēicháng xǐhuan nǐ de jiārén.
examples.english: I like your family very much.
Tonight's dinner is extremely tasty.

words.tip: 'Not ordinary'. A real step above 很, which is often just a filler. 非常感谢 = thank you very much.

examples.english: I'm especially tired today.
This present is very special.

words.tip: As an adverb it's the strongest everyday 'very': 特别好吃. As an adjective it means special, unusual.

examples.english: This shop is fairly cheap.
I tend to prefer tea.

words.tip: Softer than 很: 'fairly', or 'more than the alternative'. 我比较喜欢茶 = I tend to prefer tea. Also the verb 'to compare'.

examples.english: This film is pretty good.
I've been quite busy lately.

words.tip: Casual and northern, usually rounded off with 的: 挺好的 = pretty good. Third tone; 听 (tīng, to listen) is flat.

examples.english: This room is bright.
It's light, time to get up!

words.tip: Hidden inside 月亮 (moon) and 漂亮 (pretty), where it's toneless. 天亮了 = day is breaking. Fourth tone on its own.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ tài àn le, kāi dēng ba.
examples.english: It's too dark in here, let's put the light on.
This photo is a bit dark.

words.tip: Dim, short of light: for rooms, screens and photos. Night-time dark is 黑: 天黑了. Ironically the character contains two suns (日).

examples.text: 春节的时候家里很热闹。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié de shíhou jiā li hěn rènao.
examples.english: At Chinese New Year the house is full of life.
I like lively places.

words.tip: 'Hot and noisy', and in China that's a good thing: a full restaurant, a family at New Year. Compare it with the German love of Ruhe. Plain 'noisy' as a complaint is 吵.

examples.english: These shoes are very comfortable.
I'm not feeling very well today.

words.tip: For sofas and shoes, and for your body: 不舒服 = not feeling well, the gentle way to say you're ill. The second syllable is toneless.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de fángjiān tài luàn le!
examples.english: Your room is such a mess!
My hair's a mess.

words.tip: A messy room, wild hair, chaotic traffic. Before a verb it means 'carelessly, any old how': 别乱说! = don't talk nonsense.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng dìng yí ge fángjiān.
examples.english: I'd like to book a room.
Are the plane tickets booked?

words.tip: For rooms, tickets, tables and takeaway: 订房间, 订票, 订位. 订好了 = it's booked. 讠 is the speech radical: bookings used to be made by word of mouth.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn lí hǎi hěn jìn.
examples.english: This hotel is very close to the sea.
Which hotel are we staying at?

words.tip: Literally 'wine shop', but it's a hotel. A 饭店 can be a hotel or a restaurant; a 宾馆 is a simpler hotel. Counted with 家, like shops and restaurants.

examples.english: This hotel is right by the sea.
In summer the seaside is crowded.

words.tip: The 'sea edge'. The sandy beach itself is a 沙滩 (shātān). 边 makes many place words: 旁边, 左边, 河边 (riverside).

words.gloss: to have a holiday, to be off

examples.english: We're off tomorrow, where shall we go?
We get seven days off for Chinese New Year.

words.tip: 'Release for holiday': what schools and companies do. 放三天假 = to get three days off. Asking for leave yourself is 请假. Careful: read jiǎ, 假 means fake.

examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì yǒu hěn duō jǐngdiǎn.
examples.english: This city has lots of sights.

examples.pinyin: Zhège jǐngdiǎn rén tài duō le.
examples.english: This sight is far too crowded.

words.tip: A 'scenery spot'. Famous ones get very crowded in the national holidays: 人山人海, 'people mountain, people sea'. Two third tones, so the first one rises: jíngdiǎn.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de hángbān jǐ diǎn dào?
examples.english: What time does your flight arrive?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò tóng yí ge hángbān.
examples.english: We're on the same flight.

words.tip: The scheduled flight with its number (航班号). The 班 is the same as in 上班 and 下班: something that runs to a timetable. The plane itself is a 飞机.

words.gloss: to be delayed, to run late (transport)

examples.pinyin: Fēijī wǎndiǎn le liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: The plane was two hours late.
The trains are rarely late.

words.tip: For planes and trains only: 'late on the clock'. People who are late 迟到. Chinese high-speed trains rarely 晚点, which makes a nice comparison with German ones.

words.gloss: to pick up, to meet; to answer (the phone)

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jǐ diǎn lái jiē wǒ?
examples.english: What time are you coming to pick me up?
Why aren't you answering the phone?

words.tip: To receive someone or something: 接人, 接电话. Its partner is 送 (to see off). 扌 is the hand radical. First tone; 姐 (jiě) dips and 借 (jiè, to borrow) falls.

words.gloss: to see off, to take (someone); to give (a present); to deliver

examples.english: I'll take you to the station.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng sòng nǐ yí ge lǐwù.
examples.english: I'd like to give you a present.

words.tip: Three everyday uses: seeing someone off (送你回家), giving a present (送礼物) and delivering (送外卖). 辶 is the walking radical. A good host always 送s guests to the door, or further.

words.gloss: to be late, to arrive late

examples.english: Sorry I'm late.

examples.pinyin: Kuài diǎnr, wǒmen yào chídào le!
examples.english: Hurry up, we're going to be late!

words.tip: 'Arrive late', for people; trains and planes 晚点. Compare attitudes: how late is late in Germany, and in China?

examples.english: Let's meet at the entrance to the cinema.
This cinema is very new.

words.tip: 电影 + 院, the same 院 as in 医院. Films are 'electric shadows'. Going to the cinema is simply 看电影.

examples.english: The museum is closed on Mondays.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bówùguǎn yào mǎi piào ma?
examples.english: Do you need a ticket for this museum?

words.tip: A 'hall of many things'. 馆 is a building for the public: 饭馆, 图书馆 (library), 大使馆 (embassy). Many Chinese museums are free but need online booking with a passport.

examples.text: 我买了两张音乐会的票。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng yīnyuèhuì de piào.
examples.english: I've bought two tickets for the concert.

examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng yīnyuèhuì tài bàng le!
examples.english: This concert is fantastic!

words.tip: 音乐 + 会 (gathering): mostly classical. A pop concert is a 演唱会 (yǎnchànghuì). Counted with 场, like other events.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù jiǔbā hē yì bēi ba.
examples.english: Let's go to a bar for a drink.

examples.pinyin: Nà jiā jiǔbā rén hěn duō.
examples.english: That bar is very busy.

words.tip: 吧 copies the sound of English 'bar' and is first tone here; as a sentence particle it's toneless. The first example has both. The same trick gives 网吧 (internet café).

examples.english: We have to queue for tickets.

examples.pinyin: Páiduì de rén tài duō le.
examples.english: There are too many people queuing.

words.tip: 'Arrange in a line', with the 队 of 'team'. 请排队 = please queue. A long queue outside a restaurant means the food is good.

words.gloss: (turns a statement into a yes/no question)

examples.english: Are you hungry?

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì nǐ de shǒujī ma?
examples.english: Is this your phone?

words.tip: Add it to any statement and you have a yes/no question; the word order doesn't change. Never combine it with a question word (什么, 谁) or with 是不是. Toneless.

examples.english: I'm fine, and you?
Where are my keys?

words.tip: Bounces a question back: 你呢? = and you? Noun + 呢 also asks 'where is…?': 钥匙呢? After a question word it softens the tone: 你在做什么呢?

examples.english: You go ahead and eat.
You're German, aren't you?

words.tip: Softens a command into a suggestion (走吧! = let's go), or turns a statement into 'I guess…, right?'. 好吧 = oh, all right then. Toneless.

examples.english: Sure, let's go together!
Why aren't you eating?

words.tip: Pure feeling at the end of a sentence: 好啊! (sure!), 是啊 (yes indeed), 谁啊? (who is it?). It blends with the sound before it, which is why you also see 呀 (ya) and 哪 (na). At the start, 啊! is 'ah!'.

words.gloss: (links a verb to how it is done)

examples.english: You speak very well.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān shuì de hěn wǎn.
examples.english: I went to sleep very late yesterday.

words.tip: Verb + 得 + description: 说得很好, 跑得快. If there's an object, repeat the verb: 他说中文说得很好. It sounds the same as 的. Read děi, it means 'must'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chī le liǎng wǎn mǐfàn.
examples.english: I ate two bowls of rice.
It's started raining!

words.tip: Not a past tense! After a verb it marks a completed action (我买了一本书); at the end of a sentence it marks a new situation (下雨了 = it's started raining). Negate with 没 and drop the 了: 我没买.

examples.english: I've seen this film.
I've never eaten this dish.

words.tip: Experience at some point in your life: 去过 = have been to, 吃过 = have tried. Negative: 没…过. Compare 我去了北京 (I went) with 我去过北京 (I've been). As a full verb, 过 (guò) means to cross or to spend time.

examples.english: Where did you go just now?

examples.pinyin: Gāngcái yǒu rén gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: Someone phoned you just now.

words.tip: A time word like 昨天, so it goes before the verb or at the very start. A few minutes ago, no more. 刚 alone is an adverb: 我刚到 = I've just arrived.

examples.english: What happened?

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zuótiān fāshēng de shì.
examples.english: This is what happened yesterday.

words.tip: A little formal; for a casual 'what's up?' say 怎么了? The thing that happens comes after the verb: 发生了一件事.

examples.english: He suddenly stopped talking.
It suddenly started raining outside.

words.tip: Before the verb or right at the start of the sentence. 然 is the same '-ly' ending as in 当然 and 虽然. 太突然了! = that's so sudden!

words.gloss: when, while, at the time of

examples.text: 我吃饭的时候不看手机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chī fàn de shíhou bú kàn shǒujī.
examples.english: I don't look at my phone while I'm eating.

examples.text: 你来的时候给我打电话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lái de shíhou gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: Give me a call when you come.

words.tip: It comes at the END of the 'when' part: 下雨的时候 = when it rains. German speakers want to put it first, like wenn or als. It's inside 小时候 and 什么时候.

examples.english: I'm cooking right now.
They're in a meeting at the moment.

words.tip: The Chinese '-ing': 正在 + verb, often with 呢 at the end. The shorter 在 does the same. It works like German gerade: Ich koche gerade.

examples.english: He didn't get up until ten.
Why are you only coming now?

words.tip: Later or slower than expected: 八点才来 = didn't come until eight. Its opposite is 就 (sooner than expected). No 了 after the verb with 才. Much like German erst.

words.gloss: right away, as early as; then; just

examples.english: The food will be ready in a moment.

examples.pinyin: Tā liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
examples.english: He was up as early as six.

words.tip: Sooner or more easily than expected: 六点就起床了 = up as early as six. It pairs with 如果: 如果下雨，我就不去. Also 'exactly': 就是这个. Contrast it with 才 using the same sentence.

words.gloss: at the same time (doing two things)

examples.text: 我一边做饭一边听音乐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yìbiān zuòfàn yìbiān tīng yīnyuè.
examples.english: I listen to music while I cook.

examples.text: 别一边吃饭一边看手机。
examples.pinyin: Bié yìbiān chī fàn yìbiān kàn shǒujī.
examples.english: Don't look at your phone while you're eating.

words.tip: Always in pairs: 一边 A 一边 B = doing A while doing B, with the same person doing both. Literally 'on one side… on one side…'.

words.gloss: to hug, to hold in one's arms

examples.english: I want to give you a hug.
Give me a hug, OK?

words.tip: For hugging people and for carrying babies or pets. Doubled, it's tender: 抱抱. 扌 hand radical + 包 (to wrap): wrap your arms around. Hugging is less usual in Chinese families than in German ones.

examples.english: Give me a kiss!

examples.pinyin: Tā qīn le yíxià háizi de liǎn.
examples.english: She gave the child a kiss on the cheek.

words.tip: As a verb: to kiss. As an adjective: closely related (亲人 = close family). Online sellers call their customers 亲 ('dear'). The more formal word for a kiss is 吻 (wěn).

examples.english: Good morning, darling!

examples.pinyin: Qīn'ài de, nǐ dào jiā le ma?
examples.english: Darling, are you home yet?

words.tip: On its own it means 'darling'; before a name it's 'dear': 亲爱的妈妈. The apostrophe in the pinyin keeps qīn and ài apart. Some Chinese couples find it a bit theatrical and prefer nicknames, so say what you like to be called.

examples.english: Love is more important than money.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge àiqíng gùshi.
examples.english: This is a love story.

words.tip: Romantic love only, and a noun; 爱 covers love for family too. A 爱情片 is a romance film. 情 (feeling) has the heart radical 忄 on its left.

examples.english: Let's walk hand in hand.

examples.text: 他们在公园里牵手散步。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài gōngyuán li qiānshǒu sànbù.
examples.english: They're walking hand in hand in the park.

words.tip: Literally 'lead by the hand'. It's verb + object, so it can split: 牵着你的手 = holding your hand. Also 手拉手 (hand in hand).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yì zhǒng qíguài de gǎnjué.
examples.english: I have a strange feeling.
How are you feeling now?

words.tip: Noun and verb. 觉 is jué here and in 觉得, but jiào in 睡觉. 感觉 is about sensations and impressions; 觉得 gives an opinion.

examples.english: I believe you.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù xiāngxìn wǒ shuō de huà ma?
examples.english: Don't you believe what I'm saying?

words.tip: To believe what someone says, or to believe in them. 信 is a person 亻 standing by their word 言; it also means letter. 我不信! = I don't buy it!

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì chīcù le?
examples.english: Are you jealous?

examples.pinyin: Bié chīcù, tā zhǐ shì tóngshì.
examples.english: Don't be jealous, she's just a colleague.

words.tip: Literally 'to eat vinegar': jealousy tastes sour. Only for romantic jealousy; envy of someone's success is 羡慕 or 嫉妒. A fun one to act out.

examples.english: I'm proud of you.

examples.pinyin: Tā tài jiāo'ào le, méiyǒu péngyou.
examples.english: He's too arrogant and has no friends.

words.tip: Two sides: 为你骄傲 = proud of you, but 他很骄傲 = he's arrogant. Modesty is prized, so praise is often answered with 哪里哪里. The apostrophe in jiāo'ào keeps the syllables apart.

examples.english: I'm very disappointed in myself.

examples.pinyin: Bié shīwàng, xià cì zài lái.
examples.english: Don't be disappointed, try again next time.

words.tip: 'Lose hope'. Disappointed in someone: 对…失望. The same 望 as in 希望 (hope).

examples.english: Could I trouble you to help me for a moment?
I've put you to so much trouble!

words.tip: The polite way to ask a favour: 麻烦你… = could I trouble you to… And to thank someone afterwards: 麻烦你了. As an adjective: 太麻烦了 = what a hassle. The second syllable is toneless.

examples.english: Excuse me, how do I get to the metro station?
Excuse me, is this seat taken?

words.tip: Opens any question to a stranger. Only before asking something; to squeeze past, say 不好意思 or 借过. Have your partner use it for every question this session.

examples.english: Sorry to bother you for a moment.

examples.pinyin: Bié dǎrǎo tā, tā zài shuìjiào.
examples.english: Don't disturb him, he's sleeping.

words.tip: 打扰一下 = sorry to interrupt. When leaving someone's home, say 打扰了 ('I've disturbed you'). Two third tones, so the first one rises: dárǎo.

words.gloss: it doesn't matter, that's all right

examples.english: It's all right, take your time.
It doesn't matter if you're a little late.

words.tip: The standard reply to 对不起. 关系 means relationship or connection, so literally 'it has no connection'. 关系 is also the famous Chinese network of personal contacts.

examples.text: 不好意思，我忘了你的名字。
examples.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, wǒ wàng le nǐ de míngzi.
examples.english: I'm sorry, I've forgotten your name.

examples.text: 不好意思，我想问一个问题。
examples.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, wǒ xiǎng wèn yí ge wèntí.
examples.english: Excuse me, I'd like to ask a question.

words.tip: A lighter sorry than 对不起: for being late, squeezing past, asking a favour. Also 'to feel embarrassed': 我不好意思问 = I'm too shy to ask.

words.gloss: to go online, to use the internet

characters.meaning: to go on, to get on

examples.english: Can you get online here?
I like shopping online.

words.tip: 'Get on the net'. 网 is a picture of a net and means the internet: 网上 = online, 网站 = website, 网友 = online friend. Explain which Western sites don't open in China.

examples.english: I've forgotten the password.
What's the password here?

words.tip: For Wi-Fi, bank cards and phones alike. Usually asked with 多少, as if it were a number; 密码是什么? is fine too. Useful everywhere: Wi-Fi 密码是多少?

examples.english: Send me the photos.

examples.pinyin: Dào le gěi wǒ fā ge xiāoxi.
examples.english: Send me a message when you get there.

words.tip: For anything that goes out electronically: 发消息, 发照片, 发邮件, and 发微信 (to send a WeChat). First tone; in 头发 the same character is read fà.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de yóujiàn tài duō le.
examples.english: There are too many emails today.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎshàng gěi nǐ huí yóujiàn.
examples.english: I'll reply to your email right away.

words.tip: Short for 电子邮件 (electronic mail). Counted with 封, like letters. Tell your partner that in China work runs on WeChat far more than on email.

examples.english: Can this film be downloaded?
The download is too slow!

words.tip: 'Carry down'. Uploading is 上传. An app is an App or a 应用 (yìngyòng). 载 is zài here, though some speakers say zǎi.

examples.english: This screen is too small.
Don't stare at the screen all the time.

words.tip: For phones, computers and cinemas. Germans say Bildschirm, a 'picture shield'; the Chinese picture is a folding screen plus a curtain.

examples.english: My phone needs charging.
Where can I charge it?

words.tip: 'Fill with electricity'. The charger is a 充电器, a power bank a 充电宝 ('charging treasure'). People also say it of themselves: to recharge, to learn something new.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kànjiàn wǒ de ěrjī le ma?
examples.english: Have you seen my earphones?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò chē de shíhou dài ěrjī.
examples.english: I wear earphones when I'm on the bus.

words.tip: An 'ear machine', like 手机 (hand machine) and 飞机 (flying machine). You 戴 them, like glasses and hats. A pair is 一副耳机.

examples.english: I like your voice.

examples.pinyin: Diànshì de shēngyīn tài dà le.
examples.english: The TV is too loud.

words.tip: Both a sound and a person's voice. Volume is big or small, not loud or quiet: 声音大一点儿 = turn it up. The 音 of 音乐 and the 声 of 声调 (tone).

examples.pinyin: Shǒujī de diànchí kuài méi diàn le.
examples.english: The phone's battery is nearly dead.

examples.pinyin: Zhège yào yòng liǎng jié diànchí.
examples.english: This takes two batteries.

words.tip: An 'electricity pond'. For a dying phone people just say 没电了. 池 is also in 游泳池 (swimming pool).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān tián zhè zhāng biǎogé.
examples.english: Please fill in this form first.
You have to write your name on the form.

words.tip: Often just 表: 填表 = to fill in a form. Counted with 张 because it's a sheet. Chinese forms want the family name first, a good thing to practise.

examples.english: You need to fill in your passport number here.
I don't know how to fill it in.

words.tip: 填表 = to fill in a form; 填空 = to fill in the blanks (in a test). 土 (earth) on the left: originally filling a hole. Same sound as 甜 (sweet).

examples.english: Please sign here.
The contract hasn't been signed yet.

words.tip: Also 签名 (to sign your name). Chinese companies seal contracts with a red stamp (盖章) rather than a signature. 竹 bamboo on top: early records were bamboo slips.

words.gloss: to handle, to get (something official) done

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù yínháng bàn yì zhāng kǎ.
examples.english: I need to go to the bank to get a card.
We haven't got the keys, what shall we do?

words.tip: For paperwork and errands: 办签证 (to get a visa), 办手续 (to go through the formalities), 办卡. 怎么办? = what shall we do? It's the 办 in 办公室 (office).

examples.english: You need to get a visa to go to China.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de qiānzhèng dào shénme shíhou?
examples.english: How long is your visa valid?

words.tip: 办签证 = to apply for a visa. 证 means certificate, as in 保证 and 身份证 (ID card). Rules change, so check together what your partner needs for a trip.

examples.english: Have you been busy lately?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ máng wán le gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: I'll call you when I'm done.

words.tip: Heart 忄 + 亡 (lost): a heart with no time. 你忙吗? is a polite way of asking 'have you got a moment?'. 帮忙 = to help out. Being busy is almost a greeting in China: 最近忙吗?

examples.english: I've been under a lot of pressure lately.

examples.pinyin: Bié gěi zìjǐ tài duō yālì.
examples.english: Don't put too much pressure on yourself.

words.tip: Stress is 'big', not 'much': 压力很大. It comes from work, parents or house prices. 力 is a flexed arm, as in 努力 (hard-working).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàwǔ yào jiàn yí ge kèhù.
examples.english: I have to meet a client this afternoon.
This client is very important.

words.tip: A business client. A shopper in a store is a 顾客 (gùkè); both contain the 客 of 客人 (guest).

examples.english: I have to work overtime again today.
Does your company often work overtime?

words.tip: 'Add a shift'. Very common in China; '996' means nine to nine, six days a week. Compare it with the German Feierabend.

words.gloss: to finish work, to get off work

examples.pinyin: Xiàbān yǐhòu wǒ qù mǎi cài.
examples.english: After work I'll go and buy groceries.
I haven't finished work yet.

words.tip: Its opposite is 上班 (to go to work, to be at work). 下班了! = I'm done for the day. The same pattern works for class: 上课, 下课.

examples.english: He's probably not coming any more.

examples.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ zǒu dàgài shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: It's about ten minutes' walk from here.

words.tip: Two uses: a likely guess (大概是), and 'approximately' before a number (大概十个人). 可能 is weaker; 肯定 is certain.

examples.pinyin: Qíshí wǒ bù xǐhuan hē jiǔ.
examples.english: Actually, I don't like drinking alcohol.
Actually, Chinese isn't that hard.

words.tip: Corrects an impression: 'the truth is…'. It goes at the start of the sentence or right after the subject. Softer than a flat contradiction.

examples.english: You're finally here!
We're home at last.

words.tip: Relief after a long wait, always before the verb and usually with 了. For the last item in a list use 最后.

examples.english: He's definitely forgotten.

examples.text: 你肯定会喜欢这个地方。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěndìng huì xǐhuan zhège dìfang.
examples.english: You're sure to like this place.

words.tip: A confident guess, like 一定. In answers: 肯定! = for sure! Also a verb, 'to affirm'. The scale goes 可能, 大概, 肯定.

words.gloss: to seem; it looks as if

examples.english: He doesn't seem very happy.
It looks as if it's going to rain.

words.tip: Softens a statement: 'it seems, I think'. Handy for polite guesses: 你好像感冒了. 像 alone = to resemble: 你像你妈妈.

examples.english: The air is good today.
Open the window and let some fresh air in.

words.tip: 'Empty gas'. Air quality (空气质量) is a daily topic in Chinese cities. 气 also gives 天气 (weather) and 生气 (angry).

examples.english: Careful, don't play with fire!

examples.pinyin: Huǒ tài dà le, guān xiǎo yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: The heat's too high, turn it down a bit.

words.tip: A picture of flames, and the radical in 炒, 烤 and 灯. On the cooker, 火 is the heat: 大火, 小火. A 火车 is a 'fire vehicle', and something very popular is 很火.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xié li yǒu yí kuài shítou.
examples.english: There's a stone in my shoe.

examples.text: 孩子喜欢在河边玩石头。
examples.pinyin: Háizi xǐhuan zài hébiān wán shítou.
examples.english: Children like playing with stones by the river.

words.tip: 头 is just a toneless noun ending here, as in 木头 (wood). Rock-paper-scissors is 石头剪刀布: play a round!

examples.english: The shoes are covered in dirt.
Flowers need water and soil.

words.tip: A plant pushing out of the ground. As a radical it's in 地, 城 and 填. As slang, 太土了 = so uncool. A potato, 土豆, is an 'earth bean'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhǐ yǒu yí ge dìqiú.
examples.english: We only have one Earth.

examples.pinyin: Dìqiú shang yǒu hěn duō guójiā.
examples.english: There are many countries on Earth.

words.tip: The 'ground ball'. 球 is any ball: 足球 (football), 月球 (the moon as a body). 地 also gives 地铁 (metro) and 地方 (place).

words.gloss: to hike, to climb a mountain

examples.english: Let's go hiking at the weekend.

examples.pinyin: Páshān hěn lèi, dànshì hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: Hiking is tiring, but it makes you happy.

words.tip: The Chinese word for hiking: any walk up a hill counts, steps and all. 爬 alone is to climb or to crawl. Many famous mountains have stairs to the very top.

words.gloss: to go for a walk, to stroll

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen měi tiān wǎnshang qù sànbù.
examples.english: We go for a walk every evening.
I like walking by the river.

words.tip: 'Scatter steps'. An after-dinner walk is a Chinese habit: 饭后百步走，活到九十九 (a hundred steps after a meal and you'll live to ninety-nine). Verb + object: 散一会儿步.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de bēibāo tài zhòng le.
examples.english: My backpack is too heavy.
The passport is in the backpack.

words.tip: 背 is first tone here (to carry on the back); with a fourth tone, bèi, it's the back itself. 包 is any bag: 书包 (school bag), 钱包 (wallet).

examples.english: The scenery here is so beautiful!

examples.pinyin: Cóng shān shang kàn, fēngjǐng hěn hǎo.
examples.english: Seen from the mountain, the view is lovely.

words.tip: 'Wind scenery'. 看风景 = to enjoy the view. The same 景 as in 景点 (sight). 美 (měi) is 'beautiful' for landscapes.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāng wǒmen pāizhào ma?
examples.english: Could you take a photo of us?
You're not allowed to take photos here.

words.tip: Also 拍照片 or 照相. Taking lots of photos, with poses, is a big part of any Chinese outing. Say 茄子 (qiézi, aubergine) instead of 'cheese'!

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen měi tiān liànxí shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: We practise for ten minutes every day.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào duō liànxí shuō Zhōngwén.
examples.english: You need to practise speaking Chinese more.

words.tip: Verb and noun: 做练习 = to do exercises. It shares 习 with 学习: learning is practice. 多练习 = practise more, every teacher's favourite line.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāng wǒ fānyì yíxià ma?
examples.english: Could you translate for me?
This word is hard to translate.

words.tip: To 'turn over' words into another language. Also the person: 他是翻译. 翻译成德语 = to translate into German.

examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī shuō wǒ de fāyīn búcuò.
examples.english: The teacher says my pronunciation is pretty good.
How is this character pronounced?

words.tip: 'Send out sound'. For German speakers the hard ones are the pairs zh/j, ch/q, sh/x and the vowel ü after j, q, x. Pick three and drill them.

examples.english: Chinese has four tones.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shēngdiào duì bu duì?
examples.english: Are my tones right?

words.tip: The four tones are 一声, 二声, 三声 and 四声, plus the neutral 轻声. Run the classic mā má mǎ mà together. 调 is diào here but tiáo in 调整 (to adjust).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì xiě duōshao ge Hànzì?
examples.english: How many Chinese characters can you write?
I don't know this character.

words.tip: 'Han writing'; Japanese kanji is the same word. A word (词) is made of one or more characters (字). Show how radicals hint at meaning: 氵 water, 口 mouth, 女 woman.

examples.english: The bottle is empty.
This room is empty.

words.tip: First tone = empty (空房间), and it's the 空 of 空气. With a fourth tone, kòng, it means free time, as in 有空. One character, two readings: drill the pair.

words.gloss: to be free, to have time

examples.english: Are you free tomorrow?

examples.pinyin: Yǒu kòng lái wǒ jiā wán ba.
examples.english: Come round to my place when you're free.

words.tip: Literally 'to have a gap'. 没空 = no time. Northerners say 有空儿 (yǒu kòngr). 有空来玩! is a friendly invitation that isn't always meant literally.

examples.english: I've finished eating.

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū nǐ kàn wán le ma?
examples.english: Have you finished reading this book?

words.tip: It mostly sits after another verb to show that it's done: 吃完, 做完, 说完. 完了! on its own = oh no, that's it! Same sound as 玩 (to play), different character.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de shuǐ shì miǎnfèi de.
examples.english: The water here is free.
Children can travel for free.

words.tip: 'Exempt from the fee'. 费 turns up in every bill: 电费 (electricity), 水费 (water), 小费 (tip). Not for 'free time', which is 有空.

examples.english: Whatever, you decide.
Let's just grab a bite of something.

words.tip: The classic answer to 'what shall we eat?', and one that can drive a partner mad. To a guest, 随便坐 = sit wherever you like. Tone of voice decides whether it sounds easy-going or dismissive. 便 is biàn here, but pián in 便宜.

examples.english: Are you going home for Chinese New Year?
We're spending Chinese New Year in China.

words.tip: The biggest holiday, in January or February by the moon calendar. Everyone travels home, families eat 年夜饭 on the eve, and children get 红包. The greeting is 春节快乐! or 过年好!

examples.english: Let's see in the New Year together.
What are your wishes for the New Year?

words.tip: Usually 1 January, also called 元旦 (Yuándàn). The Chinese New Year is 春节, though celebrating it is 过年. 新年快乐 works for both.

examples.english: Which festival do you like best?
What festivals are there in Germany?

words.tip: Any festival day. 节 alone ends festival names: 春节, 中秋节 (Mid-Autumn), 情人节 (Valentine's Day). 节日快乐! is the all-purpose greeting.

examples.english: We're going to Germany for Christmas.
How do Germans celebrate Christmas?

words.tip: The 'holy birth festival'. In China it's a fun evening for shopping and dates, not a family holiday. People give apples on Christmas Eve (平安夜), because 苹果 sounds like 平安 (peace).

examples.english: At Chinese New Year all the children get red envelopes.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ fā le yí ge hóngbāo.
examples.english: I've sent you a red envelope.

words.tip: Money in a red envelope for New Year, weddings and births; today it's often sent on WeChat (发红包). Amounts with an 8 are lucky, and 4 is avoided. Explain who gives to whom in your family.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn qīdài wǒmen de lǚxíng.
examples.english: I'm really looking forward to our trip.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qīdài zǎo diǎnr jiàn dào nǐ.
examples.english: I'm looking forward to seeing you soon.

words.tip: 'Expect and wait': anticipation with pleasure, like German sich freuen auf. 期 is the same as in 星期.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīnnián de mùbiāo shì shénme?
examples.english: What's your goal for this year?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de mùbiāo shì huì shuō Zhōngwén.
examples.english: My goal is to be able to speak Chinese.
