words.tip: An 'eye mark': what you fix your eyes on. 定目标 = to set a goal. Share one language goal each for this year.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge hǎo jīhuì.
examples.english: This is a good opportunity.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài gěi wǒ yí cì jīhuì.
examples.english: Please give me one more chance.

words.tip: 有机会 = if there's a chance, some day: 有机会一起吃饭! Like 有空来玩, it's friendly rather than a fixed plan.

examples.english: This city has changed a lot.
There's been a slight change of plan.

words.tip: A change is 'big' or 'small': 变化很大. 变 alone is the verb: 你变了 = you've changed. 计划没有变化快 = plans can't keep up with changes, a favourite saying.

words.gloss: to prepare, to get ready; to plan to

examples.english: Are you ready?
We're planning to go to Germany next year.

words.tip: Two uses: to get things ready (准备晚饭), and to intend (准备去). 准备好了 = all set. Close to 打算 in the second meaning.

examples.english: We're moving next month.
Moving house is so exhausting!

words.tip: 搬 alone is to move something heavy: 搬桌子. Verb plus object, so 'moved twice' is 搬了两次家. Moving to Beijing = 搬到北京.

examples.english: This box is too heavy.

examples.pinyin: Shū dōu fàng zài xiāngzi li ba.
examples.english: Let's put all the books in the box.

words.tip: Any box or case. A suitcase is a 行李箱, a cardboard box a 纸箱, and the fridge is a 冰箱 ('ice box').

examples.english: We need to buy new furniture.

examples.text: 这件家具是在哪里买的？
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn jiājù shì zài nǎlǐ mǎi de?
examples.english: Where was this piece of furniture bought?

words.tip: 'Home tools'. One piece is 一件家具, a matching set is 一套家具. Name the furniture around you: 床, 桌子, 椅子, 沙发.

examples.text: 我们想租一个大一点儿的房子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiǎng zū yí ge dà yìdiǎnr de fángzi.
examples.english: We'd like to rent a slightly bigger place.

examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān zū gěi shéi le?
examples.english: Who has this room been rented to?

words.tip: It works in both directions: 租房子 is to rent a place, 租给 is to rent it out to someone. The same character is in 房租 (the rent). 租车 = to hire a car.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài Shànghǎi mǎi le fángzi.
examples.english: They've bought a place in Shanghai.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tào fángzi yǒu sān ge fángjiān.
examples.english: This flat has three rooms.

words.tip: The building or flat as a thing you buy or rent; 家 is home. A flat as a unit is counted with 套. 买房子 is a big topic for couples in China: explain why.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de yīfu dōu zài yīguì li.
examples.english: Your clothes are all in the wardrobe.

examples.text: 这个衣柜放不下我的衣服。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yīguì fàng bu xià wǒ de yīfu.
examples.english: This wardrobe can't hold all my clothes.

words.tip: A cupboard for 衣服. 放不下 = there isn't room to put it (verb + 不 + 下). Ask who gets more space in the wardrobe.

examples.pinyin: Wǎn zài chúfáng de guìzi li.
examples.english: The bowls are in the kitchen cupboard.

examples.pinyin: Bǎ bēizi fàng huí guìzi li ba.
examples.english: Put the cups back in the cupboard.

words.tip: Any cupboard with doors. Compounds drop the 子: 衣柜 (wardrobe), 书柜 (bookcase), 鞋柜 (the shoe cabinet by the front door).

examples.pinyin: Shūjià shang yǒu hěn duō Zhōngwén shū.
examples.english: There are lots of Chinese books on the bookshelf.

examples.text: 那本书我放在书架上了。
examples.pinyin: Nà běn shū wǒ fàng zài shūjià shang le.
examples.english: I put that book on the bookshelf.

words.tip: A 'book rack'. Things are 在书架上, on it. 架子 is any shelf or rack, and 架 is also the measure word for planes.

examples.pinyin: Yàoshi zài zhuōzi de chōuti li.
examples.english: The keys are in the desk drawer.
This drawer won't open.

words.tip: A 'pull-out tray'. 打开 = to open; 打不开 = can't be opened, with 不 in the middle. Hide something in a drawer and have your partner ask where it is.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí kuài xīn dìtǎn.
examples.english: I'd like to buy a new rug.

examples.pinyin: Māo xǐhuan shuì zài dìtǎn shang.
examples.english: The cat likes sleeping on the rug.

words.tip: A 'floor blanket'; 毯子 is a blanket. In Chinese homes shoes come off at the door, carpet or not: explain 换鞋 (changing into slippers).

examples.pinyin: Bīngxiāng li hái yǒu niúnǎi ma?
examples.english: Is there any milk left in the fridge?

examples.pinyin: Bǎ yú fàng jìn bīngxiāng ba.
examples.english: Put the fish in the fridge.

words.tip: An 'ice box'. 冰 also means ice-cold: 冰水, 冰啤酒. Open yours and name what's in it: 冰箱里有…

examples.english: The washing machine has broken down, what shall we do?

examples.text: 这些衣服可以用洗衣机洗。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē yīfu kěyǐ yòng xǐyījī xǐ.
examples.english: These clothes can go in the washing machine.

words.tip: A 'wash-clothes machine'. 机 ends many machines: 手机, 飞机, 洗碗机 (dishwasher). 怎么办? = what's to be done?

examples.text: 用微波炉热一下就可以吃。
examples.pinyin: Yòng wēibōlú rè yíxià jiù kěyǐ chī.
examples.english: Just heat it up in the microwave and it's ready to eat.
We don't have a microwave at home.

words.tip: Translated piece by piece from 'micro-wave oven'. 热 is a verb here: 热一下 = to heat up for a moment.

examples.english: There's still rice in the rice cooker.

examples.text: 没有电饭锅，我不会做米饭。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu diànfànguō, wǒ bú huì zuò mǐfàn.
examples.english: Without a rice cooker I can't make rice.

words.tip: An 'electric rice pot', also called 电饭煲. No Chinese kitchen is without one. Show how you measure the rice and the water.

examples.pinyin: Tài rè le, kāi kōngtiáo ba.
examples.english: It's too hot, let's turn on the air conditioning.

examples.text: 房间里的空调有点儿冷。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān li de kōngtiáo yǒudiǎnr lěng.
examples.english: The air conditioning in the room is a bit cold.

words.tip: An 'air adjuster'. 开空调 / 关空调 = to turn it on / off. In southern China it heats in winter too, as there's no central heating.

examples.english: Let's take the stairs.
Be careful going up and down the stairs.

words.tip: A 'building ladder'. 走楼梯 = to take the stairs; 上楼梯 / 下楼梯 = to go up / down them.

examples.text: 电梯坏了，我们走上去吧。
examples.pinyin: Diàntī huài le, wǒmen zǒu shàngqù ba.
examples.english: The lift is broken, let's walk up.

examples.text: 我在电梯里看见邻居了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài diàntī li kànjiàn línjū le.
examples.english: I saw the neighbour in the lift.

words.tip: An 'electric ladder': a lift, and also an escalator (扶梯). 坐电梯 = to take the lift. Counted with 部 or 台, like other machines.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò lóu yǒu èrshí céng.
examples.english: This building has twenty floors.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài sān céng, méiyǒu diàntī.
examples.english: I live on the third floor, with no lift.

words.tip: Number + 层, nothing in between. For where you live, 三楼 and 三层 both work. The ground floor is 一层, so Chinese floor numbers are one higher than German ones. Also layers: 两层蛋糕.

examples.text: 楼上的邻居晚上常常跳舞。
examples.pinyin: Lóushàng de línjū wǎnshang chángcháng tiàowǔ.
examples.english: The neighbours upstairs often dance in the evening.
The toilet is upstairs.

words.tip: Downstairs is 楼下. 我在楼下等你 = I'm waiting for you downstairs: the standard message when picking someone up.

examples.pinyin: Yángtái shang yǒu hěn duō huā.
examples.english: There are lots of flowers on the balcony.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài yángtái shang hē chá ba.
examples.english: Let's have tea on the balcony.

words.tip: A 'sun platform'. In China the balcony is mostly where the washing dries, not where you sit: compare it with a German Balkon.

examples.english: The clothes are drying on the balcony.

examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, bié liàng yīfu le.
examples.english: It's raining, don't hang the washing out.

words.tip: To air-dry: 晾衣服 = to hang up the washing. Most Chinese homes dry clothes on the balcony; a tumble dryer (烘干机) is rare.

examples.english: The clothes aren't dry yet.
The towel is dry already.

words.tip: First tone here, as in 干净 (clean) and 干杯 ('dry the glass'). With the fourth tone, gàn, the same character means 'to do': 你干什么? Opposite: 湿.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de tóufa hái shì shī de.
examples.english: Your hair is still wet.

examples.text: 外面下雨，我的鞋都湿了。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn xià yǔ, wǒ de xié dōu shī le.
examples.english: It's raining outside and my shoes are soaked.

words.tip: sh with the tongue curled back, first tone. The 氵 on the left means water. 湿了 = has got wet. Humid weather is 潮湿.

examples.english: I'll fold the clothes.

examples.text: 衣服干了，我们一起叠吧。
examples.pinyin: Yīfu gān le, wǒmen yìqǐ dié ba.
examples.english: The clothes are dry, let's fold them together.

words.tip: To fold cloth or paper flat: 叠衣服, and 叠被子 (to fold the quilt, that is, to make the bed). 我来 + verb = let me do it.

examples.english: There aren't enough hangers.

examples.text: 这件衣服需要一个衣架。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu xūyào yí ge yījià.
examples.english: This top needs a hanger.

words.tip: A 'clothes rack': a single hanger, or a standing rack. 挂在衣架上 = to hang on a hanger.

examples.english: Wash your hands with soap.
There's no soap left in the bathroom.

words.tip: A bar is 一块肥皂. Scented soap for the body is also called 香皂; liquid hand soap is 洗手液.

examples.english: I forgot to bring my toothbrush.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ yáshuā shì nǐ de ma?
examples.english: Is this toothbrush yours?

words.tip: The two characters of 刷牙 (to brush your teeth), flipped. Counted with 把, like other things with a handle.

examples.english: The toothpaste is nearly finished.

examples.text: 你喜欢什么味道的牙膏？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan shénme wèidào de yágāo?
examples.english: What flavour of toothpaste do you like?

words.tip: 'Tooth paste'. A tube is 一支牙膏. 快…了 = almost: 快用完了 = nearly used up.

examples.text: 我可以用你的洗发水吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ yòng nǐ de xǐfàshuǐ ma?
examples.english: Can I use your shampoo?

examples.pinyin: Zhè píng xǐfàshuǐ shì xīn de.
examples.english: This bottle of shampoo is new.

words.tip: 'Wash-hair water'. 发 is fà (fourth tone) when it means hair, as in 理发, but fā in 发消息. Shower gel is 沐浴露.

examples.english: We're out of toilet paper at home.

examples.text: 出门要带一点儿卫生纸。
examples.english: Take some toilet paper with you when you go out.

words.tip: 卫生 = hygiene, so 'hygiene paper'. A roll is 一卷. Public toilets in China often have none, so people carry tissues (纸巾).

examples.english: Are you awake?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān wǔ diǎn jiù xǐng le.
examples.english: I woke up at five today.

words.tip: 醒了 = awake now. 睡醒 = to wake after a good sleep; 叫醒 = to wake someone: 七点叫醒我. 就 stresses how early it was.

examples.english: The child is already asleep.

examples.text: 你怎么这么快就睡着了？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme zhème kuài jiù shuìzháo le?
examples.english: How did you fall asleep so quickly?

words.tip: 着 is zháo here: sleep has been 'reached'. 睡觉 is going to bed; 睡着 is actually dropping off. Can't sleep = 睡不着, with 不 in the middle.

examples.english: I didn't hear the alarm.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān de nàozhōng dìng hǎo le ma?
examples.english: Have you set the alarm for tomorrow?

words.tip: A 'noisy clock': 闹 is the same as in 热闹. 定闹钟 = to set the alarm; 闹钟响了 = it's ringing.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ bèizi dōu ná zǒu le!
examples.english: You've taken the whole quilt!

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo bèizi tài rè le.
examples.english: This quilt is too hot.

words.tip: The thick quilt you sleep under. A thinner blanket is a 毯子, a pillow a 枕头. 盖被子 = to cover yourself with it.

examples.english: I'm sleepy and want to go to bed.

examples.pinyin: Chī wán wǔfàn wǒ zǒngshì hěn kùn.
examples.english: I'm always sleepy after lunch.

words.tip: 累 is tired from effort; 困 is sleepy, with your eyes closing. 我困了 = I'm getting sleepy. The character is a tree 木 shut in a box.

examples.english: What day is it today?
Which day of the week are you free?

words.tip: The days are numbered, so you ask 'week how-many?'. No 是 needed, in the question or the answer: 今天星期三. Quiz each other with dates from the calendar.

examples.english: I'm especially busy this week.
See you next week!

words.tip: The everyday spoken twin of 星期, originally 'worship' (the church week). 礼拜三 = Wednesday, 礼拜天 = Sunday. There is also the more formal 周: 周三, 下周.

examples.english: What time do you usually get up?

examples.text: 我平时不喝酒，今天喝一点儿。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ píngshí bù hē jiǔ, jīntiān hē yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: I don't normally drink, but today I'll have a little.

words.tip: 'Ordinary times', as opposed to weekends, holidays or special occasions. It goes after the subject and before the verb.

examples.english: On weekdays I get up at six.

examples.text: 这个饭馆工作日人不多。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fànguǎn gōngzuòrì rén bù duō.
examples.english: This restaurant isn't busy on weekdays.

words.tip: 工作 + 日 (the formal word for day). China sometimes moves working days onto a weekend to build a longer holiday (调休): explain how that works.

examples.text: 我今天一整天都在开会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yì zhěngtiān dōu zài kāihuì.
examples.english: I've been in meetings all day today.
Don't stare at your phone all day!

words.tip: 整 = whole. Often followed by 都. As a complaint it means 'constantly': 他整天玩游戏. One whole day = 一整天.

examples.english: Where shall we go on Sunday?
I don't work on Sundays.

words.tip: The one day without a number: 天 instead of 七. Also 星期日 in writing, and 礼拜天 or 周日. Never 星期七!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān hěn lǎn, bù xiǎng zuòfàn.
examples.english: I'm lazy today and don't feel like cooking.
You're so lazy!

words.tip: Third tone, dipping low. 懒得 + verb = can't be bothered to: 我懒得出去. A lazybones is a 懒虫 (lazy bug) or 懒猪 (lazy pig), both said fondly between couples.

words.gloss: to sleep in, to have a lie-in

examples.english: At the weekend I like to sleep in.

examples.text: 明天不上班，可以睡懒觉。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān bú shàngbān, kěyǐ shuì lǎnjiào.
examples.english: No work tomorrow, so we can sleep in.

words.tip: 'To sleep a lazy sleep': 睡觉 with 懒 slipped into the middle. 觉 is jiào here, but jué in 觉得.

examples.text: 周末应该好好放松一下。
examples.english: At the weekend you should have a proper rest.
Don't be nervous, relax!

words.tip: 'To let loose', the opposite of 紧张. 好好 + verb = to do it properly. Say 放松! to a nervous partner before an exam or an interview.

examples.english: This job is easy-going.

examples.text: 和你在一起我觉得很轻松。
examples.pinyin: Hé nǐ zài yìqǐ wǒ juéde hěn qīngsōng.
examples.english: I feel at ease when I'm with you.

words.tip: 'Light and loose'. 放松 is what you do; 轻松 is how it feels. A 轻松的工作 is a low-stress job, a 轻松的电影 an easy film.

examples.pinyin: Hūnlǐ de rìqī dìng le ma?
examples.english: Has the wedding date been fixed?

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ xiě shàng rìqī.
examples.english: Please write the date here.

words.tip: The calendar date. Chinese dates run from big to small: 年, 月, then 号 (or 日 in writing): 五月三号. A date with your partner is 约会, not 日期.

examples.pinyin: Hòutiān shì wǒ māma de shēngrì.
examples.english: The day after tomorrow is my mum's birthday.
I won't have time until the day after tomorrow.

words.tip: The 'day behind'. In Chinese the future lies behind you (后) and the past in front (前): 后天, 前天. One step further: 大后天, in three days.

examples.english: We had dumplings the day before yesterday.
Why didn't you come the day before yesterday?

words.tip: The 'day in front'. Have your partner recite the row: 前天, 昨天, 今天, 明天, 后天. Years work the same way: 前年, 去年, 今年, 明年, 后年.

examples.english: By the end of the month I'm out of money.
Our company pays wages at the end of the month.

words.tip: The 'bottom' of the month; the start is 月初. Likewise 年底 (the end of the year). 发工资 = to pay out wages.

examples.english: Have a look at the calendar.

examples.text: 中国的日历上有两种日期。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó de rìlì shang yǒu liǎng zhǒng rìqī.
examples.english: Chinese calendars show two kinds of date.

words.tip: Show a Chinese calendar with both systems: the ordinary one (公历 or 阳历) and the lunar one (农历 or 阴历), which sets Spring Festival and many people's birthdays.

examples.english: The train is on time.
Please arrive on time tomorrow.

words.tip: 'Accurate time'; 准 is the same as in 准备. Before a verb it means punctually: 准时到, 准时下班. Germans are 很准时, says the stereotype: is it true of your partner?

words.gloss: to be in time, to still have time (to)

examples.english: There are still ten minutes, we'll make it.

examples.text: 我们现在走还来得及吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiànzài zǒu hái láidejí ma?
examples.english: If we leave now, will we still make it?

words.tip: 'Able to come and reach it'. For the opposite, 得 becomes 不: 来不及 = it's too late: 来不及吃早饭了. A verb can follow: 来得及吃饭.

examples.english: The match has been postponed until tomorrow.

examples.text: 我们可以推迟一个星期吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kěyǐ tuīchí yí ge xīngqī ma?
examples.english: Can we put it off for a week?

words.tip: 'To push late': 迟 is the same as in 迟到. 推迟到 + the new time, or 推迟 + how long. Opposite: 提前.

words.gloss: in advance, early; to bring forward

examples.english: I can finish work early today.
Please tell me in advance.

words.tip: 'To lift forward'. Mostly in front of another verb: 提前到, 提前订票. 提前十分钟 = ten minutes early. Opposite: 推迟.

examples.english: How have you been lately?
I've been working a lot of overtime lately.

words.tip: 'Most near' in time: the recent past up to now, and sometimes the near future (最近要下雨). 你最近怎么样? is the standard greeting for someone you haven't seen in a while.

examples.text: 我每天早上吃一根香蕉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang chī yì gēn xiāngjiāo.
examples.english: I eat a banana every morning.

examples.pinyin: Xiāngjiāo fàng zài zhuōzi shang le.
examples.english: The bananas are on the table.

words.tip: The 'fragrant banana'. Counted with 根, like other long, thin things. x and j are said with a flat, smiling mouth.

examples.english: These strawberries are so sweet!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yì jīn cǎoméi.
examples.english: I'd like to buy half a kilo of strawberries.

words.tip: A 'grass berry'. At the market fruit is sold by the 斤 (half a kilo). 草莓 is also slang for a love bite.

examples.english: Nothing beats eating watermelon in summer.

examples.pinyin: Zhège xīguā duōshao qián yì jīn?
examples.english: How much is this watermelon per half kilo?

words.tip: The 'western melon', which came along the Silk Road. The fruit of the Chinese summer; a slice is 一块西瓜. 瓜 is in many names: 黄瓜 (cucumber), 南瓜 (pumpkin).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì zuò xīhóngshì chǎo jīdàn.
examples.english: I can make stir-fried tomato and egg.

examples.text: 西红柿是水果还是蔬菜？
examples.english: Is a tomato a fruit or a vegetable?

words.tip: A 'western red persimmon'; in the south it's 番茄 (fānqié). 西红柿炒鸡蛋 is the first dish every Chinese student learns: cook it together.

examples.pinyin: Déguó rén hěn xǐhuan chī tǔdòu.
examples.english: Germans love eating potatoes.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bāng wǒ qiē yíxià tǔdòu.
examples.english: Help me cut up the potatoes.

words.tip: An 'earth bean', much like German Erdapfel. In Chinese cooking it's a vegetable dish, not the side: make 土豆丝 (stir-fried shredded potato).

examples.english: Add a little more soy sauce.

examples.pinyin: Jiā li de jiàngyóu yòng wán le.
examples.english: We've used up the soy sauce at home.

words.tip: 'Sauce oil', though there's no oil in it. Light 生抽 is for seasoning, dark 老抽 for colour. 打酱油 ('just out buying soy sauce') is slang for 'nothing to do with me'.

examples.english: You need vinegar with dumplings.

examples.pinyin: Zhège cài cù tài duō le.
examples.english: There's too much vinegar in this dish.

words.tip: c = ts with a puff of air, fourth tone. Dark rice vinegar goes with dumplings and noodles. You know it already from 吃醋, to be jealous.

examples.pinyin: Guō li xiān fàng yìdiǎnr yóu.
examples.english: First put a little oil in the pan.

examples.pinyin: Shǎo fàng yóu, duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Use less oil, it's better for you.

words.tip: Cooking oil, and also petrol: 加油 is 'add fuel', hence 'come on!'. 少 + verb = do less of it: 少放油, 少喝酒. Greasy food is 油腻.

examples.english: I can't eat chilli.

examples.pinyin: Zhège cài li yǒu hěn duō làjiāo.
examples.english: There's a lot of chilli in this dish.

words.tip: The 'spicy pepper'. 椒 names the whole family: 胡椒 (black pepper), 青椒 (green pepper), 花椒 (numbing Sichuan pepper). In a restaurant: 不要辣椒 = no chilli, please.

examples.pinyin: Gǎnmào le hē yìdiǎnr jiāng chá.
examples.english: When you have a cold, drink some ginger tea.
You need ginger when you cook fish.

words.tip: With 葱 (spring onion) and 蒜 (garlic) it forms the trio that starts most Chinese dishes. Ginger counts as 'warming': 姜茶 is the home cure for colds.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chī yí kuài dàngāo.
examples.english: I'd like a piece of cake.

examples.text: 这个蛋糕是我自己做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dàngāo shì wǒ zìjǐ zuò de.
examples.english: I made this cake myself.

words.tip: An 'egg cake'. A whole cake is 一个蛋糕, a slice 一块. A 生日蛋糕 is standard for birthdays now. Many Chinese find German cake very sweet: ask.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào bu yào chī qiǎokèlì?
examples.english: Do you want some chocolate?

examples.text: 我给你带了德国的巧克力。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ dài le Déguó de qiǎokèlì.
examples.english: I've brought you some German chocolate.

words.tip: A sound loan: say it fast and you hear 'chocolate'. The characters are chosen for their sound alone. German chocolate is a welcome present for Chinese relatives.

examples.text: 天气这么热，吃冰淇淋吧。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì zhème rè, chī bīngqílín ba.
examples.english: It's so hot, let's have ice cream.

examples.text: 我要一个巧克力冰淇淋。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào yí ge qiǎokèlì bīngqílín.
examples.english: I'll have a chocolate ice cream.

words.tip: Half meaning, half sound: 冰 (ice) plus 淇淋 for 'cream'. Also written 冰激凌. An ice lolly is a 冰棍儿.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ è le, yǒu bǐnggān ma?
examples.english: I'm hungry, are there any biscuits?

examples.pinyin: Háizi bǎ bǐnggān dōu chī wán le.
examples.english: The child has eaten all the biscuits.

words.tip: A 'dry cake'. 饼 is anything flat and round made of dough: 月饼 (mooncake), 煎饼 (savoury pancake). One biscuit is 一块, a packet 一包.

examples.text: 看电影的时候我喜欢吃零食。
examples.pinyin: Kàn diànyǐng de shíhou wǒ xǐhuan chī língshí.
examples.english: I like eating snacks while watching a film.

examples.text: 别吃太多零食，快吃饭了。
examples.pinyin: Bié chī tài duō língshí, kuài chī fàn le.
examples.english: Don't eat too many snacks, dinner's nearly ready.

words.tip: 'Odd-bits food': crisps, nuts, sweets, dried fruit, anything eaten between meals. Chinese supermarkets have whole aisles of it. Swap your favourites.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān guā fēng, duō chuān yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: It's windy today, wrap up warm.

examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn yòu guā fēng yòu xià yǔ.
examples.english: It's windy and rainy outside.

words.tip: Weather is verb + object in Chinese: 刮风, 下雨, 下雪. A strong wind is 刮大风. 又…又… = both… and…

examples.english: Listen, it's thundering!

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā de gǒu hěn pà dǎ léi.
examples.english: Our dog is very scared of thunder.

words.tip: 'To strike thunder'. Lightning is 闪电. The character 雷 is rain 雨 over a field 田.

examples.english: What's the temperature today?

examples.pinyin: Fángjiān li de wēndù tài gāo le.
examples.english: The temperature in the room is too high.

words.tip: 'Warm degree'. A temperature is 高 or 低 (low), not hot or cold. The weather report says 气温; body temperature is 体温.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān sānshí dù, tài rè le!
examples.english: It's thirty degrees today, far too hot!
It's only two degrees outside.

words.tip: Number + 度, nothing in between; two degrees is 两度. Below zero is 零下: 零下五度. Also the strength of alcohol: 这个酒多少度?

examples.pinyin: Tiānqì yùbào shuō míngtiān xià xuě.
examples.english: The forecast says it will snow tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn tiānqì yùbào le ma?
examples.english: Have you seen the weather forecast?

words.tip: A 'weather advance-report'. 天气预报说… = the forecast says…, a handy way to open a sentence.

examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn lěng, chuān shàng wàitào ba.
examples.english: It's cold outside, put your jacket on.
This jacket is a bit big.

words.tip: An 'outer cover': any jacket or coat worn on top. A long coat is a 大衣, a down jacket a 羽绒服. Every Chinese parent's line: 多穿点儿!

examples.pinyin: Tā chuān bái chènshān hěn shuài.
examples.english: He looks handsome in a white shirt.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn chènshān shì gěi nǐ mǎi de.
examples.english: I bought this shirt for you.

words.tip: A shirt with buttons and a collar, for men or women. A T-shirt is a T恤. Both characters have the clothes radical 衤 on the left.

examples.text: 她今天穿了一条红裙子。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān chuān le yì tiáo hóng qúnzi.
examples.english: She's wearing a red skirt today.

examples.text: 这条裙子是在网上买的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi shì zài wǎngshang mǎi de.
examples.english: I bought this skirt online.

words.tip: A skirt; a dress is properly a 连衣裙 ('joined-top skirt'), but 裙子 is often used for both. Counted with 条, like trousers. The u after q is ü: qún.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn máoyī shì māma sòng de.
examples.english: This jumper was a present from my mum.

examples.pinyin: Tiān lěng le, yào chuān máoyī le.
examples.english: It's turned cold, time to wear a jumper.

words.tip: 'Wool clothing'. 毛 is hair, fur and wool, and also the spoken word for a tenth of a yuan. A hand-knitted 毛衣 from mum is a classic.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎo bu dào wǒ de wàzi le.
examples.english: I can't find my socks.
These socks are cute.

words.tip: A pair is 一双袜子, a single sock 一只. 找不到 = can't find. Socks make a fine present; clocks and shoes don't: explain the gift taboos.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī zài bāo li.
examples.english: My phone is in my bag.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bāo shì xīn mǎi de ma?
examples.english: Is this bag new?

words.tip: Any bag: 书包 (school bag), 钱包 (wallet), 背包 (backpack). As a verb it means to wrap: 包饺子 = to make dumplings. Also a packet of something: 一包饼干.

examples.english: He looks good in glasses.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng huàn yí fù xīn yǎnjìng.
examples.english: I'd like to get a new pair of glasses.

words.tip: An 'eye mirror'. Mind the tones: yǎnjìng (glasses) against yǎnjing (眼睛, eye). Worn with 戴, not 穿. Sunglasses: 太阳镜 or 墨镜.

examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng hěn dà, dài shàng màozi ba.
examples.english: The sun is strong, put a hat on.

examples.pinyin: Zhè dǐng màozi shì shéi de?
examples.english: Whose hat is this?

words.tip: Any hat or cap, worn with 戴. Its measure word 顶 means 'top'. One taboo: never give a man a green hat. 戴绿帽子 means his partner is cheating on him.

examples.text: 我给妈妈买了一条围巾。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi māma mǎi le yì tiáo wéijīn.
examples.english: I bought my mum a scarf.
In winter you need a scarf when you go out.

words.tip: A 'wrap-around cloth'. 巾 is a piece of cloth: 毛巾 (towel), 纸巾 (tissue). Worn with 戴, or 围 for wrapping it round.

examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, nǐ dài sǎn le ma?
examples.english: It's raining, did you bring an umbrella?

examples.text: 我们两个人用一把伞吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎng ge rén yòng yì bǎ sǎn ba.
examples.english: Let's share one umbrella between the two of us.

words.tip: The character looks like an open umbrella. Also 雨伞. In China it's used against the sun as much as the rain. Don't give one as a present: 伞 sounds like 散, to split up.

examples.english: This top fits well.

examples.pinyin: Zhège shíjiān duì nǐ héshì ma?
examples.english: Does this time suit you?

words.tip: An adjective, so nothing follows it: 这件很合适. The verb is 适合, with the characters flipped: 这件衣服很适合你. For sizes, times, jobs and partners.

words.gloss: size; number; day of the month

examples.pinyin: Nǐ chuān duō dà hào de xié?
examples.english: What size shoes do you wear?

examples.pinyin: Yǒu méiyǒu xiǎo yí hào de?
examples.english: Do you have it one size smaller?

words.tip: A number in a series: clothes sizes (大号, 中号, 小号), the date (五月三号), bus lines and room numbers. It's the 号 of 号码 and 挂号. 小一号 = one size smaller.

examples.text: 这件衬衫太紧了，换一件吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn chènshān tài jǐn le, huàn yí jiàn ba.
examples.english: This shirt is too tight, let's try another one.
The shoes are a bit tight and uncomfortable.

words.tip: The first half of 紧张: nerves pulled tight. Tight clothes, a tight schedule (时间很紧), and money being tight. Opposite: 松.

examples.text: 这件有点儿松，有小号的吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yǒudiǎnr sōng, yǒu xiǎo hào de ma?
examples.english: This one is a bit loose, do you have a small?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shòu le, kùzi dōu sōng le.
examples.english: I've lost weight and my trousers have gone loose.

words.tip: Loose or slack, the opposite of 紧. You met it in 放松 and 轻松. The same character also means pine tree (松树).

examples.english: Can I return it if it doesn't fit?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ zhè shuāng xié tuì le.
examples.english: I'd like to return this pair of shoes.

words.tip: To give back and undo: 退货 (return goods), 退钱 (refund), 退票 (cancel a ticket), 退房 (check out of a hotel). Swapping it for another is 换.

examples.english: Your parcel has arrived.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xià lóu qù ná yí ge kuàidì.
examples.english: I'm going downstairs to fetch a parcel.

words.tip: 'Fast handover': the courier service and the parcel itself. 寄快递 = to send one, 拿快递 = to fetch one. Delivery in China is astonishingly fast and cheap: tell a story about it.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yīfu dōu shì wǎnggòu de.
examples.english: All my clothes were bought online.

examples.text: 你喜欢网购还是去商店？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan wǎnggòu háishi qù shāngdiàn?
examples.english: Do you prefer shopping online or going to the shops?

words.tip: Short for 网上购物; 网 is the net of 上网. Explain 双十一 (Singles' Day, 11 November), the biggest online sale in the world.

words.gloss: to give a discount, to be reduced

examples.english: Are these shoes reduced?

examples.text: 今天所有的衣服都打折。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān suǒyǒu de yīfu dōu dǎzhé.
examples.english: All clothes are reduced today.

words.tip: Careful: Chinese states what you PAY, not what comes off. 打八折 = you pay eighty per cent, so it's twenty per cent off. 打五折 = half price.

words.gloss: to receive; to accept, to collect

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shōudào wǒ de yóujiàn le ma?
examples.english: Did you get my email?
They don't take cash here.

words.tip: 收到 = to have received; 收到! on its own is a brisk 'got it!' at work. 收钱 = to take payment. The opposite of 发 (to send).

examples.pinyin: Bǎ nǐ de dìzhǐ fā gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Send me your address.
Is this address right?

words.tip: Chinese addresses run from big to small: country, province, city, street, number, flat, and the name last. The exact reverse of a German address: write yours both ways.

examples.english: Can I use a credit card here?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xìnyòngkǎ bú jiàn le!
examples.english: My credit card has gone missing!

words.tip: 信用 = credit, trustworthiness; 卡 is the sound of 'card'. A bank card is a 银行卡. Foreign credit cards often don't work in China, where almost everyone pays by phone. 不见了 = has disappeared.

words.gloss: to withdraw, to fetch, to collect

examples.text: 我没有现金了，要去取钱。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu xiànjīn le, yào qù qǔ qián.
examples.english: I'm out of cash and need to take some out.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de piào qǔ le ma?
examples.english: Have you collected your ticket?

words.tip: To go and get something that's waiting for you: 取钱 (withdraw cash), 取票 (collect tickets), 取快递. The u after q is ü: pucker your lips, third tone.

words.gloss: to deposit; to save (up); to store

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi ge yuè cún yìdiǎnr qián.
examples.english: I put a little money aside every month.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ qián cún zài nǎge yínháng?
examples.english: Which bank do you keep your money in?

words.tip: 存钱 = to save up, or to pay money in; the opposite of 取. Also to store: 存行李 (leave luggage), 存号码 (save a number). c = ts with a puff of air.

words.gloss: to pay by card, to swipe a card

examples.text: 我没带现金，可以刷卡吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méi dài xiànjīn, kěyǐ shuākǎ ma?
examples.english: I've no cash on me, can I pay by card?

examples.pinyin: Zuò dìtiě shuākǎ jiù kěyǐ le.
examples.english: On the metro you just swipe your card.

words.tip: 'To brush the card', the same 刷 as in 刷牙. For paying, entering the metro or opening the office door. 刷手机 = to scroll on your phone.

examples.english: Please scan the code to pay.

examples.text: 在中国买菜也可以扫码。
examples.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó mǎi cài yě kěyǐ sǎomǎ.
examples.english: In China you can even scan a code to buy vegetables.

words.tip: 'Sweep the code': how China pays, orders food, hires bikes and adds friends. The code itself is a 二维码. Show your partner how 微信支付 or 支付宝 works before a trip.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kāichē sòng nǐ qù jīchǎng.
examples.english: I'll drive you to the airport.

examples.pinyin: Hē le jiǔ bù néng kāichē.
examples.english: You can't drive after drinking.

words.tip: Verb + object: 开了三个小时的车 = drove for three hours. Driving somewhere is 开车去: 我开车去上班. 会, not 能, for the learned skill.

words.gloss: to park; to stop the car

examples.english: Can I park here?

examples.pinyin: Zài zhège chéngshì tíngchē hěn guì.
examples.english: Parking is expensive in this city.

words.tip: A car park is a 停车场, a single space a 停车位. 停 alone is to stop: 雨停了 = the rain has stopped; 停电 = a power cut.

words.gloss: to be jammed with traffic; traffic jam

examples.text: 路上堵车，我会晚一点儿到。
examples.pinyin: Lùshang dǔchē, wǒ huì wǎn yìdiǎnr dào.
examples.english: There's a traffic jam, I'll be a bit late.
There are traffic jams in Beijing every day.

words.tip: 'Blocked cars', used as a verb: 堵车了! The most widely accepted excuse for being late in any Chinese city. 堵 alone: 路很堵.

examples.english: There's a petrol station up ahead.
Let's go to the petrol station first.

words.tip: An 'add-fuel station'. Here 加油 is literal; shouted at a match it means 'come on!'. 站 ends many stops and stations: 车站, 地铁站.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qùnián ná dào le jiàzhào.
examples.english: I got my driving licence last year.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu Zhōngguó de jiàzhào ma?
examples.english: Do you have a Chinese driving licence?

words.tip: Short for 驾驶执照. 考驾照 = to take the driving test. A German licence isn't valid in China: you need a Chinese one, which means passing a theory test.

words.gloss: to get on (a bus, train, car)

characters.meaning: to get on, to go up

examples.english: Quick, get in, we're leaving!
Where do we get on?

words.tip: 上 as a verb: to go up, to board. For anything on wheels; boarding a plane is 上飞机. The same 上 starts 上班, 上网 and 上学.

words.gloss: to get off (a bus, train, car)

characters.meaning: to get off, to go down

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài xià yí zhàn xiàchē.
examples.english: I'm getting off at the next stop.
We're here, let's get off.

words.tip: 下 as a verb: to go down, to get off. In 下一站 (the next stop) it's the other 下, 'next'. On a crowded bus, ask 你下车吗? to work your way to the door.

examples.text: 我们坐出租车去机场吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò chūzūchē qù jīchǎng ba.
examples.english: Let's take a taxi to the airport.
There are very few taxis at this hour.

words.tip: A 'rent-out car'. In Taiwan it's a 计程车, in the south also a 的士. Address the driver as 师傅 (shīfu), 'master'.

words.gloss: to take a taxi, to hail a ride

examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ de shíhou hěn nán dǎchē.
examples.english: It's hard to get a taxi when it rains.
Ordering a ride by phone is quick.

words.tip: 打 is the do-anything verb: 打电话, 打车, 打折. Nowadays it mostly means ordering a ride by app (滴滴). 打的 (dǎ dī) means the same.

examples.pinyin: Qù jīchǎng yào zuò jǐ hào xiàn?
examples.english: Which line do I take to the airport?

examples.pinyin: Èr hào xiàn rén tài duō le.
examples.english: Line two is far too crowded.

words.tip: Metro lines are number + 号线: 一号线, 二号线. Also thread, wire and cable: 电线 (power cable), 在线 (online), 无线 (wireless).

examples.english: The sun comes up in the east.
Shanghai is in the east of China.

words.tip: In speech it needs a partner: 东边 (the east side), 东方 (the East), 东北 (the north-east). Chinese recites the directions as 东南西北. And 东西, 'east-west', is a thing!

examples.english: I'm from the south.
The rooms on the south side are brighter.

words.tip: 南方 = the south of China: rice, humidity, no central heating. 南方人 and 北方人 tease each other about food and height. A flat facing south (朝南) is prized.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài chéngshì de xībian.
examples.english: My home is in the west of the city.

examples.text: 西方人和中国人有什么不一样？
examples.pinyin: Xīfāng rén hé Zhōngguó rén yǒu shénme bù yíyàng?
examples.english: What's different about Westerners and Chinese people?

words.tip: 西方 = the West (Europe and America); 西餐 = Western food; 西医 = Western medicine. You met it in 西瓜 and 西红柿, things that arrived from the west.

examples.english: Winters in the north are extremely cold.

examples.pinyin: Wǎng běi zǒu wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
examples.english: Walk north for five minutes and you're there.

words.tip: 北京 is the 'northern capital', 南京 the southern one. In northern cities people give directions by compass: 往北走. Chinese puts east and west first: 东北 (north-east), 西南 (south-west).

examples.english: We've gone in the wrong direction.
Which direction is the metro station?

words.tip: 方 is the 'side' in 东方, 南方 and 对方. Someone with no sense of direction is a 路痴, a 'road fool': which of you is it?

examples.text: 这辆公交车经过火车站吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng gōngjiāochē jīngguò huǒchēzhàn ma?
examples.english: Does this bus go past the railway station?

examples.text: 我每天上班都经过这个公园。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān shàngbān dōu jīngguò zhège gōngyuán.
examples.english: I pass this park every day on my way to work.

words.tip: To go past a place on the way somewhere else. 过 keeps its tone here (guò, to cross), unlike the toneless 过 of experience. Also 'after going through': 经过这件事…

examples.english: The bank is opposite the supermarket.

examples.pinyin: Duìmiàn nàge rén nǐ rènshi ma?
examples.english: Do you know that person across from us?

words.tip: The 'facing side'. Like other place words it comes after the landmark: 学校对面 = opposite the school; 我对面 = across from me.

examples.english: Is there a pharmacy nearby?

examples.text: 我家附近有一个很大的公园。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā fùjìn yǒu yí ge hěn dà de gōngyuán.
examples.english: There's a big park near my home.

words.tip: The neighbourhood around a point: 学校附近 = near the school; alone, 'around here'. The first question in any new city: 附近有…吗?

examples.english: It's very quiet around our home.

examples.pinyin: Zhōuwéi de rén dōu zài kàn wǒmen.
examples.english: Everyone around is looking at us.

words.tip: All around, in a circle; 附近 is merely near. 周围的人 = the people around you. 周 is the cycle in 周末, and 围 wraps round in 围巾.

examples.text: 这是我们两个人之间的事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen liǎng ge rén zhījiān de shì.
examples.english: This is between the two of us.

examples.text: 八点到九点之间我在家。
examples.pinyin: Bā diǎn dào jiǔ diǎn zhījiān wǒ zài jiā.
examples.english: I'm at home between eight and nine.

words.tip: It follows what it links: A 和 B 之间, for places, times and people. 我们之间 = between us. 中间 is the physical middle; 之间 is about the relation.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ tuī yíxià chē.
examples.english: Please help me push the car.
Don't push me!

words.tip: On doors: 推 (push) and 拉 (pull). You know it from 推迟, 'to push late'. The 扌 on the left is the hand radical, found in most hand actions.

examples.pinyin: Zhège mén yào lā, bú yào tuī.
examples.english: You pull this door, you don't push it.
Come on, pull me up!

words.tip: 拉手 = to hold hands, more casual than 牵手. 拉面 are 'pulled' noodles: ramen. And, bluntly, 拉肚子 = to have diarrhoea, worth knowing when you travel.

examples.english: Throw me the keys!

examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōngxi hái yǒu yòng, bié rēng.
examples.english: These things are still useful, don't throw them out.

words.tip: To throw, and to throw away: 扔垃圾. 扔给我 = throw it to me. The r is like English r with the tongue curled back; eng as in 'sung'.

words.gloss: to fall, to drop; to lose

examples.english: You've dropped something.

examples.text: 我的手机掉在出租车上了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī diào zài chūzūchē shang le.
examples.english: I left my phone in the taxi.

words.tip: Something falls or gets lost: 手机掉了. After another verb it means 'away, off': 扔掉 (throw away), 忘掉 (forget completely), 吃掉 (eat up). Losing hair is 掉头发.

words.gloss: to jump; (of the heart) to beat

examples.english: How high can you jump?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xīn tiào de hěn kuài.
examples.english: My heart is beating fast.

words.tip: To jump or hop, and for a heart to beat: 心跳 = heartbeat. You know it from 跳舞. 吓我一跳! = you made me jump!

examples.pinyin: Nǐ wén, shénme dōngxi zhème xiāng?
examples.english: Smell that: what is it that smells so good?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, wén bu dào wèidào.
examples.english: I've got a cold and can't smell anything.

words.tip: To smell with your nose: 闻一下 = have a sniff; 闻到 = to notice a smell. The character is an ear 耳 in a doorway 门: it once meant 'to hear', as in 新闻 (news).

words.gloss: to touch, to feel, to stroke

examples.text: 我可以摸一下你的狗吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ mō yíxià nǐ de gǒu ma?
examples.english: May I stroke your dog?

examples.pinyin: Bié mō, nàge pánzi hěn rè!
examples.english: Don't touch, that plate is hot!

words.tip: To feel something with your hand: 摸一下 = have a feel. First tone, held high and level. A mother checks for fever with 摸摸头.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò de cài zhēn xiāng!
examples.english: Your cooking smells wonderful!
These flowers smell lovely.

words.tip: For food, flowers and perfume (香水). Say 好香啊! as soon as you walk into the kitchen. 睡得很香 = to sleep soundly. 香港 is the 'fragrant harbour'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de wàzi tài chòu le!
examples.english: Your socks stink!

examples.text: 臭豆腐很臭，但是很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Chòu dòufu hěn chòu, dànshì hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: Stinky tofu smells awful, but it's delicious.

words.tip: The opposite of 香. 臭豆腐 (stinky tofu) is the test of courage for visitors: 闻着臭，吃着香, smells bad, tastes great.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ tài chǎo le, wǒ tīng bu jiàn.
examples.english: It's too noisy here, I can't hear.

examples.text: 小声一点儿，别吵到邻居。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo shēng yìdiǎnr, bié chǎo dào línjū.
examples.english: Keep it down, don't disturb the neighbours.

words.tip: Noisy, and to bother someone with noise: 别吵! = be quiet! It's the first half of 吵架. Pleasant bustle is 热闹; 吵 is the unwelcome kind.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng chuáng tài ruǎn le.
examples.english: This bed is too soft.

examples.text: 我喜欢吃软一点儿的米饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī ruǎn yìdiǎnr de mǐfàn.
examples.english: I like my rice a bit softer.

words.tip: Soft to the touch or to the bite. 心软 = soft-hearted, unable to say no. It's the 'soft' in 软件, software. Opposite: 硬.

examples.text: 面包放了三天，已经硬了。
examples.pinyin: Miànbāo fàng le sān tiān, yǐjīng yìng le.
examples.english: The bread has been lying around for three days and has gone hard.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ yǐzi tài yìng, bù shūfu.
examples.english: This chair is too hard and uncomfortable.

words.tip: Hard, stiff, firm. Hardware is 硬件; a hard seat on a train is a 硬座. 嘴硬 ('hard mouth') = never admitting you're wrong.

examples.pinyin: Xià xuě le, lù hěn huá.
examples.english: It has snowed and the road is slippery.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, xǐshǒujiān de dì hěn huá.
examples.english: Careful, the bathroom floor is slippery.

words.tip: Slippery floors, smooth skin, silky tofu. As a verb, to slide: 滑雪 (to ski), 滑冰 (to skate). The sign 小心地滑 means 'caution, slippery floor'.

examples.english: This book is really thick!

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān hěn lěng, chuān hòu yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: It's cold today, wear something thicker.

words.tip: For flat things and layers: books, walls, coats, quilts. Thick for round things like legs is 粗. 脸皮厚 ('thick face-skin') = shameless. Opposite: 薄.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài báo, huì lěng de.
examples.english: This top is too thin, you'll be cold.

examples.pinyin: Ròu yào qiē de báo yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: The meat needs to be sliced a bit thinner.

words.tip: Thin for flat things: paper, clothes, slices, phones. A thin person is 瘦, a thin stick 细. Said báo in everyday speech; in some formal compounds it's bó.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān kàn qǐlái hěn lèi.
examples.english: You look very tired today.

examples.pinyin: Zhège cài kàn qǐlái hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: This dish looks delicious.

words.tip: Verb + 起来 gives an impression: 看起来 (looks), 听起来 (sounds), 吃起来 (tastes), 闻起来 (smells). The judgment follows directly, usually with 很. In fluent speech 起来 is toneless.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīngshuō nǐ yào jiéhūn le.
examples.english: I hear you're getting married.
I've heard that restaurant is pretty good.

words.tip: 'Hear-say': news that reached you second hand. It opens the sentence or follows the subject, with no word for 'that'. 听说过 = to have heard of: 我听说过他.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhǎng de hěn xiàng nǐ māma.
examples.english: You look a lot like your mum.
He talks like a child.

words.tip: A 像 B = A is like B; 很像 = very like. 长得像 = to look like, in face and build. You know it from 好像. 像…一样 = just like…: 像家一样.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan nǐ xiào de yàngzi.
examples.english: I love the way you look when you smile.

examples.pinyin: Tā hái shì yǐqián de yàngzi.
examples.english: He still looks the way he used to.

words.tip: How someone or something looks or acts. 看样子 = by the look of it: 看样子要下雨. 样 is the 'shape' in 一样, 怎么样 and 这样.

words.gloss: good-looking, nice to look at; good (film, book)

examples.pinyin: Nǐ chuān zhè tiáo qúnzi hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: You look lovely in this skirt.

examples.text: 这本书很好看，你也看看吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū hěn hǎokàn, nǐ yě kànkan ba.
examples.english: This book is really good, you should read it too.

words.tip: 好 + verb = pleasant to do: 好看 (to look at), 好听 (to hear), 好吃 (to eat), 好玩 (fun). A relaxed compliment for men and women alike, and the word for a good film or book.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi ge zhōumò dōu qù páshān.
examples.english: I go hiking every weekend.

examples.pinyin: Měi ge rén dōu xǐhuan tā.
examples.english: Everybody likes him.

words.tip: 每 + measure word + noun, and 都 nearly always follows: 每个人都…, 每次都… 天 and 年 take no measure word: 每天, 每年. Doubling does the same job: 天天, 人人.

examples.text: 有任何问题都可以问我。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rènhé wèntí dōu kěyǐ wèn wǒ.
examples.english: If you have any questions at all, you can ask me.

examples.text: 这件事不要告诉任何人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì bú yào gàosu rènhé rén.
examples.english: Don't tell anyone about this.

words.tip: 'No matter which'. No measure word is needed: 任何人, 任何时候, 任何地方. With 都 it's 'any at all'; in a negative sentence, 'not a single one'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de qián quánbù huā wán le.
examples.english: I've spent every last bit of my money.

examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē quánbù shì nǐ zuò de ma?
examples.english: Did you make all of these?

words.tip: Every last bit, with nothing left over. 所有的 goes before a noun (所有的人); 全部 sums up afterwards. 全 alone also works before a verb: 全忘了.

examples.english: The supermarket has all kinds of fruit.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan shì gèzhǒng xīn dōngxi.
examples.english: I like trying all sorts of new things.

words.tip: 'Each kind'. Straight before the noun: 各种颜色. The long form 各种各样的 means every sort imaginable. 各位 = everyone, as a polite way to address a group.

examples.english: When are the others arriving?

examples.text: 我只要这个，其他的不要。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ yào zhège, qítā de bú yào.
examples.english: I only want this one, not the rest.

words.tip: The remaining ones of a known group: 其他人, 其他的. 别的 leans towards 'something else, something different'; often either will do. 其 is the same as in 其实.

examples.english: We should help each other.
They aren't speaking to each other.

words.tip: It goes before the verb: 互相学习, 互相了解. The two of you are doing 互相学习 right now. 相 alone does the same job in 相信 and 相爱.

words.gloss: the other person, the other side

examples.text: 我们要多听对方的意见。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào duō tīng duìfāng de yìjiàn.
examples.english: We should listen more to each other's opinions.

examples.text: 吵架的时候要想想对方的感觉。
examples.pinyin: Chǎojià de shíhou yào xiǎngxiang duìfāng de gǎnjué.
examples.english: When you argue, think about how the other one feels.

words.tip: The 'facing side': whoever you're dealing with, in love, on the phone or in a match. A good rule for couples: 多为对方想想, think more of the other one.

examples.english: Let's each pay for ourselves.

examples.text: 周末我们各自回父母家。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen gèzì huí fùmǔ jiā.
examples.english: At the weekend we each go to our own parents'.

words.tip: Each one separately; it follows the subject. Splitting the bill is also called AA: 我们AA吧. Among Chinese friends one person more often treats the rest: explain 请客.

words.gloss: other people; someone else; (coyly) I, me

examples.text: 你看人家的孩子多聪明！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn rénjia de háizi duō cōngming!
examples.english: Look how clever other people's children are!

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì rénjia de dōngxi, bié dòng.
examples.english: That belongs to someone else, don't touch it.

words.tip: Other people in general, or a certain someone you both know. Parents love 人家的孩子, 'other people's children', who are always better. In a coy voice it can even mean 'me': 人家不要嘛!

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎ dōu xǐhuan chī là de.
examples.english: We both like spicy food.
What's the relationship between those two?

words.tip: A fusion of 两个, so never add 个 after it: 我们俩, 你们俩, 他们俩. The natural word for couples and pairs of friends. 咱俩 = you and me.

examples.pinyin: Kuài zǒu ba, yàobùrán huì chídào.
examples.english: Let's go quickly, otherwise we'll be late.

examples.text: 多穿点儿，要不然会感冒的。
examples.pinyin: Duō chuān diǎnr, yàobùrán huì gǎnmào de.
examples.english: Put more on, or else you'll catch a cold.

words.tip: 'If not so'. The shorter forms 不然 and 要不 mean the same. 要不 also makes a gentle suggestion: 要不我们明天去? = how about we go tomorrow?

examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào nǐ gāoxìng, wǒ jiù gāoxìng.
examples.english: As long as you're happy, I'm happy.

examples.text: 只要有时间，我就去看你。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào yǒu shíjiān, wǒ jiù qù kàn nǐ.
examples.english: Whenever I have time, I'll come and see you.

words.tip: 只要 A, 就 B = as long as A, then B. The 就 in the second half is close to obligatory. A romantic favourite: 只要有你, as long as I have you.

examples.pinyin: Chúle nǐ, wǒ shéi dōu bù xiāngxìn.
examples.english: I don't trust anyone except you.

examples.text: 除了中文，你还会说什么语言？
examples.pinyin: Chúle Zhōngwén, nǐ hái huì shuō shénme yǔyán?
examples.english: What languages do you speak besides Chinese?

words.tip: The second half decides the meaning. With 都: except (除了他，大家都来了). With 还 or 也: in addition to (除了茶，我还喝咖啡). It's often rounded off with 以外.

examples.text: 另外，明天别忘了带护照。
examples.pinyin: Lìngwài, míngtiān bié wàng le dài hùzhào.
examples.english: Also, don't forget to bring your passport tomorrow.

examples.text: 我们换另外一个饭馆吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen huàn lìngwài yí ge fànguǎn ba.
examples.english: Let's go to a different restaurant.

words.tip: At the start of a sentence: 'also, one more thing', handy in emails and meetings. Before a number and measure word it means another: 另外一个, or just 另一个.

examples.text: 不管多忙，我都会给你打电话。
examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn duō máng, wǒ dōu huì gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: However busy I am, I'll always call you.

examples.text: 不管你去哪里，我都跟你去。
examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn nǐ qù nǎlǐ, wǒ dōu gēn nǐ qù.
examples.english: Wherever you go, I'll go with you.

words.tip: 不管 + a question word or a choice, then 都 in the second half: 不管谁, 不管怎么样, 不管贵不贵. As a verb it means not to bother about: 我不管! = I don't care!

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān yǒu kǎoshì, wǒ hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: There's an exam tomorrow and I'm nervous.

examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì nán bu nán?
examples.english: Was this exam hard?

words.tip: Noun and verb: 我明天考试. 考 alone is the verb in 考大学 and 考驾照. The 高考, the national university entrance exam, decides futures: tell your partner what it's like.

examples.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì yìzhí hěn hǎo.
examples.english: His marks have always been good.
Are the exam results out yet?

words.tip: Marks at school, and results at work or in sport. Chinese marks are usually out of a hundred (一百分), with sixty as the pass mark.

examples.pinyin: Zuòyè zuò wán le cái kěyǐ wán.
examples.english: You can only play once the homework is done.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de zuòyè tài duō le.
examples.english: There's too much homework today.

words.tip: 写作业 or 做作业 = to do homework; Chinese pupils get a great deal of it. Set your partner some 作业: three sentences with today's words.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàwǔ yǒu liǎng jié kè.
examples.english: I have two classes in the afternoon.

examples.text: 今天的中文课很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de Zhōngwén kè hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: Today's Chinese class was really interesting.

words.tip: One period is 一节课; a whole subject is 一门课. 上课 = to have or attend class; 下课 = class is over. A lesson in a textbook is also a 课: 第五课.

examples.english: I'm still a student.

examples.text: 他是老师最喜欢的学生。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì lǎoshī zuì xǐhuan de xuésheng.
examples.english: He's the teacher's favourite student.

words.tip: Anyone who studies, from primary school to doctorate: 小学生, 中学生, 大学生. A classmate is a 同学.

words.gloss: to have a job interview; job interview

examples.english: I'm going for a job interview tomorrow.
Don't be nervous during the interview.

words.tip: A 'face test'. Verb and noun: 参加面试 = to attend an interview. Practise the classic opening: 请介绍一下你自己.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ jiǎnlì fā gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Please send me your CV.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiǎnlì xiě hǎo le.
examples.english: My CV is finished.

words.tip: A 'brief history'. 投简历 = to send out CVs. Chinese CVs usually carry a photo and may state age and marital status: compare with yours.

examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu hěn duō gōngzuò jīngyàn.
examples.english: She has a lot of work experience.

examples.text: 我没有经验，但是我可以学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu jīngyàn, dànshì wǒ kěyǐ xué.
examples.english: I have no experience, but I can learn.

words.tip: Know-how gained by doing: 有经验 = experienced. Something you lived through once is a 经历 (jīnglì): don't mix the two up.

words.gloss: to resign, to quit one's job

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng cízhí, nǐ juéde ne?
examples.english: I'm thinking of resigning, what do you think?

examples.pinyin: Tā cízhí yǐhòu qù lǚxíng le.
examples.english: After he resigned he went travelling.

words.tip: To hand in your notice. Being fired is 被开除, or in slang 被炒鱿鱼, 'to be stir-fried like squid'. Changing jobs is 换工作, or 跳槽, 'to jump troughs'.

words.gloss: to go to work, to be at work

examples.pinyin: Nǐ měi tiān jǐ diǎn shàngbān?
examples.english: What time do you start work every day?
I don't have to work on Saturday.

words.tip: The partner of 下班. Both going to work and being there: 我在上班 = I'm at work. 上班族 = office workers. 不用 = don't need to.

examples.english: We did it!
I wish you success!

words.tip: Verb, noun and adjective in one: 成功了 (it worked), 很成功 (very successful). 失败是成功之母 = failure is the mother of success, a saying every Chinese schoolchild knows.

examples.text: 失败了没关系，再试一次。
examples.pinyin: Shībài le méi guānxi, zài shì yí cì.
examples.english: It doesn't matter if you fail, try once more.
I'm not afraid of failing.

words.tip: 'To lose and be beaten', for plans, attempts and businesses. You saw 失 in 失望. Failing an exam is rather 没考好 or 不及格.

examples.pinyin: Bú yào fàngqì, nǐ kěyǐ de!
examples.english: Don't give up, you can do it!
He gave up that opportunity.

words.tip: 'To let go and discard'. 别放弃! goes well with 加油! It takes an object: 放弃工作, 放弃机会. 你可以的 = you can do it.

words.gloss: to persist, to keep at it; to insist

examples.english: Learning a language takes perseverance.
I stick to running every day.

words.tip: 'To hold firm'. 坚持 + verb = to keep on doing it. 坚持一下! = hang in there! 坚持就是胜利 = to persist is to win. Also to insist: 他坚持要去.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de Zhōngwén jìnbù hěn dà.
examples.english: Your Chinese has improved a lot.
I feel I'm not making any progress.

words.tip: A 'step forward'. Progress is 'big' or 'fast': 进步很大, 进步很快. The best thing to tell your partner after a lesson: 你进步了!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiànyì nǐ zǎo yìdiǎnr qù.
examples.english: I suggest you go a bit earlier.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme hǎo jiànyì ma?
examples.english: Do you have any good suggestions?

words.tip: Verb and noun. 我建议你… is a polite way to give advice. As a noun it counts with 个 or 条: 给我一个建议.

examples.text: 你可以推荐一个好医生吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ tuījiàn yí ge hǎo yīshēng ma?
examples.english: Can you recommend a good doctor?

examples.pinyin: Péngyou tuījiàn wǒ kàn zhè běn shū.
examples.english: A friend recommended that I read this book.

words.tip: To 'push forward' something good: a restaurant, a book, a person for a job. In a restaurant: 有什么推荐的? = what do you recommend?

words.gloss: to urge, to try to persuade

examples.english: Go and talk some sense into him.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ quàn nǐ bié mǎi nàme guì de.
examples.english: I'd advise you not to buy such an expensive one.

words.tip: To talk someone into or out of something for their own good: 劝他少喝酒. Stronger and more personal than 建议. 劝架 = to step in and calm a quarrel. The u after q is ü.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí ge hǎo bànfǎ.
examples.english: I have a good idea how to do it.
There's nothing I can do either.

words.tip: A way of getting something done. 想办法 = to think of a way. 没办法 = nothing to be done, said with a shrug many times a day. 办 is the same as in 怎么办.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuìhǎo xiān dǎ ge diànhuà.
examples.english: You'd better phone first.
We'd better leave early.

words.tip: Before a verb it gives firm advice: 你最好… = you'd better… As an adjective it's simply 'the best': 最好的朋友.

examples.english: I like chatting with you.

examples.text: 他们一边喝茶一边聊天。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yìbiān hē chá yìbiān liáotiān.
examples.english: They're chatting over tea.

words.tip: 'To chat about the sky'. Verb + object: 聊了一会儿天; 聊聊天 = to have a little chat. Also for texting: 在微信上聊天. 聊 alone takes a topic: 聊工作.

examples.pinyin: Bié shēngqì, wǒ zài kāi wánxiào.
examples.english: Don't be angry, I'm joking.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì zài kāi wánxiào?
examples.english: Are you kidding?

words.tip: 'To open a play-laugh'. Joking with someone is 跟他开玩笑; at his expense, 开他的玩笑. 别开玩笑了! = stop kidding!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ jiǎng yí ge xiàohua.
examples.english: Let me tell you a joke.
This joke isn't funny.

words.tip: 'Laugh-talk'. 讲笑话 = to tell a joke. One that falls flat is a 冷笑话, a 'cold joke'. As a verb, 笑话 means to laugh at someone: 别笑话我.

examples.english: I mean it.
Be serious, stop laughing!

words.tip: 'To take as real'. 我是认真的 is the answer to 你在开玩笑吗? Also conscientious: 认真学习, 工作很认真, high praise from a Chinese teacher or boss.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen huàn yí ge huàtí ba.
examples.english: Let's change the subject.
This is an interesting topic.

words.tip: 'Talk-topic'. 换话题 = to change the subject. Safe topics with Chinese relatives: food, travel, health. Expect direct questions about salary, marriage and children too.

words.gloss: to lie, to tell a lie

examples.english: Why are you lying?

examples.pinyin: Tā cónglái bú duì wǒ sāhuǎng.
examples.english: He never lies to me.

words.tip: Also 说谎, with the same meaning. Lying to someone: 对 or 跟 + person + 撒谎. A lie is a 谎话.

words.gloss: to deceive, to cheat, to trick

examples.english: Don't you fool me!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bèi piàn le yìbǎi kuài qián.
examples.english: I was cheated out of a hundred yuan.

words.tip: The person follows directly: 骗我. It runs from teasing (你骗人! = you're having me on!) to real fraud. A swindler is a 骗子; 被骗 = to be cheated. Phone and online scams are a big topic in China.

examples.english: Let me tell you a secret.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen liǎ de mìmì.
examples.english: This is our secret, just the two of us.

words.tip: Two fourth tones, both falling: mì-mì. 保守秘密 = to keep a secret. 密 is the same as in 密码, a 'secret code'.

examples.english: Tell me the truth.

examples.pinyin: Shuō shíhuà, wǒ bú tài xǐhuan tā.
examples.english: To be honest, I don't like him much.

words.tip: 'Real words'. 说实话 = to tell the truth, and at the start of a sentence, 'to be honest…'. 实 is the 'real' in 其实. Opposite: 谎话 or 假话.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chéngrèn shì wǒ cuò le.
examples.english: I admit I was the one in the wrong.

examples.text: 他不承认吃了我的蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù chéngrèn chī le wǒ de dàngāo.
examples.english: He won't admit to eating my cake.

words.tip: To own up, or to concede a point: 我承认… = I admit… Admitting a mistake is 承认错误 or, shorter, 认错. 认 is the same as in 认识 and 认真.

words.gloss: to be surprised, to be startled

examples.text: 听到这个消息，我很吃惊。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, wǒ hěn chījīng.
examples.english: I was very surprised to hear the news.

examples.text: 你怎么一点儿都不吃惊？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme yìdiǎnr dōu bù chījīng?
examples.english: How come you're not the least bit surprised?

words.tip: 'To eat a fright', built like 吃醋. 大吃一惊 = to get a real shock. A pleasant surprise is a 惊喜: 给你一个惊喜! The written word is 惊讶.

examples.english: That was so awkward just now!

examples.text: 我忘了他的名字，很尴尬。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wàng le tā de míngzi, hěn gāngà.
examples.english: I forgot his name, which was embarrassing.

words.tip: Both the situation and the person can be 尴尬. The two characters exist only in this word. Internet slang: 尬聊, a painfully awkward chat. Milder embarrassment is 不好意思.

examples.text: 一个人在外国，有时候很孤单。
examples.pinyin: Yí ge rén zài wàiguó, yǒu shíhou hěn gūdān.
examples.english: On your own abroad, it sometimes gets lonely.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu nǐ zài, wǒ bù gūdān.
examples.english: With you here I'm not lonely.

words.tip: Feeling alone. The heavier, more literary word is 孤独. 单 is the 'single' of 单身 (unmarried). 一个人 = alone, by oneself.

examples.text: 看到你的礼物，我很感动。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào nǐ de lǐwù, wǒ hěn gǎndòng.
examples.english: I was very touched when I saw your present.
I was moved to tears.

words.tip: Stirred by kindness, a story, a gesture. The person is 感动; the thing that moves is 感人: 这个故事很感人. With an object: 你的话感动了我.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhège jiǔdiàn hěn mǎnyì.
examples.english: I'm very pleased with this hotel.

examples.text: 老板对你的工作满意吗？
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn duì nǐ de gōngzuò mǎnyì ma?
examples.english: Is the boss happy with your work?

words.tip: 'Wishes filled'. Satisfied with: 对…很满意. After a meal or a purchase you may be asked 您满意吗? 不满意 is a polite way to complain.

examples.english: Thank you for being so patient.
I've run out of patience for waiting.

words.tip: An 'enduring heart'. 有耐心 = to be patient; 没耐心 = impatient. Patient with someone: 对孩子很有耐心. Before a verb it means patiently: 耐心等.

examples.english: She works very hard.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì nǔlì xué hǎo Zhōngwén de.
examples.english: I'll work hard to learn Chinese well.

words.tip: 'To exert strength'. Before a verb: 努力学习, 努力工作. 我会努力的 = I'll do my best, the modest answer to praise or encouragement.

examples.english: Don't be shy, speak up!

examples.pinyin: Tā jiàn dào xīn péngyou huì hàixiū.
examples.english: She gets shy when she meets new people.

words.tip: 'To suffer shame': shy and blushing. 害 + feeling is also in 害怕 (afraid). Tell a shy learner: 别害羞，说错了没关系.

examples.english: You're so brave!

examples.text: 勇敢一点儿，去跟她说话吧。
examples.pinyin: Yǒnggǎn yìdiǎnr, qù gēn tā shuōhuà ba.
examples.english: Be a bit braver and go and talk to her.

words.tip: Two third tones in a row, so the first one rises: yóng-gǎn. 敢 alone = to dare: 你敢吗? 我不敢. Adjective + 一点儿 is a nudge: be a bit more…

examples.english: He's very generous to his friends.

examples.text: 她说话很大方，一点儿也不紧张。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà hěn dàfang, yìdiǎnr yě bù jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: She speaks with poise, not nervous at all.

words.tip: Open-handed with money, and also poised and unaffected in manner. The opposite of the first sense is 小气 (stingy). Fighting to pay the bill is being 大方.

examples.english: They get on very well.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé tóngshì de guānxi búcuò.
examples.english: I'm on good terms with my colleagues.

words.tip: Any tie between people, and famously the web of useful connections: 有关系 = to know the right people. 没关系 literally says 'there's no connection'.

examples.english: This is my boyfriend.

examples.text: 她的男朋友比她大三岁。
examples.pinyin: Tā de nánpéngyou bǐ tā dà sān suì.
examples.english: Her boyfriend is three years older than her.

words.tip: Only for a romantic partner. A friend who happens to be male is a 男的朋友 or 男性朋友: the 的 makes all the difference. Close relations drop 的 after 我: 我男朋友.

examples.english: Do you have a girlfriend?

examples.text: 我想介绍女朋友给父母认识。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jièshào nǚpéngyou gěi fùmǔ rènshi.
examples.english: I'd like to introduce my girlfriend to my parents.

words.tip: ü with rounded lips: nǚ. Bringing a 女朋友 home to meet the parents (见父母) is a serious step in China: it signals marriage plans. Husband and wife are 老公 and 老婆.

words.gloss: date (with someone); to go on a date

examples.text: 我们第一次约会是在公园。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dìyī cì yuēhuì shì zài gōngyuán.
examples.english: Our first date was in the park.

examples.text: 今天晚上我有一个约会。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang wǒ yǒu yí ge yuēhuì.
examples.english: I have a date this evening.

words.tip: An 'arranged meeting', mostly romantic. As a verb: 跟她约会. 约 alone = to arrange to meet: 我约了朋友吃饭. Tell the story of your 第一次约会.

words.gloss: to break up, to split up

examples.pinyin: Tāmen shàng ge yuè fēnshǒu le.
examples.english: They broke up last month.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng gēn nǐ fēnshǒu.
examples.english: I don't want to break up with you.

words.tip: 'To part hands', the opposite of 牵手. Breaking up with someone: 跟…分手. For married couples it's 离婚 (to divorce). 分 is the 'divide' in 分钟.

examples.text: 宝宝睡着了，小声一点儿。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao shuìzháo le, xiǎo shēng yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: The baby's asleep, keep your voice down.
Their baby is so cute!

words.tip: A 'little treasure'. The formal word is 婴儿. Couples call each other 宝宝 or 宝贝 too. On meeting a baby, 真可爱! is always right.

words.gloss: to be pregnant, to get pregnant

examples.english: My older sister is pregnant.

examples.pinyin: Tā huáiyùn wǔ ge yuè le.
examples.english: She's five months pregnant.

words.tip: A verb: 她怀孕了 = she's pregnant. After the birth comes 坐月子, a month of rest and special food for the mother: explain how your family does it.

words.gloss: to give birth to; to be born

examples.pinyin: Tā shēng le yí ge nǚhái.
examples.english: She's had a baby girl.
They're planning to have a baby next year.

words.tip: 生孩子 = to have a baby. The same character means raw (生鱼), unfamiliar (生词 = a new word), and starts 生日, 生病 and 生气. 你是哪年生的? asks for the year you were born.

examples.english: Children start kindergarten at three.
I'm going to the kindergarten to pick up my child.

words.tip: A 'young children's garden', built just like Kindergarten. Chinese children start at three, and grandparents often do the pick-up. 上幼儿园 = to go to kindergarten.

words.gloss: to look after, to take care of

characters.meaning: to shine on; to look after

examples.text: 我不在的时候，好好照顾自己。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú zài de shíhou, hǎohǎo zhàogù zìjǐ.
examples.english: Take good care of yourself while I'm away.
Grandma helps us look after the children.

words.tip: To care for a child, a patient, a guest, or your parents in old age. 照顾好自己 = look after yourself, a caring goodbye. Grandparents raising grandchildren is normal in China.

examples.english: They have a daughter.
My daughter is five this year.

words.tip: Here 儿 is a full syllable, ér, not the -r ending; the apostrophe in nǚ'ér keeps the two apart. A son-in-law is a 女婿.

examples.english: His son works in Germany.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ érzi zhǎng de zhēn gāo!
examples.english: Your son has grown so tall!

words.tip: 儿 as a full word again: ér. A daughter-in-law is a 儿媳妇. Traditional families wanted a 儿子 to carry on the name: ask how that has changed.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye jīnnián bāshí suì le.
examples.english: My grandpa is eighty this year.

examples.pinyin: Yéye měi tiān zǎoshang qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: Grandpa goes to the park every morning.

words.tip: Father's father. Mother's father is 外公 (in the north 姥爷): 外 marks the mother's side as 'outside' the family line. German Opa covers both.

examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zuò de jiǎozi zuì hǎochī.
examples.english: Grandma's dumplings are the best.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì nǎinai dài dà de.
examples.english: I was brought up by my grandma.

words.tip: Father's mother. Mother's mother is 外婆 (in the north 姥姥). 奶 is the milk in 牛奶. Children politely call any elderly woman 奶奶. 带大 = to bring up.

examples.pinyin: Chūnjié yào qù kàn hěn duō qīnqi.
examples.english: At Spring Festival you have to visit lots of relatives.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ māma de qīnqi.
examples.english: He's a relative of my mum's.

words.tip: Everyone you're related to. Spring Festival means 走亲戚, the round of visits to all of them. Uncles and aunts: 叔叔 and 阿姨, which are also the polite words for any adult of your parents' age.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan zhèlǐ de shēnghuó ma?
examples.english: Do you like life here?

examples.text: 我们在德国生活了五年。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài Déguó shēnghuó le wǔ nián.
examples.english: We lived in Germany for five years.

words.tip: Daily life and how you live it. As a verb, to live your life somewhere; 住 only says where your bed is. A whole lifetime is 一生 or 一辈子.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì zài Shànghǎi chūshēng de.
examples.english: I was born in Shanghai.

examples.text: 宝宝是昨天晚上出生的。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao shì zuótiān wǎnshang chūshēng de.
examples.english: The baby was born last night.

words.tip: 'To come out into life'. Use 是…的 for the where and when: 我是一九九五年出生的. On forms, 出生日期 = date of birth. 生 alone is what the mother does.

examples.english: My fish has died.
I'm starving!

words.tip: Blunt, so for people Chinese prefers 去世 (to pass away) or 走了 ('has gone'). After an adjective, 死了 just means 'extremely': 累死了, 热死了, even 高兴死了. 死 sounds like 四, which is why four is unlucky.

examples.english: I'm thirty this year.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǐ wǒ dà liǎng suì.
examples.english: He's two years older than me.

words.tip: Number + 岁, and no verb is needed: 我三十岁. To ask: 你多大? for adults, 你几岁? for children, 您多大年纪? for the elderly. By traditional reckoning (虚岁) you are one at birth.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì zài Běijīng zhǎngdà de.
examples.english: I grew up in Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhǎngdà le xiǎng zuò shénme?
examples.english: What do you want to be when you grow up?

words.tip: 长 is zhǎng here (to grow), not cháng (long). 你是在哪里长大的? is a standard question. 孩子长大了 = the children have grown up.

examples.english: I really like Chinese culture.

examples.text: 我们两个国家的文化很不一样。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎng ge guójiā de wénhuà hěn bù yíyàng.
examples.english: The cultures of our two countries are very different.

words.tip: 文 is the writing in 中文: culture is what is 'transformed by writing'. 文化差异 = cultural differences; 文化冲击 = culture shock. 没文化 means uneducated.

examples.pinyin: Zǎo shuì zǎo qǐ shì hǎo xíguàn.
examples.english: Early to bed and early to rise is a good habit.

examples.text: 我还不习惯这里的天气。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái bù xíguàn zhèlǐ de tiānqì.
examples.english: I'm still not used to the weather here.

words.tip: Noun and verb in one: 好习惯 (a good habit), 我习惯了 (I've got used to it). 习 is the same as in 学习 and 练习. Ask: 你习惯这里的生活了吗?

examples.text: 春节吃饺子是我们的传统。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié chī jiǎozi shì wǒmen de chuántǒng.
examples.english: Eating dumplings at Spring Festival is our tradition.
My parents are fairly traditional.

words.tip: What is 'passed on': noun and adjective. 传统节日 = traditional festivals. Of people, 很传统 means conservative, old-fashioned.

words.gloss: home town, where one's family comes from

examples.english: Where's your family from?
I'm going back to my home town for Spring Festival.

words.tip: The 'old home': where your family is from, even if you've never lived there. 你老家在哪里? is one of the first questions between Chinese strangers. Someone from the same place is a 老乡. The written word is 家乡.

examples.english: I'm feeling a bit homesick.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài wàiguó huì xiǎngjiā ma?
examples.english: Do you get homesick when you're abroad?

words.tip: 'To miss home': 想 in its sense of missing. Verb + object, so 'very homesick' is 很想家. What do you miss most? 我想我妈妈做的菜.

examples.english: Have you ever had a pet?
You can bring pets to this hotel.

words.tip: A 'pampered creature'. 宠 alone = to spoil: 他很宠女朋友. Pet-keeping has boomed in Chinese cities; a cat owner jokingly calls himself a 铲屎官, 'poop-scooping officer'.

words.gloss: to keep (animals), to raise, to grow

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǎng le liǎng zhī māo.
examples.english: We have two cats.

examples.pinyin: Zài chéngshì li yǎng gǒu bù róngyì.
examples.english: Keeping a dog in the city isn't easy.

words.tip: To keep and care for something living: 养狗, 养花 (grow flowers), 养孩子 (bring up children). 养家 = to support a family. Third tone.

examples.english: Have you fed the dog?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang wèi māo.
examples.english: I feed the cat every morning.

words.tip: To feed an animal or a baby. Said with a rising tone, wéi, it's how you answer the phone: 喂? The 口 on the left is a mouth.

examples.pinyin: Bié pà, tā bù yǎo rén.
examples.english: Don't be scared, it doesn't bite.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xié bèi gǒu yǎo huài le.
examples.english: The dog has chewed up my shoes.

words.tip: Dogs, snakes and mosquitoes all 咬, where German separates beißen and stechen. 被…咬了 = got bitten by. 咬一口 = to take a bite.

examples.english: I kept rabbits when I was little.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī tùzi de ěrduo zhēn cháng!
examples.english: This rabbit's ears are so long!

words.tip: The fourth of the twelve zodiac animals: 我属兔 = I was born in the year of the rabbit. Ask your partner's sign: 你属什么? The jade rabbit (玉兔) lives on the moon.

examples.english: What instruments can you play?

examples.text: 我小时候学过两种乐器。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎoshíhou xuéguo liǎng zhǒng yuèqì.
examples.english: I learned two instruments as a child.

words.tip: 乐 is yuè for music (音乐) but lè for joy (快乐). Each family of instruments has its own verb: 弹 for plucked strings and keys, 拉 for bowed strings, 吹 for wind, 打 for drums.

examples.english: He plays the guitar and I sing.
I'd like to learn the guitar.

words.tip: A sound loan from 'guitar'. Counted with 把, like other things you grip. You 弹 it, with your fingers.

examples.pinyin: Tā de gāngqín tán de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: She plays the piano very well.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǎinai jiā yǒu yí jià gāngqín.
examples.english: There's a piano at my grandma's.

words.tip: A 'steel zither'. 琴 names many instruments: 小提琴 (violin), 口琴 (harmonica), 古琴 (the ancient zither). Counted with 架, like planes. Millions of Chinese children take piano lessons.

words.gloss: to play (a plucked or keyboard instrument)

examples.english: Can you play the piano?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ gěi wǒmen tán yì shǒu gē ba.
examples.english: Play us a song.

words.tip: To pluck or strike with the fingers: 弹钢琴, 弹吉他. Never 玩 for an instrument. Second tone. A bowed instrument takes 拉: 拉小提琴.

examples.text: 这个乐队的歌我都喜欢。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuèduì de gē wǒ dōu xǐhuan.
examples.english: I like all of this band's songs.

examples.text: 他们的乐队周末在酒吧唱歌。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de yuèduì zhōumò zài jiǔbā chànggē.
examples.english: Their band sings in a bar at weekends.

words.tip: A 'music team', anything from a rock band to a symphony orchestra. A pop concert is an 演唱会; a classical one is an 音乐会.

examples.text: 我爸爸每个周末都看足球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba měi ge zhōumò dōu kàn zúqiú.
examples.english: My dad watches football every weekend.
Whose football is this?

words.tip: A 'foot ball', word for word. The ball itself is 一个足球; a match is 一场足球. Many Chinese fans follow the German Bundesliga (德甲): a ready-made topic.

examples.pinyin: Tā dǎ lánqiú dǎ de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He plays basketball very well.

examples.text: 下班以后我们去打篮球吧。
examples.pinyin: Xiàbān yǐhòu wǒmen qù dǎ lánqiú ba.
examples.english: Let's go and play basketball after work.

words.tip: A 'basket ball', hugely popular in China. Ball games played with the hands take 打: 打篮球, 打网球 (tennis), 打乒乓球 (table tennis). Note how the verb is repeated before 得.

examples.text: 我们明天早上去跑步吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān zǎoshang qù pǎobù ba.
examples.english: Let's go for a run tomorrow morning.
Running is very good for you.

words.tip: 'To run steps': running as exercise, while 跑 alone is to run somewhere. Verb + object: 跑了半个小时步. A treadmill is a 跑步机.

examples.text: 我每个星期去两次健身房。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi ge xīngqī qù liǎng cì jiànshēnfáng.
examples.english: I go to the gym twice a week.

examples.text: 这个健身房晚上人很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiànshēnfáng wǎnshang rén hěn duō.
examples.english: This gym is crowded in the evenings.

words.tip: A 'strengthen-the-body room'. 健身 = to work out; 健 is the same as in 健康. In Chinese parks, older people exercise for free on outdoor equipment and dance in the square (广场舞).

examples.text: 他每个星期六都去踢足球。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi ge xīngqīliù dōu qù tī zúqiú.
examples.english: He goes to play football every Saturday.
Stop kicking my chair!

words.tip: Football is kicked: 踢足球, never 打足球 or 玩足球. The 足 on the left is the foot radical.

words.gloss: to be injured, to get hurt

examples.english: Is anyone hurt?

examples.text: 他踢足球的时候受伤了。
examples.pinyin: Tā tī zúqiú de shíhou shòushāng le.
examples.english: He got injured playing football.

words.tip: 'To receive an injury'. The injured part goes in front: 他的腿受伤了. 伤 alone is a wound, and feelings can be hurt too: 伤心 = heartbroken.

examples.english: Your hand is bleeding!
It's not bleeding much, it's all right.

words.tip: 'To flow blood'. 血 is xuè in careful speech and xiě in everyday talk, so you'll often hear liú xiě: both are fine. 流 is also for tears and runny noses: 流眼泪, 流鼻涕.

words.gloss: to fall over; to drop and break

examples.english: Careful, don't fall!

examples.pinyin: Bēizi diào zài dì shang shuāi huài le.
examples.english: The glass fell on the floor and smashed.

words.tip: A person falls hard: 摔倒了, 摔了一跤. A thing gets dropped and smashed: 摔坏了. 掉 is simply falling down or off; 摔 has the impact in it.

examples.english: Call an ambulance, quick!
The ambulance will be here in ten minutes.

words.tip: A 'rescue-and-protect vehicle'; 救 is the same as in 救命. In mainland China the ambulance is 120, the police 110 and the fire brigade 119: learn them before you travel. 叫 = to call for.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dài tā qù kàn jízhěn ba.
examples.english: Let's take him to A&E.

examples.pinyin: Jízhěn zài yīyuàn de yī lóu.
examples.english: A&E is on the ground floor of the hospital.

words.tip: An 'urgent consultation'. 看急诊 = to go to A&E; the department is the 急诊室 or 急诊科. In China people go straight to hospital even for small things, and 挂号 comes first.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎo bu dào nàge wénjiàn le.
examples.english: I can't find that file any more.

examples.pinyin: Zhège wénjiàn tài dà, fā bu liǎo.
examples.english: This file is too big to send.

words.tip: A computer file and an official paper document alike. A folder is a 文件夹. 件 is the measure word you know from clothes. 发不了 = can't be sent.

words.gloss: to save (a file); to keep, to preserve

examples.pinyin: Xiě wán le bié wàng le bǎocún.
examples.english: When you've finished writing, don't forget to save.

examples.text: 这些照片我想好好保存。
