examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē zhàopiàn wǒ xiǎng hǎohǎo bǎocún.
examples.english: I want to keep these photos safe.

words.tip: 'Protect and store': the Save button, and also keeping photos or food. You know 存 from 存钱. Saving money is 存 or 省, never 保存.

examples.text: 这张照片不好看，删了吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn bù hǎokàn, shān le ba.
examples.english: This photo isn't nice, delete it.

examples.text: 我不小心把你的消息删了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎoxīn bǎ nǐ de xiāoxi shān le.
examples.english: I deleted your message by accident.

words.tip: The everyday word; the button says 删除 (shānchú). 删掉 = to delete for good. 不小心 = by accident. First tone.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào dǎyìn liǎng zhāng piào.
examples.english: I need to print two tickets.
Where can I print something round here?

words.tip: One more 打 verb. The printer is a 打印机, a copy shop a 打印店. To photocopy is 复印. 印 alone is a seal or stamp.

examples.english: This app is really handy.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yòng shénme ruǎnjiàn xué Zhōngwén?
examples.english: What app do you use to learn Chinese?

words.tip: A 'soft item': software on a computer and apps on a phone (also 应用, or just APP). 好用 = good to use. 下载软件 = to download an app.

examples.english: Let's add each other on WeChat.

examples.text: 我在微信上给你发了照片。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài Wēixìn shang gěi nǐ fā le zhàopiàn.
examples.english: I've sent you the photos on WeChat.

words.tip: 'Micro-message': the app that runs daily life in China, for chatting, paying, booking and much more. 加微信 = to add someone, the modern way of swapping numbers. Family news arrives in the 家人群 (family group).

examples.english: This video is hilarious!
In the evening I video-call my parents.

words.tip: Noun and verb: 看视频 = to watch videos; 跟妈妈视频 = to video-call mum. 短视频 are the short clips on 抖音, the Chinese TikTok.

examples.text: 我想跟你分享一个好消息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ fēnxiǎng yí ge hǎo xiāoxi.
examples.english: I want to share some good news with you.

examples.text: 他喜欢在网上分享照片。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài wǎngshang fēnxiǎng zhàopiàn.
examples.english: He likes sharing photos online.

words.tip: 'Divide and enjoy': sharing joy, news, experiences, a post. For splitting a cake or a bill, plain 分 is enough: 我们分一个蛋糕吧.

words.gloss: to follow (online); to pay attention to

examples.english: Have you followed me?

examples.pinyin: Hěn duō rén guānzhù zhège wèntí.
examples.english: A lot of people are following this issue.

words.tip: On social media: 关注 = to follow, 取消关注 = to unfollow, and followers are 粉丝 ('vermicelli', from the sound of 'fans'). More generally, to take a close interest in something.

words.gloss: to like (a post), to give a thumbs-up

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ de zhàopiàn diǎnzàn le.
examples.english: I liked your photo.

examples.pinyin: Māma měi tiān dōu gěi wǒ diǎnzàn.
examples.english: Mum likes my posts every day.

words.tip: 'To tap praise'. You like someone's post with 给…点赞. 赞! on its own means 'great!'. 点 as a verb, to tap or pick, is the 点 of 点菜.

examples.english: I'm called Anna, and you?

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu jiào tā Lǎo Wáng.
examples.english: Everyone calls him Lao Wang.

words.tip: Fourth tone, sharp and falling. 我叫… gives your name. It also means to shout, to call someone over, and to order: 叫外卖 = to order takeaway. 老 + surname is a friendly way to address an older colleague.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xìng Lǐ, jiào Lǐ Míng.
examples.english: My surname is Li, my full name is Li Ming.
What surname does your child have?

words.tip: The surname comes first: 李明 is Mr Li. The polite question is 您贵姓? Women keep their own surname after marriage. 女 (woman) is on the left of the character.

examples.english: Mr Wang, please come in!

examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi xiānsheng shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.english: This gentleman is my teacher.

words.tip: The title goes after the surname: 王先生 = Mr Wang. On its own it addresses a man politely. 我先生 = my husband, a little formal.

examples.text: 李女士今天不在办公室。
examples.pinyin: Lǐ nǚshì jīntiān bú zài bàngōngshì.
examples.english: Ms Li isn't in the office today.
Who is that lady?

words.tip: The polite title for a woman, after the surname: 李女士. ü needs rounded lips: nǚ. Speeches begin 女士们，先生们 = ladies and gentlemen.

words.gloss: pet name (used by the family since childhood)

examples.english: Did you have a pet name as a child?

examples.pinyin: Nǎinai hái jiào wǒ de xiǎomíng.
examples.english: Grandma still calls me by my pet name.

words.tip: Most Chinese children get a 'little name' at home, often a doubled syllable or 小 + something. Tell yours and the story behind it. The official name is 大名.

examples.english: January in Germany is very cold.
We're moving house in January.

words.tip: Months are just number + 月: 一月, 二月 … 十二月. Count through all twelve together. Don't mix up 一月 (January) and 一个月 (one month). Dates go big to small: 一月五号.

examples.english: This year I want to exercise more.

examples.text: 今年的生日你想怎么过？
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de shēngrì nǐ xiǎng zěnme guò?
examples.english: How do you want to spend your birthday this year?
alternatives: 你今年的生日想怎么过？

words.tip: The same 今 as in 今天. Time words go before the verb, never at the end of the sentence. 你今年多大? is the usual way to ask an adult's age.

examples.english: We met last year.
Last summer was especially hot.

words.tip: The 'gone year'. The year before that is 前年, like 前天. The 是…的 pattern in the first example stresses when something happened.

examples.english: Next year I want to learn to drive.

examples.text: 你明年还在这里工作吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ míngnián hái zài zhèlǐ gōngzuò ma?
examples.english: Will you still be working here next year?
alternatives: 明年你还在这里工作吗？

words.tip: The same 明 as in 明天. The year after next is 后年, like 后天. So: 前年, 去年, 今年, 明年, 后年.

examples.text: 下个月月初我有一个考试。
examples.pinyin: Xià ge yuè yuèchū wǒ yǒu yí ge kǎoshì.
examples.english: I have an exam at the start of next month.
alternatives: 我下个月月初有一个考试。

examples.text: 月初的时候钱总是够的。
examples.pinyin: Yuèchū de shíhou qián zǒngshì gòu de.
examples.english: At the start of the month there's always enough money.

words.tip: The opposite of 月底. With a month name it shortens: 五月初 = early May, 五月底 = late May. The same works for years: 年初, 年底.

examples.english: At the Dragon Boat Festival we eat zongzi.
This year the Dragon Boat Festival is in June.

words.tip: The fifth day of the fifth lunar month, usually in June. People race dragon boats and eat 粽子 (zòngzi): sticky rice wrapped in leaves. Say whether your family likes them sweet or salty.

examples.english: Where are you planning to go in the summer holidays?

examples.text: 孩子们七月开始放暑假。
examples.english: The children's summer holidays start in July.

words.tip: School and university holidays in July and August; the winter ones around Spring Festival are 寒假. 放暑假 = to break up for the summer. 假 is fourth tone here, as in 放假.

examples.text: 中秋节一家人一起吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngqiūjié yì jiā rén yìqǐ chī fàn.
examples.english: At the Mid-Autumn Festival the whole family eats together.
Do you get homesick at the Mid-Autumn Festival?

words.tip: The fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month, in September or early October, under the full moon. It is the festival of family reunion, so people far from home feel it most.

examples.english: This mooncake is too sweet.
Have you ever eaten a mooncake?

words.tip: The round, rich cake for 中秋节, given in boxes to family and colleagues. Fillings differ by region: describe your favourite. They are very filling, so people cut them up and share.

examples.english: There are seven days off for National Day.

examples.text: 国庆节很多人出去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Guóqìngjié hěn duō rén chūqù lǚxíng.
examples.english: Lots of people go travelling at National Day.

words.tip: The first of October. The week off is called 黄金周, the 'golden week', when trains and sights are packed. People also just say 十一 (ten-one) for the holiday.

examples.pinyin: Nǐmen nàlǐ yǒu jǐ ge jìjié?
examples.english: How many seasons do you have where you're from?
It often rains at this time of year.

words.tip: The four are 春天, 夏天, 秋天, 冬天. Also for food in season: 这个季节的草莓最好吃. Fourth tone, then second.

examples.english: Everyone is busy at the end of the year.
We're planning to get married at the end of the year.

words.tip: The 'bottom of the year', built like 月底. It can mean December, or the weeks before Spring Festival, when people settle bills and companies pay the yearly bonus.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǎinai zhǐ guò nónglì shēngrì.
examples.english: My grandma only celebrates her lunar-calendar birthday.
Spring Festival is the lunar New Year.

words.tip: The 'farming calendar' that sets 春节, 端午节 and 中秋节, so they move every year. Many older people keep their birthday by it. Look up your partner's 农历 birthday together.

examples.text: 今天是我们的结婚纪念日。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì wǒmen de jiéhūn jìniànrì.
examples.english: Today is our wedding anniversary.
You've forgotten our anniversary again!

words.tip: A 'day of remembering'. 结婚纪念日 = wedding anniversary. Couples also count days together: 在一起一百天. r in rì is made with the tongue curled back.

words.gloss: New Year's Day (the first of January)

examples.english: There's one day off for New Year's Day.

examples.text: 元旦那天我们在家看电视。
examples.pinyin: Yuándàn nà tiān wǒmen zài jiā kàn diànshì.
examples.english: On New Year's Day we stayed at home and watched TV.
alternatives: 我们元旦那天在家看电视。

words.tip: The first of January. It is a day off, but a small affair next to 春节, the lunar New Year. 旦 shows the sun 日 rising over the horizon.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu shíhou tā gōngzuò dào hěn wǎn.
examples.english: Sometimes he works until very late.

examples.text: 我们有时候去外面吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu shíhou qù wàimiàn chī fàn.
examples.english: We sometimes go out to eat.
alternatives: 有时候我们去外面吃饭。

words.tip: 'There are times'. It goes before the verb or at the very start, never at the end. Often shortened to 有时. Repeat it for 'sometimes… sometimes…'.

examples.english: We often video-chat.
Do you exercise often?

words.tip: Means the same as 常常 and is at least as common in speech. For 'not often' say 不经常 or 不常, never 不常常.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ ǒu'ěr hē yì bēi jiǔ.
examples.english: I have a drink once in a while.
Now and then he cooks too.

words.tip: Less often than 有时候. Two third tones together, so the first one rises: óu-ěr. The apostrophe in the pinyin only marks where the syllables split.

examples.english: I usually get up at seven.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài hěn yìbān.
examples.english: The food at this restaurant is nothing special.

words.tip: Two uses. Before a verb: usually, as a rule. As a description: average, so-so, a polite way to say something isn't good. 一般来说 = generally speaking.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān dōu xiǎng nǐ.
examples.english: I think of you every day.

examples.pinyin: Měi tiān xué wǔ ge cí bù nán.
examples.english: Learning five words a day isn't hard.

words.tip: No measure word between 每 and 天, just as with 年: 每年. It often teams up with 都 before the verb. Also 天天, a little more emphatic.

examples.english: I have two older brothers.
Let's meet at two o'clock.

words.tip: 二 is for counting and for numbers like 十二 and 二十; 两 is for 'two of something': 两个人, 两天, 两点, 两百. An easy slip for learners: never 二个.

examples.english: This car costs a hundred thousand yuan.

examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì yǒu yìbǎi wàn rén.
examples.english: This city has a million people.

words.tip: Chinese groups big numbers in fours, not threes: 十万 = 100,000, 一百万 = a million, 一千万 = ten million. Practise converting slowly on paper. 一万 takes yí: yíwàn.

examples.text: 八是中国人喜欢的数字。
examples.pinyin: Bā shì Zhōngguó rén xǐhuan de shùzì.
examples.english: Eight is a number Chinese people like.

examples.pinyin: Zhège shùzì wǒ méi kàn dǒng.
examples.english: I didn't understand this figure.

words.tip: Lucky and unlucky numbers: 八 sounds like 发 (to get rich), 四 sounds like 死 (to die). Explain which floor and phone numbers people avoid. 号码 is a number that identifies something.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ suàn yíxià yígòng duōshao qián.
examples.english: Work out how much it is altogether.
I worked it out wrong, sorry.

words.tip: For sums and bills. 算了 = forget it, never mind, something you'll hear a lot. 打算 (to plan) uses the same character. 一共 = altogether.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qī diǎn zuǒyòu dào jiā.
examples.english: I'll be home at about seven.
He's about thirty.

words.tip: 'Left-right' of a number = a bit either side. It always comes after the number and its measure word: 十个左右, 两点左右. 差不多 goes before instead.

words.gloss: matter, thing (to do or that happens)

examples.text: 我有一件事情想告诉你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí jiàn shìqing xiǎng gàosu nǐ.
examples.english: There's something I want to tell you.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shìqing bú shì nǐ de cuò.
examples.english: This isn't your fault.

words.tip: Things that happen or need doing; 东西 is for things you can touch. Often just 事: 我有事 = I'm busy, 没事 = it's nothing. The measure word is 件.

examples.english: The reason for being late is the traffic.

examples.text: 我不知道他生气的原因。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào tā shēngqì de yuányīn.
examples.english: I don't know the reason he's angry.

words.tip: The 因 of 因为. The reason goes in front with 的: 迟到的原因. 什么原因? is a slightly more formal 为什么?

examples.english: This problem is easy to solve.
Arguing can't solve problems.

words.tip: To 'untie and decide'. The usual partner is 问题: 解决问题. j is made with the tongue flat behind the lower teeth, and ue is like German ü + e.

words.gloss: what's to be done? what shall we do?

characters.meaning: word ending, no meaning of its own

examples.pinyin: Yàoshi zhǎo bu dào le, zěnme bàn?
examples.english: I can't find the keys, what shall we do?
What do we do if it rains?

words.tip: 'How to handle it?' Said on its own when something goes wrong, or after an 'if'. The calm answer: 没事，我有办法.

examples.english: What's the situation now?

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng qíngkuàng wǒ méi jiànguo.
examples.english: I've never seen a situation like this.

words.tip: How things stand. 看情况 = it depends, a very handy answer. 这种情况下 = in a situation like this.

examples.english: Now I finally understand.

examples.text: 你说得太快，我没听明白。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de tài kuài, wǒ méi tīng míngbai.
examples.english: You spoke too fast, I didn't catch it.

words.tip: 'Bright and plain': to see the point. 懂 is more about knowing a language or subject; often either works. 明白了! = got it! 听明白 = to understand by listening.

examples.english: Please say it a bit more clearly.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kàn bu qīngchu nàge zì.
examples.english: I can't see that character clearly.

words.tip: Goes after verbs of the senses and speech: 看清楚, 听清楚, 说清楚. 我不清楚 = I'm not sure, I don't know the details. q is like 'ch' with the tongue flat.

words.gloss: to discover, to notice, to find out

examples.english: I've noticed you've lost weight.

examples.text: 他到家才发现没带钥匙。
examples.pinyin: Tā dào jiā cái fāxiàn méi dài yàoshi.
examples.english: Only when he got home did he notice he had no keys.

words.tip: Something 'comes into view': noticing a change, finding a mistake, discovering a nice café. Usually followed by a whole sentence saying what you found.

examples.english: You have to mind your safety when driving.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ méi zhùyì tā chuān shénme.
examples.english: I didn't notice what he was wearing.

words.tip: 注意! on its own = attention, watch out. 注意身体 = look after your health, a caring thing to say. Don't confuse with 主意 (zhǔyi, idea): different tones.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ shì Zhōngguó rén.
examples.english: I thought you were Chinese.

examples.text: 对不起，我以为今天星期五。
examples.english: Sorry, I thought today was Friday.

words.tip: For a belief that turned out wrong; 觉得 is for a real opinion. So 我以为你不来了 means 'I thought you weren't coming (but here you are)'. 为 is second tone here.

examples.english: Don't worry, I'll be there in a moment.

examples.pinyin: Bié zǒu, zài hē yì bēi chá ba.
examples.english: Don't go, have another cup of tea.

words.tip: The short, everyday way to say 'don't', straight before the verb. It is a contraction of 不要. 别…了 asks someone to stop: 别说了! = stop talking! You know it from 别的 (other).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyòng děng wǒ, xiān chī ba.
examples.english: You needn't wait for me, go ahead and eat.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān búyòng shàngbān, tài hǎo le!
examples.english: No work tomorrow, great!

words.tip: 'No use' = you don't have to. It releases someone from a duty; 别 tells them not to. 不用谢 = no need for thanks. 不用了，谢谢 politely turns down an offer.

words.gloss: to let, to make, to have (someone do something)

examples.pinyin: Māma bú ràng wǒ hē jiǔ.
examples.english: Mum doesn't let me drink alcohol.

examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒ kànkan nǐ de shǒu.
examples.english: Let me have a look at your hand.

words.tip: A 让 B + verb: let B, make B, or tell B to do it; the context decides. 让我想想 = let me think. The r is made with the tongue curled back, not a German r.

examples.english: Taking photos isn't permitted here.

examples.text: 公司允许我们在家工作。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yǔnxǔ wǒmen zài jiā gōngzuò.
examples.english: The company allows us to work from home.

words.tip: The formal word for rules, signs and companies; at home people say 让. Both syllables have the ü sound (written u after y and x). Two third tones: the first rises.

examples.english: Is smoking allowed here?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba yǐjīng bù chōuyān le.
examples.english: My dad doesn't smoke any more.

words.tip: 'To draw smoke'. Signs say 禁止吸烟 with the formal word 吸烟. Offering cigarettes is a common social gesture among men: 我不抽烟，谢谢 turns it down politely.

examples.english: You can hang your coat here.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zài kètīng guà yì fú huà.
examples.english: I'd like to hang a picture in the living room.

words.tip: Also to hang up the phone: 我先挂了 = I'll hang up now. You've met it in 挂号 (to register at a hospital). The hand radical 扌 is on the left.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang bǎizhe hěn duō cài.
examples.english: There are lots of dishes set out on the table.

examples.text: 吃饭了，帮我摆一下筷子。
examples.pinyin: Chī fàn le, bāng wǒ bǎi yíxià kuàizi.
examples.english: Dinner's ready, help me set out the chopsticks.

words.tip: To place things neatly or on display: dishes on a table, books on a shelf, chairs in a row. 放 just puts something down; 摆 arranges it. 摆着 = is set out there.

words.gloss: to move, to carry (something big or heavy)

examples.text: 这个箱子太重，我搬不动。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāngzi tài zhòng, wǒ bān bu dòng.
examples.english: This box is too heavy, I can't move it.

examples.text: 我们一起搬这张桌子吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ bān zhè zhāng zhuōzi ba.
examples.english: Let's move this table together.

words.tip: The 搬 of 搬家: shifting furniture and boxes, usually with both arms. 搬不动 = can't budge it. 拿 is for things you can simply hold in your hand.

examples.text: 你的东西掉了，我帮你捡。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de dōngxi diào le, wǒ bāng nǐ jiǎn.
examples.english: You've dropped something, I'll pick it up for you.

examples.text: 我在公园捡到一部手机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài gōngyuán jiǎndào yí bù shǒujī.
examples.english: I found a mobile phone in the park.

words.tip: To pick up something that has fallen or been lost. 捡到 = to find something lying around. Don't mix up with 剪 (to cut with scissors): same sound, same tone, different character.

words.gloss: to pack, to put in; to hold; to install

examples.pinyin: Zhège bāo néng zhuāng hěn duō dōngxi.
examples.english: This bag can hold a lot of things.

examples.pinyin: Xíngli dōu zhuāng hǎo le ma?
examples.english: Is the luggage all packed?

words.tip: To put things into a container, or what a container can hold. Also to install: 装空调, 装软件. zh is made with the tongue curled back, and the tone is high and level.

examples.english: I've been looking for you everywhere!

examples.pinyin: Fángjiān li dàochù dōu shì shū.
examples.english: There are books all over the room.

words.tip: 'Reaching every place'. It goes before the verb and likes 都 after it: 到处都是 = they're everywhere. Two fourth tones.

examples.english: This place is really beautiful!
What kind of place do you want to go to?

words.tip: Any place or spot, big or small. 什么地方? is another way to ask 哪里? Also a part of something: 这个地方我不懂 = I don't understand this bit.

examples.english: Where did you two meet?

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ nǎr dōu bù xiǎng qù.
examples.english: At the weekend I don't want to go anywhere.

words.tip: The northern form of 哪里; in the same way 这儿 = 这里 and 那儿 = 那里. Say which you use at home. 哪儿都不… = not anywhere. Careful with the tone: 那儿 (nàr) means 'there'.

words.gloss: over here, this side, this way

examples.english: Come and sit over here!

examples.pinyin: Zhèbiān de tiānqì bǐ nàbiān hǎo.
examples.english: The weather here is better than over there.

words.tip: The partner is 那边 (over there). Waiters and hosts say 这边请 = this way, please. On the phone, 我这边 and 你那边 mean 'where I am' and 'where you are'.

examples.text: 外面太冷，我们去里面吧。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn tài lěng, wǒmen qù lǐmiàn ba.
examples.english: It's too cold outside, let's go inside.
What's inside the box?

words.tip: The full form of 里 and the opposite of 外面. It can stand alone (在里面), while 里 needs a noun in front. Also 里边.

examples.english: My little sister starts university next year.

examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ dàxué lí wǒ jiā hěn jìn.
examples.english: This university is close to my home.

words.tip: The 'big school'; below it come 中学 (middle) and 小学 (small = primary). 上大学 = to go to university. Getting in depends on one huge exam, the 高考.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de dàxué tóngxué.
examples.english: He's a classmate of mine from university.

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ gēn lǎo tóngxué jiànmiàn.
examples.english: At the weekend I'm meeting old classmates.

words.tip: 'Same study', built like 同事 (same work). Teachers address pupils as 同学们. 老同学 are old classmates, a bond that lasts for life.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì nǎ nián bìyè de?
examples.english: What year did you graduate?

examples.text: 毕业以后我想去德国工作。
examples.pinyin: Bìyè yǐhòu wǒ xiǎng qù Déguó gōngzuò.
examples.english: After graduating I'd like to go and work in Germany.

words.tip: For any school level. The school goes in front: 大学毕业 = to graduate from university, never 毕业大学. Two fourth tones.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de Déyǔ shuō de zhēn hǎo!
examples.english: You speak German really well!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde Déyǔ bǐ Zhōngwén nán.
examples.english: I think German is harder than Chinese.

words.tip: 德 from 德国 + 语 (spoken language). 德文 is also fine. In the same way: 英语 (English), 汉语 (Chinese, a little more formal than 中文).

examples.text: 你教我中文，我教你德语。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiāo wǒ Zhōngwén, wǒ jiāo nǐ Déyǔ.
examples.english: You teach me Chinese, I'll teach you German.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma zài xuéxiào jiāo yīnyuè.
examples.english: My mum teaches music at a school.

words.tip: First tone as a verb, and the person comes straight after it: 教我. In nouns it's fourth tone: 教室 (jiàoshì, classroom). The first example is what the two of you do!

words.gloss: (moves the object in front of the verb: take it and…)

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ yào chī le ma?
examples.english: Have you taken your medicine?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ shǒujī fàng zài nǎlǐ le?
examples.english: Where did you put your phone?

words.tip: Subject + 把 + thing + verb + result: what you do to a particular, known thing. The verb can't stand bare at the end; it needs 了, a place or a result. Used all the time for requests around the house. You know 把 as a measure word too.

examples.pinyin: Dàngāo bèi dìdi chī wán le.
examples.english: The cake got eaten up by my little brother.

examples.text: 我的手机被孩子摔坏了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi háizi shuāi huài le.
examples.english: My phone got broken by the child.

words.tip: Thing + 被 + doer + verb + result. Mostly for something unwelcome that happened to you. The doer can be left out: 蛋糕被吃完了. Far rarer than the German passive, so don't overuse it.

examples.english: You should apologise to her.

examples.pinyin: Xiàng zuǒ guǎi jiù shì dìtiězhàn.
examples.english: Turn left and there's the underground station.

words.tip: For directions it is a slightly more formal 往: 向左拐. With people it marks who an action is aimed at: 向他道歉, 向老师问好. Same sound as 像 (to resemble).

examples.text: 这是一本关于中国的书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì běn guānyú Zhōngguó de shū.
examples.english: This is a book about China.

examples.text: 关于这件事，我们明天再说。
examples.pinyin: Guānyú zhè jiàn shì, wǒmen míngtiān zài shuō.
examples.english: As for this matter, let's talk about it tomorrow.

words.tip: Two positions only: before a noun with 的 (关于…的书), or at the very start of the sentence as a topic. It never comes after the verb, unlike German über.

words.gloss: for, in place of, on behalf of

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng tì wǒ qù ma?
examples.english: Can you go in my place?
I'm really happy for you!

words.tip: Doing something in someone's place: 替我问他好 = say hello to him from me. With feelings it means 'for': 替你高兴, 替你担心. Fourth tone.

characters.meaning: to be fond of (fourth tone here)

examples.english: What hobbies do you have?

examples.text: 我的爱好是爬山和拍照。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de àihào shì páshān hé pāizhào.
examples.english: My hobbies are hiking and taking photos.

words.tip: 好 is fourth tone here (hào, to be fond of), not the third tone of 'good'. A standard question when people get to know each other. Two fourth tones.

examples.text: 我对中国文化很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì Zhōngguó wénhuà hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: I'm very interested in Chinese culture.
He has no interest in football.

words.tip: The pattern is 对 + thing + 感兴趣 (to feel interest) or 有兴趣. The thing never comes after 兴趣 as it does in English. 兴 is fourth tone here, as in 高兴.

examples.english: I hate meetings in the morning.
This kind of weather is so annoying!

words.tip: The everyday opposite of 喜欢, less heavy than 恨 (real hatred). As a description it means annoying. Said with a smile, 讨厌! is also a flirty 'oh, you!'

examples.pinyin: Bié fán wǒ, wǒ zài gōngzuò.
examples.english: Don't bother me, I'm working.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shìqing tài duō, wǒ hěn fán.
examples.english: There's too much to do today, I'm fed up.

words.tip: The feeling of being pestered or worn down by too much. 烦死了! = so annoying! It's the second half of 麻烦 (trouble). 火 (fire) is on the left.

words.gloss: not to mind, not to care either way

examples.english: I don't mind what we eat.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ qù bu qù, wǒ wúsuǒwèi.
examples.english: Whether you go or not, it's all the same to me.

words.tip: Literally 'nothing worth mentioning'. Like 随便, but about your attitude rather than a choice. Careful with the tone of voice: it can sound cold, just like German 'Mir egal'.

examples.english: It's a small world!

examples.text: 我想去看看外面的世界。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù kànkan wàimiàn de shìjiè.
examples.english: I want to go and see the world out there.

words.tip: 全世界 = the whole world. 世界上 = in the world: 世界上最好的妈妈. 世界杯 is the World Cup. Two fourth tones.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn jīntiān de xīnwén le ma?
examples.english: Have you seen today's news?

examples.text: 我爸爸每天晚上看新闻。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba měi tiān wǎnshang kàn xīnwén.
examples.english: My dad watches the news every evening.

words.tip: 'Newly heard'. News in the media; personal news is 消息. One news item is 一条新闻. The evening news on state TV at seven is an institution: 新闻联播.

examples.english: Chinese society is changing fast.

examples.text: 他刚毕业，没有社会经验。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāng bìyè, méiyǒu shèhuì jīngyàn.
examples.english: He's just graduated and has no experience of the real world.

words.tip: Also 'the real world' after school: 进入社会 = to start working life, and 社会经验 = life experience. 刚 = just now, only just.

examples.english: China's history is very long.

examples.text: 这个城市有两千年的历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì yǒu liǎngqiān nián de lìshǐ.
examples.english: This city has two thousand years of history.

words.tip: The 历 of 日历 and 农历. 有…年的历史 says how old a place or thing is. sh is made with the tongue curled back, and the i after it is just a buzz.

examples.english: We all hope for world peace.
Peace is more important than anything.

words.tip: Peace between countries. The same 和 as the word for 'and', here in its older sense of harmony. The opposite is 战争 (war). 比什么都… = more … than anything.

examples.text: 我想提高我的中文水平。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tígāo wǒ de Zhōngwén shuǐpíng.
examples.english: I want to improve my level of Chinese.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de fāyīn tígāo le hěn duō.
examples.english: Your pronunciation has improved a lot.

words.tip: To 'lift higher': a level, a skill, a price, a salary. 进步 is about the person making progress; 提高 is about the level going up.

examples.pinyin: Tā de Zhōngwén shuǐpíng hěn gāo.
examples.english: His level of Chinese is very high.
Our levels are about the same.

words.tip: 'Water-level': how good someone is at something. A level is 高 or 低 (low), not big or small. When praised, the modest reply is 我的水平还不行.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiànzài shuō de hěn liúlì!
examples.english: You speak very fluently now!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de Déyǔ hái bú tài liúlì.
examples.english: My German isn't very fluent yet.

words.tip: 'Flowing', the same picture as German fließend. Use it with 说得: 说得很流利. liú is spelled iu but said 'lyoh'.

examples.text: 这些照片里有很多回忆。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē zhàopiàn li yǒu hěn duō huíyì.
examples.english: There are a lot of memories in these photos.

examples.text: 小时候的夏天是我最好的回忆。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoshíhou de xiàtiān shì wǒ zuì hǎo de huíyì.
examples.english: The summers of my childhood are my best memories.

words.tip: To 'go back and recall'. 回忆 is a memory you treasure; 记得 is simply to remember a fact. Also a verb: 回忆过去 = to think back on the past.

words.gloss: to learn (and now be able to), to master

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngyú xuéhuì yòng kuàizi le!
examples.english: I've finally learned to use chopsticks!

examples.text: 这一年我学会了一千个词。
examples.pinyin: Zhè yì nián wǒ xuéhuì le yìqiān ge cí.
examples.english: This year I've learned a thousand words.
alternatives: 我这一年学会了一千个词。

words.tip: 学 is the trying, 会 is the result: you learned it and now you can. Not yet there: 还没学会. The second example is true for both of you now!

examples.english: Congratulations on finding a new job!

examples.text: 听说你们要结婚了，恭喜！
examples.pinyin: Tīngshuō nǐmen yào jiéhūn le, gōngxǐ!
examples.english: I hear you're getting married, congratulations!

words.tip: Often doubled: 恭喜恭喜! At Spring Festival people greet each other with 恭喜发财 = may you get rich. For birthdays say 生日快乐 instead.

words.gloss: to thank, to be grateful to

examples.english: Thank you for always helping me.

examples.text: 我真的很感谢我的老师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhēn de hěn gǎnxiè wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.english: I'm truly grateful to my teacher.

words.tip: Deeper and more formal than 谢谢: for speeches, messages and real gratitude. 非常感谢! = thank you very much indeed.

examples.english: You've worked hard, go and rest now.

examples.text: 妈妈一个人带孩子很辛苦。
examples.pinyin: Māma yí ge rén dài háizi hěn xīnkǔ.
examples.english: It's hard for Mum, looking after the children on her own.

words.tip: 辛苦了! thanks someone by recognising their effort: to a partner after cooking, a driver, a colleague. There's no neat translation, so act out a few situations.

examples.english: The teacher praised my pronunciation.

examples.text: 别夸我了，我会不好意思的。
examples.pinyin: Bié kuā wǒ le, wǒ huì bù hǎoyìsi de.
examples.english: Stop praising me, I'll get embarrassed.

words.tip: Praise is traditionally turned down modestly rather than accepted: 哪里哪里, or 没有没有. Practise both ways of answering a compliment.

characters.meaning: to finish (here read liǎo, not le)

examples.english: You're really amazing!

examples.text: 会说三种语言，真了不起！
examples.pinyin: Huì shuō sān zhǒng yǔyán, zhēn liǎobuqǐ!
examples.english: Speaking three languages, that's really remarkable!

words.tip: For real achievements. Here 了 is read liǎo, not le. 没什么了不起 = it's nothing special, the modest reply.

examples.text: 我给你准备了一个惊喜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ zhǔnbèi le yí ge jīngxǐ.
examples.english: I've prepared a surprise for you.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ lái le! Zhēn shì ge jīngxǐ!
examples.english: You came! What a lovely surprise!

words.tip: 'Startled joy': only for nice surprises. Plain astonishment, good or bad, is 吃惊; a nasty fright is 惊吓. 给你一个惊喜 = to give you a surprise.

examples.pinyin: Dàngāo shang yǒu sān gēn làzhú.
examples.english: There are three candles on the cake.

examples.pinyin: Tíngdiàn le, jiā li yǒu làzhú ma?
examples.english: The power's gone off, do we have candles at home?

words.tip: 吹蜡烛 = to blow out the candles; before that you 许愿 (make a wish). 停电 = a power cut. 火 (fire) is on the left of 烛.

examples.text: 我们开一瓶香槟庆祝吧！
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kāi yì píng xiāngbīn qìngzhù ba!
examples.english: Let's open a bottle of champagne to celebrate!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ hē le yì bēi xiāngbīn.
examples.english: I only had one glass of champagne.

words.tip: Borrowed by sound from 'champagne' and written with 香 (fragrant). In everyday use it covers any sparkling wine. Both syllables are high and level.

examples.text: 春节的时候很多人放烟花。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié de shíhou hěn duō rén fàng yānhuā.
examples.english: At Spring Festival lots of people let off fireworks.
Tonight's fireworks are really beautiful!

words.tip: 'Smoke flowers', the kind that light up the sky. 放烟花 = to let off fireworks. The loud bangers are 鞭炮. Many big cities now restrict both.

words.gloss: to toast, to offer (a drink) respectfully

examples.english: Here's to you!

examples.text: 这杯酒敬我们的爸爸妈妈。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi jiǔ jìng wǒmen de bàba māma.
examples.english: This glass is to our mums and dads.

words.tip: At a Chinese dinner you don't just drink: you 敬 someone, starting with the eldest, and hold your glass a little lower than theirs to show respect. Practise before meeting the in-laws.

examples.english: I'll love you forever.

examples.text: 我永远不会忘记这一天。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn bú huì wàngjì zhè yì tiān.
examples.english: I'll never forget this day.

words.tip: 'Forever far': from now on without end. 永远不 = never (in the future). Two third tones, so the first rises. 忘记 is the full form of 忘.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ guò yíbèizi.
examples.english: I want to spend my whole life with you.

examples.text: 他一辈子都住在这个城市。
examples.pinyin: Tā yíbèizi dōu zhù zài zhège chéngshì.
examples.english: He's lived in this city all his life.

words.tip: 'One generation': a whole life. The first example is close to a proposal, so use it wisely! 下辈子 = in the next life, said jokingly.

words.gloss: to keep (someone) company, to go along with

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ zài jiā péi nǐ.
examples.english: Today I'm staying home to keep you company.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng péi wǒ qù yīyuàn ma?
examples.english: Can you come to the hospital with me?

words.tip: Being there for someone, with your time. 陪 + person + verb. 你都不陪我 is a classic complaint between partners; 我陪你 is the answer everyone wants.

examples.english: My husband is a great cook.
Darling, who's washing up today?

words.tip: The everyday word for 'my husband', also used to call him. The neutral, formal word is 丈夫. Young couples often use it before they are married.

examples.text: 这是我老婆，她是德国人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ lǎopo, tā shì Déguó rén.
examples.english: This is my wife, she's German.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ lǎopo shuō shénme dōu duì.
examples.english: Whatever my wife says is right.

words.tip: The partner word of 老公, just as warm and informal. The neutral word is 妻子; 太太 is polite for someone else's wife. Neither has anything to do with being old.

examples.english: Let's carry on studying tomorrow.
Take a short break, then carry on.

words.tip: 继续 + verb = to keep doing it: 继续说, 继续走. 继续努力! = keep up the good work. x is like 'sh' with the tongue flat, and the u after it is ü.

examples.pinyin: Zhè yì nián de nǔlì hěn zhídé.
examples.english: This year's effort was well worth it.

examples.text: 这个地方值得再去一次。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìfang zhídé zài qù yí cì.
examples.english: This place is worth going to again.

words.tip: 值得 + verb = worth doing: 值得看, 值得学. On its own: 很值得 = it was worth it; 不值得 = not worth it.

examples.pinyin: Xià yí bù wǒmen zuò shénme?
examples.english: What do we do as the next step?

examples.pinyin: Xué Zhōngwén yào yí bù yí bù lái.
examples.english: You have to learn Chinese one step at a time.

words.tip: A footstep and a stage in a plan. It counts itself, with no measure word: 一步, 两步. 一步一步 = step by step. You know it from 散步, 跑步 and 进步.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì nánwàng de yì nián.
examples.english: This has been an unforgettable year.

examples.pinyin: Nà cì lǚxíng ràng wǒ hěn nánwàng.
examples.english: That trip was unforgettable for me.

words.tip: 'Hard to forget'. 难 + verb makes many such words: 难吃 (tastes bad), 难看 (ugly), 难说 (hard to say).

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de bǐsài tài jīngcǎi le!
examples.english: Today's match was brilliant!

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiǎng de gùshi zhēn jīngcǎi.
examples.english: The story you told was really wonderful.

words.tip: For anything that holds an audience: a show, a match, a speech, a story, a life. Not for food or people's looks. c is 'ts': jīng-tsǎi.
